'''Christine Chatelain''' (born 8 February 1985)<ref>{{cite web |title=Christine Chatelain |url=https://watch.plex.tv/person/christine-chatelain |website=watch.plex.tv |publisher=[[Plex]] |access-date=30 October 2025}}</ref> is a [[Canadians|Canadian]] film and television actress.<ref>[https://www.northernstars.ca/actor/christine-chatelain/ Christine Chatelain's bio] at www.northernstars.ca</ref> She had a recurring role on ''[[The Collector (Canadian TV series)|''The Collector'']]'' as Taylor Slate. Originally an art student in [[Vancouver]], she tried acting as a [[hobby]] and quickly gained roles in ''[[40 Days and 40 Nights]]'' and ''[[3000 Miles to Graceland]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thecollectortv.com/42.html|title=TAYLOR SLATE|accessdate=2007-01-07|archive-date=2017-11-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171104160033/http://www.thecollectortv.com/42.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards and nominations==
Chatelain has twice been nominated for [[Leo Awards]], first in 2005 in the category of Best Guest Performance by a Female: Dramatic Series for her role in the episode "The Superhero" of television series ''[[The Collector (Canadian TV series)|The Collector]]''<ref>[https://www.leoawards.com/past_winners/pdf/2005.pdf Past Nominees & Winners 2005] at [[Leo Awards|www.leoawards.com]]</ref> and again in 2013 in the category of Best Supporting Performance by a Female: Motion Picture for her role in ''[[Death Do Us Part]]''.<ref>[https://www.leoawards.com/past_winners/pdf/2013.pdf Past Nominees & Winners 2013] at [[Leo Awards|www.leoawards.com]]</ref>

'''Drew Sidora Jordan''' (born May 1, 1985)<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2024 |title=Drew Sidora |url=https://in.bookmyshow.com/person/drew-sidora/IEIN001454 |access-date=August 29, 2024 |website=Book My Show}}</ref> is an American actress, singer and TV personality. She is known for her recurring role as Chantel in the [[Disney Channel Original Series]] ''[[That's So Raven]]'', her portrayal of [[Tionne Watkins]] in the [[VH1]] [[TLC (group)|TLC]] biographical film ''[[CrazySexyCool: The TLC Story]]'', and playing a fictionalized version of herself in the [[Black Entertainment Television|BET]] comedy-drama television series ''[[The Game (2006 TV series)|The Game]]''. She also appeared in the films ''[[White Chicks]]'' (2004) and ''[[Step Up (film)|Step Up]]'' (2006). Sidora joined the cast of the [[Bravo (American TV network)|Bravo]] reality show ''[[The Real Housewives of Atlanta]]'' in 2020.

==Career==
===Acting===
Sidora completed numerous industrial films and was the youngest member of the "Hook Players Theater Ensemble" in Hollywood, California, with residence at the [[Richard Pryor]] Theater.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.metacritic.com/person/drew-sidora?filter-options=movies|title=Drew Sidora|website=[[Metacritic]]|date=October 26, 2023 }}</ref> At age 9, she appeared in the [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox TV]] movie ''Divas'', acting alongside [[Khalil Kain]], [[Lisa Nicole Carson]] and [[Nicole Ari Parker]]. In August 2026, Drew Sidora signed with CGEM Talent for Management Representation.<ref>[https://www.instagram.com/p/DcWvT5dBELK/ CGEM Talent]</ref> 

Besides her roles in ''That's So Raven'', ''Step Up'' and ''Blessed & Cursed'', Sidora has also guest starred in ''[[Girlfriends (American TV series)|Girlfriends]] '' in 2006 as a High School Girl Group recruiter, as well as ''[[Without a Trace]]'', ''[[The Game (2006 TV series)|The Game]]'', and ''[[What I Like About You (TV series)|What I Like About You]]''. She has also appeared in the feature films ''[[White Chicks]]'' and ''[[Never Die Alone]]'', and made a cameo appearance in [[GLC (rapper)|GLC]]'s single "Honor Me".{{citation needed|date=November 2023}}<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131019222227/http://blog.vh1.com/2013-10-16/crazysexycool-drew-sidora-interview/ Drew Sidora Interview Two]</ref>

In 2013, she was cast as a member [[Tionne Watkins]] of the girl group [[TLC (group)|TLC]] in the group's biopic that aired on [[VH1]]. Sidora also starred as Genesis "Genny" Winters in the 2014 BounceTV original ''One Love''.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131019222227/http://blog.vh1.com/2013-10-16/crazysexycool-drew-sidora-interview/ Drew Sidora Interview Two]</ref>

===Reality television===
Sidora joined the cast of ''[[The Real Housewives of Atlanta]]'' beginning its [[The Real Housewives of Atlanta season 13|thirteenth season]]. She made her debut in December 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-07-21|title=Newest Addition! Drew Sidora Is Joining 'Real Housewives of Atlanta'|url=https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/actress-drew-sidora-is-joining-real-housewives-of-atlanta/|access-date=2020-09-08|website=Us Weekly|language=en-US}}</ref>

===Music===
In January 2006, Sidora first signed a record deal with [[J Records]]. Sidora featured on the [[Step Up (Original Soundtrack)]] with two songs entitled "For The Love" and "Til The Dawn" in 2006. In 2007, she featured on the [[Three Can Play That Game]] soundtrack with a song entitled "Three Can Play".{{Citation needed |date=January 2021}} In December 2008, Sidora signed a record deal with [[Slip-n-Slide Records]]. In 2010, the album's first single titled "Juke It" was released. She played [[Trey Songz]]'s lover in the video for "[[Last Time (Trey Songz song)|Last Time]]" of the album [[Trey Day]]. She also appears in [[Yung Berg]]'s "Sexy Lady" video as the girlfriend. She also danced in [[Sean Paul]]’s "Give It Up to Me" video.

On September 16, 2022, Sidora released a single entitled "Already Know". The accompanying music video was released on June 25, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2024 |title=Drew Sidora: Already Know |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt28224808/ |website=IMDB}}</ref>

In March 2025, Sidora released her debut album, ''I Did It to Me''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Drew Sidora - I did it to me on Apple Music. |url=https://music.apple.com/us/album/i-did-it-to-me/1803366551}}</ref> Two singles preceded the album's release, the title track and "Love 4 a Min", the latter having two versions, one featuring American R&B singer Torica and another featuring ''[[Love & Hip Hop: Atlanta]]'' cast member and rapper Sierra Gates. The album was executive-produced by Sidora's ''[[The Real Housewives of Atlanta]]'' costar [[Porsha Williams]]' former partner, Dennis McKinley, and released under his label MusicXchange.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2025 |title=Drew Sidora Instagram post |url=https://www.instagram.com/reel/DHWdXrHx_JX/?utm_source=ig_embed&ig_rid=e73ee0c6-7064-4f42-aaf5-595ada1b8012}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sidora has a son, Josiah, from a previous relationship. Sidora married Ralph Pittman and together they have two children: a son, Machai, born in June 2015,<ref>{{cite web|title=Drew Sidora Welcomes Son Machai David |url=https://people.com/parents/drew-sidora-welcomes-son-machai-david/ |website=People |access-date=February 23, 2020 |date=June 30, 2015}}</ref> and a daughter, Aniya, born in February 2018.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Reitman|first1=Shelby |last2=Mizoguchi |first2=Karen |title=A Baby Girl! Step Up Star Drew Sidora Welcomes Second Child with Husband Ralph Pittman |url=https://people.com/babies/drew-sidora-welcomes-daughter-aniya-grace/ |website=People |access-date=February 23, 2020 |date=February 15, 2018}}</ref> On February 27, 2023, Sidora filed a petition to divorce Pittman.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=RHOA Star Drew Sidora's Husband Ralph Pittman Files for Divorce After Nearly 9 Years of Marriage |url=https://people.com/tv/real-housewives-of-atlanta-drew-sidora-ralph-pittman-divorce/ |access-date=2023-03-02 |magazine=People}}</ref>

Her father, Robert Andrew "Bob" Jordan, a prominent [[Chicago]] [[pediatrician]], died on August 11, 2023, of [[Alzheimer's disease]].<ref>{{Cite web |title='RHOA' Star Drew Sidora Mourns Her Father's Death from Alzheimer's: 'You're Never Prepared' |url=https://people.com/rhoa-star-drew-sidora-mourns-father-death-from-alzheimers-7643992 |access-date=2023-09-13 |website=Peoplemag |language=en}}</ref>  He and her mother, Jeanette, married on July 29, 1962. Drew is one of their five children.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-20 |title="The Support Goes On and On" – Illinois Chapter Blog |url=https://www.alzheimers-illinois.org/wp/2020/02/20/the-support-goes-on-and-on/ |access-date=2023-09-13}}</ref>

'''Rajiv Surendra'''  (born July 19, 1986)<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 18, 2016 |title=Memoir by Rajiv Surendra traces actor's parallels with Life of Pi |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/arts/books-and-media/memoir-by-rajiv-surendra-traces-actors-parallels-with-life-of-pi/article32930166/ |access-date=May 7, 2024 |work=The Globe and Mail}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E702sw69ACs |title=It's My Birthday, This is What I'm Doing Today – with Rajiv Surendra |date=July 19, 2024 |last=Rajiv Surendra |access-date=November 21, 2025 |via=YouTube}}</ref>{{efn|Some sources indicate a birth year of 1988 or 1989,<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 8, 2023 |title=How Rajiv Surendra Went from 'Mean Girls' to the Renaissance Man of Your Dreams |url=https://www.gq.com/story/rajiv-surendra-mean-girls-renaissance-man-interview |access-date=May 7, 2024 |website=GQ}}</ref> which contradicts several statements in his book ''The Elephants in My Backyard'', such as being twelve when he auditioned for the TV series ''[[Goosebumps (1995 TV series)|Goosebumps]]'' (which ended in 1998), and his audition for ''[[Mean Girls]]'' (filmed in 2003) coming after a hiatus at age sixteen.}} is a Canadian American actor, artist, content creator, and writer.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rajiv Surendra, Who Played Kevin G in Mean Girls, Is Now a YouTube Chef |url=https://people.com/food/kevin-g-mean-girls-rajiv-surendra-youtube-cooking-videos/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=Peoplemag}}</ref> He is known for his portrayal of high school student Kevin Gnapoor in the 2004 teen comedy film ''[[Mean Girls]]'' and for his 2016 memoir, ''The Elephants in My Backyard'', which chronicles his unsuccessful bid to win the lead role in the 2012 film ''[[Life of Pi (film)|Life of Pi]]''.<ref name="cbcbooks">[https://web.archive.org/web/20170421021701/http://www.cbc.ca/books/2016/11/the-elephants-in-my-backyard.html "The Elephants in My Backyard"]. [[CBC Books]], November 18, 2016.</ref>

==Early life==
Surendra's parents immigrated to Canada from [[Sri Lanka]]. He grew up in Toronto, in a neighbourhood close to [[Toronto Zoo]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The life of Rajiv|url=https://alumni.utoronto.ca/news-and-stories/news-and-articles/life-rajiv|access-date=January 6, 2022|website=University of Toronto Alumni}}</ref> He attended [[Wexford Collegiate School for the Arts]] as a musical theatre student and performer, graduating in 2003.<ref name="globe" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/books/rajiv-surendra-traveled-from-mean-girls-to-chalk-artist/2016/11/15/7c58ee88-909f-11e6-a6a3-d50061aa9fae_story.html|title=Rajiv Surendra traveled from 'Mean Girls' to chalk artist|last=Lee|first=Nicole|date=November 15, 2016|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|access-date=December 4, 2019|issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

==Career==
===Acting===
Among other roles, Surendra played Chuck Singh in the third season of the [[YTV (Canadian TV channel)|YTV]] sitcom ''[[System Crash (TV series)|System Crash]]'' (2000) and [[mathlete]] Kevin Gnapoor in the 2004 comedy film ''[[Mean Girls]]''. After losing his bid for the lead role in the 2012 film ''[[Life of Pi (film)|Life of Pi]]'', he decided to leave acting behind. He began reevaluating his life after that disappointment, saying, "It took a year for me to mourn the loss of what happened."<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=November 24, 2016 |title=Rajiv Surendra explores what it means to fail in his new memoir |url=https://www.cbc.ca/radio/q/schedule-for-thursday-november-24-2016-1.3863961/rajiv-surendra-explores-what-it-means-to-fail-in-his-new-memoir-1.3863981 |website=CBC Radio}}</ref> Surendra subsequently worked as an [[au pair]] in [[Munich]], Germany.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Mean Girls Alum Rajiv Surendra Felt 'Dead Inside' After Losing Life of Pi Role |url=https://people.com/movies/mean-girls-rajiv-surendra-felt-dead-inside-after-losing-life-of-pi/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=Peoplemag}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> On October 3, 2020, he appeared in a ''Mean Girls Reunion'' video on Instagram, with several original cast members, to encourage people to vote in the [[2020 United States presidential election]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram post by Katie Couric |url=https://www.instagram.com/tv/CF43tnjpvL-/?igshid=mbhbi3rtzj0f |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Janet W. |date=October 3, 2020 |title='Mean Girls' Cast Reunites After 16 Years to Encourage Voting |url=https://variety.com/2020/film/news/mean-girls-reunion-voting-musical-movie-1234791593/ |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=Variety}}</ref>

In November 2023, Surendra reprised his role as Kevin Gnapoor in a ''Mean Girls''-themed [[Black Friday (shopping)|Black Friday]] commercial for [[Walmart]], alongside his original co-stars [[Lindsay Lohan]], [[Lacey Chabert]], [[Amanda Seyfried]], and [[Daniel Franzese]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title='Mean Girls' Cast Reunites for Epic Walmart Shopping Spot: 'Great Catching Up' |url=https://people.com/watch-mean-girls-cast-reunite-for-epic-walmart-shopping-commercial-exclusive-8385283 |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=Peoplemag}}</ref> The commercial shows that Kevin is now a proud dad, as the original cast return to the halls of North Shore High School, where a new crew of [[It girl]]s rule the school.<ref name=":1" />

===Writing===
In 2016, Surendra published the book ''The Elephants in My Backyard'', a memoir of his failed attempt to win the lead role in the 2012 film ''[[Life of Pi (film)|Life of Pi]]''.<ref name="globe">[https://www.theglobeandmail.com/arts/books-and-media/memoir-by-rajiv-surendra-traces-actors-parallels-with-life-of-pi/article32930166/ "Memoir by Rajiv Surendra traces actor's parallels with Life of Pi"]. ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', November 18, 2016.</ref> He read ''Life of Pi'' for the first time on the set of ''Mean Girls'' in 2004 and noticed many parallels between his own life and that of the novel's lead character, Piscine Molitor "Pi" Patel, including the fact that Surendra himself grew up in a home adjacent to the [[Toronto Zoo]].<ref name="globe" /> To prepare for the role, Surendra temporarily dropped out of school at the [[University of Toronto]] and travelled to [[Puducherry (city)|Pondicherry]], India to learn the specific dialect of the character. Upon returning to Canada and going back to school, Surendra learned how to swim. While he did meet with the casting director of the film, Surendra was not selected to play the role of Pi.<ref>{{Citation|title=The Elephants in My Backyard {{!}} Rajiv Surendra {{!}} TEDxUofT| date=June 28, 2017 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nUn4iTzYPfw|language=en|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref> In a ''[[GQ]]'' interview, he said: "The project kept getting delayed. Three months turned into a year turned into four years. It was actually six years because of that year off. ''Life of Pi'' was attached to four different directors over the years, so every time a new director [came aboard], I'd go to the library and get out all the movies they had made and research that director. I worked really, really hard to try to get this part. In the end, they gave it to somebody else."<ref name=":0" />

He reflected on these experiences in ''The Elephants in My Backyard''. The book was longlisted for the 2017 edition of ''[[Canada Reads]]'',<ref name="cbcbooks" /> and Surendra was nominated for the [[Kobo Emerging Writer Prize]] in 2017.<ref>[http://www.cbc.ca/books/2017/05/teva-harrison-rajiv-surendra-nominated-for-10k-kobo-emerging-writer-prize.html "Teva Harrison, Rajiv Surendra nominated for $10K Kobo Emerging Writer Prize"]. [[CBC Books]], May 1, 2017.</ref>

===Fine arts and crafts===
While working at [[Black Creek Pioneer Village]] in Toronto as a teenager, Surendra developed an interest in traditional crafts and antiques. As a result, he practices a number of traditional arts and crafts, including letter writing, calligraphy, [[bookbinding]], and [[painting]]. He was  an [[Apprenticeship|apprentice]] to Connecticut-based [[Pottery|potter]] Guy Wolff, whose work has appeared in ''[[Martha Stewart Living]]'' magazine.<ref>{{Cite web|title="Mean Girls" Star Rajiv Surendra Has a Pottery Collection with PlantShed|url=https://www.apartmenttherapy.com/mean-girls-rajiv-surendra-plantshed-collection-37012306|access-date=January 6, 2022|website=Apartment Therapy}}</ref>

In 2010, Surendra founded Letters in Ink, a bespoke [[calligraphy]] and [[graphic design]] service based in [[Manhattan]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Kevin G from Mean Girls Wants to Teach You How to Make Tamil Food |url=https://www.foodandwine.com/kevin-g-mean-girls-tamil-food-7092446 |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=Food & Wine}}</ref> He uses pen and ink and chalk to create art and branding for restaurants and other businesses.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Letters in Ink|url=https://lettersinink.com/|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref>

In 2020, Surendra created a two-video [[YouTube]] series on the art of letter writing for the [[Morgan Library & Museum]].<ref>{{Citation|title=Letter-writing is not dead! Part 1: Tips and Inspiration| date=October 3, 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2Tzq23Ux4Ds|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|title=Letter-writing is not dead! Part 2: Handwriting is Not Dead!| date=October 10, 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fTC_z4kRwbs|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref> Starting in 2021, he appeared in a series of videos posted on [[HGTV]]'s YouTube channel,<ref name="Vox 2022">{{cite news |last1=Grady |first1=Constance |title=Kevin G. from Mean Girls is my favorite lifestyle influencer |url=https://www.vox.com/23000448/kevin-g-homeboy-tv-show-discovery-plus |access-date=March 9, 2025 |work=[[Vox (website)|Vox]] |date=March 29, 2022}}</ref> highlighting his personal collection of handmade objects,<ref>{{Citation|title=Tour Rajiv Surendra's NYC Apartment Filled with Handmade Decor...and Chalk Art! {{!}} Handmade Home Tour| date=June 15, 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7Uo2nomf4I0|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref> chalk art,<ref>{{Citation|title=A Beginner's Guide to Chalk Art with Rajiv Surendra {{!}} Chalk Art for Beginners| date=June 17, 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4rmwQIL4W0Y|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref> bookbinding,<ref>{{Citation|title=Rajiv Surendra's Bookbinding Guide for Beginners {{!}} Intro to Bookbinding| date=September 7, 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ER9FIyYr_QA|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref> and [[paper marbling]].<ref>{{Citation|title=A Beginner's Guide to Paper Marbling, with Rajiv Surendra {{!}} Paper Marbling Tutorial| date=September 7, 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3x36f713jZA|access-date=September 16, 2021}}</ref> He created how-to videos, such as "A Beginner's Guide to Chalk Art" and "How to Be a Good Host", which eventually accumulated over eight million views and encouraged him to create his own channel.<ref name=":2" />

In 2022, Surendra started a self-titled YouTube channel, which has garnered over 385,000 subscribers.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Surendra |first1=Rajiv |title=YouTube Channel |url=https://www.youtube.com/@rajivsurendra/about |website=Youtube.com |publisher=Rajiv Surendra |access-date=January 30, 2026}}</ref> The channel began with a [[GoFundMe]], created after the success of Surendra's videos with [[HGTV]], as a means of continuing to share his passions and interests. The videos on the channel are presented largely as tutorials, many of them on cooking, antiques, and crafts.<ref>{{cite web |title=Why you should use your nicest things, every day! |url=https://youtube.com/ClAqiBqqtu0?si=2Kc7vshNtyL0SCc5 |website=Youtube |publisher=Rajiv Surendra |access-date=October 17, 2023 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The [[Pilot (television)|pilot]] of a planned lifestyle show hosted by Surendra, ''Homeboy'', premiered on the streaming service [[Discovery Plus]] early that year.<ref name="Vox 2022" />

==Personal life==
Surendra is gay.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 12, 2023 |title=Rajiv Surendra traveled from 'Mean Girls' to chalk artist |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/books/rajiv-surendra-traveled-from-mean-girls-to-chalk-artist/2016/11/15/7c58ee88-909f-11e6-a6a3-d50061aa9fae_story.html |access-date=May 4, 2024 |newspaper=Washington Post |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> As of February 2023, he lives in [[New York City]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 8, 2023 |title=How Rajiv Surendra Went from 'Mean Girls' to the Renaissance Man of Your Dreams |url=https://www.gq.com/story/rajiv-surendra-mean-girls-renaissance-man-interview |access-date=November 3, 2023 |website=GQ}}</ref> In 2024, he became an American citizen.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Instagram |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C8ut64pua6v/?hl=en |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=instagram.com}}</ref>

'''Emily Jane Browning''' (born December 7, 1988) is an Australian actress. She made her film debut in the television film ''[[The Echo of Thunder]]'' (1998), and subsequently appeared in television shows such as ''[[High Flyers (Australian TV series)|High Flyers]]'' (1999), ''[[Something in the Air (TV series)|Something in the Air]]'' (2000–2001), and ''[[Blue Heelers]]'' (2000–2002)''.'' Her breakthrough role was in the 2002 horror film ''[[Ghost Ship (2002 film)|Ghost Ship]]'', which introduced her to a wider audience. In 2005, Browning won the [[Australian Film Institute]] International Award for Best Actress for her portrayal of [[Violet Baudelaire]] in the film ''[[Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events]]'' (2004).

Browning is also known for her roles in ''[[The Uninvited (2009 film)|The Uninvited]]'' (2009), ''[[Sucker Punch (2011 film)|Sucker Punch]]'' (2011), ''[[Sleeping Beauty (2011 film)|Sleeping Beauty]]'' (2011), and ''[[Pompeii (film)|Pompeii]]'' (2014). She was named the Breakthrough Performer of The Year by the [[Hamptons International Film Festival]] for her role in the latter. Browning's other films include ''[[Summer in February]]'', ''[[Plush (film)|Plush]]'' (both 2013), ''[[Legend (2015 film)|Legend]]'' (2015) and ''[[Golden Exits]]'' (2017). From 2017 to 2021, she starred as Laura Moon in the [[Starz]] series [[American Gods (TV series)|''American Gods'']]. She also had a recurring role in [[Showtime (TV network)|Showtime]]'s drama series ''[[The Affair (TV series)|The Affair]]'' (2018–2019). In 2023, she starred as Zoe in [[Amazon Prime Video]]'s series ''[[Class of '07]]''.

==Early life and education==
Emily Jane Browning was born in [[Melbourne]], [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], the daughter of Andrew and Shelley Browning. She has two younger brothers.<ref name =tvguide/>

She attended Hurstbridge Learning Co-op and [[Eltham High School]].<ref name="tvguide">{{cite web |last=<!-- no author attribution --> |date=<!-- no clear date for creation or update --> |title=Emily Browning |url=https://www.tvguide.com/celebrities/emily-browning/bio/3000205896/ |accessdate=4 June 2025 |work=[[TV Guide]]}}</ref>

==Career==
===1998–2008===
Browning's debut acting role was in the 1998 [[Hallmark Channel (Australia)|Hallmark Channel]] movie ''[[The Echo of Thunder]]''.<ref name="The Age">{{cite news |last=Benedictus |first=Luke |date=19 December 2004 |title=See Emily play ... while you can |url=http://www.theage.com.au/articles/2004/12/17/1102787260949.html |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=[[The Age]] |location=Australia}}</ref> Additional roles in Australian film and television productions soon followed, including recurring roles in the television series ''[[Blue Heelers]]'' from 2000 to 2002, and ''[[Something in the Air (TV series)|Something in the Air]]'' from 2000 to 2001. In 2001, Browning appeared as the daughter of the character played by [[Billy Connolly]] in ''[[The Man Who Sued God]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Emily Browning 2014 02 05 (11:03am) The Man Who Sued God 2001 By R.R.S Sweden |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=van1V-AMXt8 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715112718/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=van1V-AMXt8 |archive-date=15 July 2015 |access-date=25 July 2014 |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=}}</ref>

She made her American film debut in 2002's ''[[Ghost Ship (2002 film)|Ghost Ship]]'', and won an [[Australian Film Institute Award]] for Best Young Actress, the same year.<ref>{{cite web |last=<!-- no author attribution --> |date=<!-- no clear source or edited date--> |title=AACTA Winners & Nominees 2000–2010: 2002 |url=https://www.aacta.org/aacta-awards/winners-and-nominees/range/2000-2010/year/2002/ |access-date=4 June 2025 |work=AACTA Awards |publisher=[[Australian Academy of Cinema and Television Arts]]}}</ref> In 2003, she appeared opposite [[Heath Ledger]] and [[Orlando Bloom]] in 2003's ''[[Ned Kelly (2003 film)|Ned Kelly]]'', and reunited with Connolly the following year in the film adaptation of ''[[Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events]]'', in which she played [[Violet Baudelaire]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Paul|last=Fischer|title=Interview: Emily Browning for "Lemony Snicket's A Series of Unfortunate Events" |url=http://www.darkhorizons.com/features/658 |website=[[Dark Horizons]] |date=13 December 2004 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140727040253/http://www.darkhorizons.com/features/658 |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 July 2014 |access-date=25 July 2014 }}</ref>

In 2006, Browning appeared in the music video for [[Evermore (band)|Evermore]]'s "Light Surrounding You". In the behind-the-scenes video for the clip, the band stated, "[We] suck as actors, so we decided to get Emily".<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KJoYoCxlXDo Making of Light Surrounding You]. YouTube. Retrieved on 16 May 2007</ref> She attended the [[L'Oreal]] Fashion Festival as a festival ambassador on 1 February 2007.<ref>[http://www.thewest.com.au/aapstory.aspx?StoryName=352370 Emily Browning] ''Thewest.com.au'' Retrieved on 20 April 2007 {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930022424/http://www.thewest.com.au/aapstory.aspx?StoryName=352370 |date=30 September 2007 }}</ref>

===2008–2011===
Browning played the lead role in the 2009 horror film ''[[The Uninvited (2009 film)|The Uninvited]]'', an American remake of the 2003 South Korean film ''[[A Tale of Two Sisters]]''. She turned down a request to audition for the role of [[Bella Swan]] in ''[[The Twilight Saga (film series)|Twilight]]'', citing exhaustion, despite an endorsement from series author [[Stephenie Meyer]].<ref>[http://www.stepheniemeyer.com/movie_archives.html Twilight the Movie (archives)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091026171539/http://www.stepheniemeyer.com/movie_archives.html |date=26 October 2009 }}. ''StephenieMeyer.com''</ref><ref>Larry Carroll: [https://web.archive.org/web/20091028133044/http://www.mtv.com/movies/news/articles/1610299/story.jhtml Emily Browning addresses her Twilight notoriety]. [[MTV|Mtv.com]], retrieved 4 April 2011</ref> In 2009, she was cast as Babydoll in [[Zack Snyder]]'s action film ''[[Sucker Punch (2011 film)|Sucker Punch]]'', as a replacement for [[Amanda Seyfried]], who dropped out due to scheduling conflicts.<ref>[http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/entertainment/confidential/emily-browning-tipped-for-starring-role-in-prison-flick/story-e6fredqc-1225693356289 Emily Browning tipped for starring role in prison flick]. ''Adelaidenow.com.au'', retrieved 15 August 2010</ref> Filming took place in [[Vancouver]] from September 2009 to January 2010,<ref>Carl DiOrio: [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/content_display/news/e3ie79635783d4581279d4e62cadbe23522 ''Green Lantern'', ''Sucker Punch'' going 3D]. ''[[Associated Press]]'', 14 October 2010, retrieved on ''Hollywoodreporter.com'' on 4 April 2011</ref> and the film was released on 25 March 2011.<ref>Steve Barton: [https://www.dreadcentral.com/news/36259/zack-snyder-deliver-his-sucker-punch-3d Zack Snyder to Deliver His Sucker Punch in 3D]. ''Dreadcentral.com'', 5 March 2010, retrieved 4 April 2011</ref> In an interview at [[San Diego Comic-Con International|Comic-Con]], she confirmed that she would be singing in the film, while claiming that her audition tape brought tears to her casting agent's eyes and the song she selected ("[[Killing Me Softly (song)|Killing Me Softly]]") was one of [[Zack Snyder]]'s wife [[Deborah Snyder|Deborah]]'s favourites, which Browning referred to as the "selling point" on her being cast in the role.<ref>[https://www.comingsoon.net/news/movienews.php?id=68523 SDCC EXCLUSIVE: Emily Browning & Jamie Chung on Sucker Punch] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022232748/http://www.comingsoon.net/news/movienews.php?id=68523 |date=22 October 2013 }}. ''Comingsoon.net'', retrieved on 15 August 2010</ref>

In February 2010, it was announced that Browning would play the lead role in the independent Australian film ''[[Sleeping Beauty (2011 film)|Sleeping Beauty]]'', directed by [[Julia Leigh]].<ref>Michael Bodey: [http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/arts/whos-who-in-tim-wintons-cloudstreet/story-e6frg8n6-1225826089128 Who's who in Tim Winton's Cloudstreet]. [[The Australian]], 3 February 2010, retrieved 4 April 2011</ref><ref name=browning>{{cite news|url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/news/arts/whos-who-in-tim-wintons-cloudstreet/story-e6frg8n6-1225826089128|title=Who's who in Tim Winton's Cloudstreet|first=Michael|last=Bodey|date=3 February 2010|work=[[The Australian]]|access-date=14 April 2011}}</ref> She replaced [[Mia Wasikowska]], who was committed to a film adaptation of ''[[Jane Eyre (2011 film)|Jane Eyre]]'' at the time.<ref name="firstshowing">{{cite news | url = http://www.firstshowing.net/2010/02/09/emily-browning-replaces-mia-wasikowska-in-sleeping-beauty/ | title = Emily Browning Replaces Mia Wasikowska in ''Sleeping Beauty'' | last = Billington | first = Alex | work=FirstShowing.net | date = 9 February 2010 | access-date = 1 August 2010}}</ref> The film screened at the 2011 [[Cannes Film Festival]] and the [[Sydney Film Festival]]. In a review from the festival, [[Peter Bradshaw]] of ''[[The Guardian]]'' called the film "Technically elegant with vehemence and control ... Emily Browning gives a fierce and powerful performance ... There is force and originality in Leigh's work".<ref>{{Cite news|last=Bradshaw|first=Peter|author-link=Peter Bradshaw|date=12 May 2011|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2011/may/12/cannes-film-festival-sleeping-beauty-review|title=Cannes 2011 review: ''Sleeping Beauty''|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=12 May 2011|location=London}}</ref> Fionnuala Halligan in ''[[Screen International]]'' wrote "Browning has gone the distance for her director and together, they have delivered something here that sometimes catches your breath".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Halligan|first=Fionnuala|date=12 May 2011|url=http://www.screendaily.com/reviews/latest-reviews/sleeping-beauty/5027326.article|title=''Sleeping Beauty''|work=[[Screen Daily]]|access-date=12 May 2011}}</ref> At the festival Browning said, "Even reading the screenplay, it made me feel uncomfortable. But that was something that attracted me to it. I would prefer to polarise an audience as opposed to making an entertaining film everybody feels ambivalent about."<ref name=dailytel0611>{{cite news | url = http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/entertainment/emily-browning-on-being-naked-in-erotic-thriller-sleeping-beauty-and-going-nude-again/story-e6frewyr-1226079974957 | title = Emily Browning on being naked in erotic thriller ''Sleeping Beauty'' and going nude again | first = Vicky | last = Roach |date = 22 June 2011 | work = Daily Telegraph | access-date = 22 June 2011}}</ref>

===2012–2020===
In 2012, she replaced English actress [[Ophelia Lovibond]] as female lead [[Florence Carter-Wood]] in the film ''[[Summer in February]]''.<ref name="indiewire">{{cite news | url = http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/emily-browning-will-spend-summer-in-february-instead-of-ophelia-lovibond | title = Emily Browning Will Spend 'Summer In February' Instead Of Ophelia Lovibond | date = 13 January 2012 | work = IndieWire | access-date = 20 July 2012 | archive-date = 16 January 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120116201704/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/emily-browning-will-spend-summer-in-february-instead-of-ophelia-lovibond | url-status = dead }}</ref> The film is based on the book of the same title, by [[Jonathan Smith (novelist)|Jonathan Smith]].<ref name=vintageseekers>{{ cite news | url = http://www.vintageseekers.com/vantage-point/film-news-summer-in-february | title = Downton Abbey lead Dan Stevens and My Week With Marilyn's Dominic Cooper are to co-star in a new film set in a Cornish artist's colony circa 1913|date = 13 January 2012 | work = Vintage Seekers}}</ref> In July 2012, Browning was cast in ''[[God Help the Girl (film)|God Help the Girl]]'', a musical film by [[Belle and Sebastian]] front-man [[Stuart Murdoch (musician)|Stuart Murdoch]].<ref name="troikatalent">{{cite web|url=http://www.troikatalent.com/#/michael-duff/hannah-murray/ |title=Hannah is currently filming the lead in GOD HELP THE GIRL with Emily Browning |work=TroikaTalent |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120616034618/http://www.troikatalent.com/ |archive-date=16 June 2012 }}</ref> Browning played Eve, and the role required live singing.<ref name="IndieWire">{{cite web | url = http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/hannah-murray-replaces-elle-fanning-in-god-help-the-girl-emily-browning-joins-the-film-20120709 | title = Hannah Murray Replaces Elle Fanning In 'God Help The Girl'; Emily Browning Joins The Film | first = Kevin | last = Jagernauth | date = 9 July 2012 | work = IndieWire | access-date = 7 December 2013 | archive-date = 8 March 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130308063622/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/hannah-murray-replaces-elle-fanning-in-god-help-the-girl-emily-browning-joins-the-film-20120709 | url-status = dead }}</ref> Filming on the production began on 8 July 2012 and wrapped on 12 August 2012.<ref name="godhelpthegirl Official Twitter">{{ cite news | url = https://twitter.com/godhelpthegirl/status/218631882668122112| title = It's all go at the 'god help the girl' production office – we start shooting July 8th. Exciting!| work = Twitter}}</ref>

Browning was cast in [[Catherine Hardwicke]]'s ''[[Plush (film)|Plush]]'' alongside [[Cam Gigandet]],<ref name="Cinema Blend">{{ cite news | url = https://www.cinemablend.com/new/Cam-Gigandet-Joins-Emily-Browning-Catherine-Hardwicke-Plush-31459.html | title = Cam Gigandet Joins Emily Browning In Catherine Hardwicke's Plush | first = Eric | last = Eisenberg | date = 18 June 2012| work = Cinema Blend| access-date=7 December 2013}}</ref> replacing [[Evan Rachel Wood]] (who was originally attached to the project) due to scheduling conflicts.<ref name="Digital Spy">{{ cite news | url = http://www.digitalspy.com/movies/news/a383829/emily-browning-to-star-in-catherine-hardwickes-plush.html | title = Emily Browning to star in Catherine Hardwicke's 'Plush'| first = Zeba | last = Blay | date = 27 May 2012| work = Digital Spy| access-date=7 December 2013 }}</ref> Browning also starred alongside [[Xavier Samuel]]<ref name="Variety">{{ cite news | url = https://variety.com/2012/film/news/xavier-samuel-joins-hardwicke-s-plush-1118057577/ | title = Xavier Samuel joins Hardwicke's 'Plush' | date = 7 August 2012 | work = Variety}}</ref> whom she met on the set during filming. ''[[Magic Magic (2013 film)|Magic Magic]]'', directed by Sebastián Silva, screened at the 2013 [[Sundance Film Festival]]. Film.com designated the film as a "Top Pick".<ref name="Film.com">{{ cite news | url = http://www.film.com/movies/magic-magic-review | title = Review: 'Magic, Magic'| first = Amanda Mae | last = Meyncke | date = 7 August 2013 | work = Film.com | access-date=7 December 2013}}</ref>

Browning starred in [[Paul W. S. Anderson]]'s 2014 epic romantic historical disaster film ''[[Pompeii (2014 film)|Pompeii]]''. The project was filmed in [[Toronto]] and the city of [[Pompeii]].<ref name="The Star">{{ cite news | url=https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/movies/2013/02/19/paul_ws_anderson_to_shoot_pompeii_in_toronto.html | title = Paul W.S. Anderson to shoot Pompeii in Toronto|last=DeMara|first=Bruce|date=19 February 2013|access-date=7 December 2013|work=The Star}}</ref>  The film received generally mixed to negative reviews, although Browning's performance was generally assessed more favorably.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 21, 2014 |title=Movie Review: Pompeii |url=https://www.vulture.com/2014/02/movie-review-pompeii.html |access-date=March 9, 2015 |publisher=Vulture}}</ref> Browning took a break from filming on ''Pompeii'', and returned home to Australia to film a music video for the song "No Matter What You Say" by the band [[Imperial Teen]]. The video follows Browning as the lead character, conducting a 'live art-piece'.<ref name="StarNow">{{cite news | url = http://www.starnow.com/listing/441742 | title = Imperial Teen - Music Video - Victoria - Supporting actors required for Sunday 24th March | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131013205020/https://www.starnow.com/listing/441742 | archive-date = 13 October 2013 | website = StarNow | date = 2013}}</ref><ref name="Godhelp">{{cite news |last=Trunick |first=Austin |url= http://www.undertheradarmag.com/interviews/scotland_week_god_help_the_girls_emily_browning |title=Scotland Week: God Help the Girl's Emily Browning |work=[[Under the Radar (magazine)|Under the Radar]] |date=4 September 2014 }}</ref>

In 2014, Browning filmed ''[[Shangri-La Suite]]''. The story follows two young lovers who break out of a mental hospital in 1974 and set out on a road trip to [[Los Angeles]] to fulfill the boy's lifelong dream of killing his idol [[Elvis Presley]], who appears as a supporting character. [[Luke Grimes]] and [[Avan Jogia]] co-star.<ref name="TheWrap">{{cite news | url = https://www.thewrap.com/movies/column-post/sucker-punch-star-emily-browning-joins-luke-grimes-shangri-la-suite-exclusive-100226 | title = 'Sucker Punch' Star Emily Browning Joins Luke Grimes in 'The Shangri-La Suite' (Exclusive) | access-date = 20 April 2020 | archive-date = 27 March 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180327023453/https://www.thewrap.com/movies/column-post/sucker-punch-star-emily-browning-joins-luke-grimes-shangri-la-suite-exclusive-100226/ | url-status = dead }}</ref> The same year, she appeared in [[Years & Years]]'s "Take Shelter" music video.<ref>{{cite web|title=Years & Years' music video for "Take Shelter", featuring Emily Browning!|url=http://getmusicasia.com/2014/08/04/years-years-take-shelter-featuring-emily-browning-music-video-premiere-watch/|access-date=4 November 2014|date=5 August 2014}}</ref>

In 2015, Browning appeared in the biopic crime thriller ''[[Legend (2015 film)|Legend]]'', alongside [[Tom Hardy]], who portrayed twin brothers and infamous 1960s London gangsters [[Kray twins|Reggie and Ronnie Kray]]. She portrayed [[Frances Shea]], the first wife of Reggie Kray.<ref>{{cite web|title=Emily Browning: Legend star on her new role|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/film/emily-browning-legend-star-on-her-new-role-1.2347177|publisher=irishtimes.com|access-date=2 October 2015}}</ref>

Browning was cast in ''[[American Gods (TV series)|American Gods]]'' (2017-2021) as Laura Moon. [[Neil Gaiman]], author of the [[American Gods|novel]], said, "I've been fascinated by Emily Browning since ''A Series of Unfortunate Events''. She has a challenge ahead of her: Laura is a tricky character, and the Laura on the screen is even trickier and more dangerous than the one on the page. She's going to have a wonderful time bringing Laura to life".<ref>{{cite web|title=Starz's 'American Gods' Casts Its Laura Moon|date=17 March 2016 |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/american-gods-casts-laura-moon-876567|publisher=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=17 March 2016}}</ref>

===2021–present===
Browining appeared in [[Andrea Pallaoro]]'s 2022 drama ''[[Monica (2022 film)|Monica]]'', alongside [[Trace Lysette]], [[Patricia Clarkson]] and [[Adriana Barraza]], replacing [[Anna Paquin]] who had dropped out of the movie due to scheduling conflicts.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Wiseman|first1=Andreas|date=19 June 2021|title=Emily Browning Replaces Anna Paquin In Drama 'Monica' With Trace Lysette, Patricia Clarkson & Adriana Barraza; Filming Underway In Ohio|url=https://deadline.com/2021/06/american-gods-emily-browning-anna-paquin-monica-trace-lysette-filming-ohio-1234783216/|access-date=21 July 2022|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en-US}}</ref> {{Asof|2022}} she was also set to star in Lance Edmands' thriller ''Brightwater'', starring alongside [[Scoot McNairy]] and [[Jack Reynor]].<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Wiseman|first1=Andreas|date=6 May 2022|title=Scoot McNairy, Jack Reynor & Emily Browning Lead Thriller 'Brightwater' With James Schamus Exec Producer & Bankside Launching Sales|url=https://deadline.com/2022/05/scoot-mcnairy-narcos-jack-reynor-emily-browning-brightwater-james-schamus-cannes-1235017908/|access-date=21 July 2022|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en-US}}</ref>

She stars in ''[[The Fox (2025 film)|The Fox]]'', the debut feature film directed by Australian filmmaker [[Dario Russo]], which premieres at the 2025 [[Adelaide Film Festival]] in October. It also stars [[Jai Courtney]], [[Damon Herriman]], and the voices of [[Sam Neill]] and [[Olivia Colman]].<ref>{{cite web | title=‘It is a ripper’: Adelaide Film Festival adds frontier history and a talking fox in 2025 reveal | website=[[InDaily]]|first= Walter |last= Marsh | date=10 September 2025 | url=https://www.indailysa.com.au/inreview/film-tv/2025/09/10/it-is-a-ripper-adelaide-film-festival-adds-frontier-history-and-a-talking-fox-in-2025-reveal | access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
From 2012 to 2013, she dated British actor [[Max Irons]], whom she met while filming [[The Host (2013 film)|''The Host'']]. From 2013 to 2015, Browning was in a relationship with ''[[Plush (film)|Plush]]'' co-star [[Xavier Samuel]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Osenlund |first=R. Kurt |date=10 October 2013 |title=Catherine Hardwicke On Her Kinky, Twisted Thriller 'Plush' and Why She Considers 'Twilight' an Indie |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2013/10/catherine-hardwicke-on-her-kinky-twisted-thriller-plush-and-why-she-considers-twilight-an-indie-34087/ |access-date=6 August 2023 |website=IndieWire |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Khera |first=Japleen |date=10 January 2021 |title=Is Emily Browning Dating or Married? Who is Emily Browning's Boyfriend? |url=https://thecinemaholic.com/is-emily-browning-dating-anyone-who-is-her-boyfriend/ |access-date=6 July 2023 |website=The Cinemaholic |language=en-US}}</ref>

She married Eddie O'Keefe in April 2023.<ref>{{Cite Instagram |postid=CqxCyugJh-B |user=okeeeeeeefe |title=I got married. |date=2023-04-08}}</ref><ref>{{Cite Instagram |postid=Cuxsf1zPG1F |user=okeeeeeeefe |title=Wedding Dump #1 |date=2023-07-16}}</ref>

When Browning was 21 years old, she moved to [[London]], but then moved to Los Angeles when London became "too expensive to live". She initially disliked Los Angeles but then settled down on the [[Eastside Los Angeles|Eastside]] and was residing there in 2023.<ref>{{cite web | last=Clark | first=Lucie | title=Australian actress Emily Browning on nerves, social media and that Twilight audition | website=Vogue Australia | date=2 April 2019 | url=https://www.vogue.com.au/celebrity/news/australian-actress-emily-browning-on-nerves-social-media-and-that-twilight-audition/news-story/c2075e796904a8c8eb779e829f60b0a5 | access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=26 March 2023 |title=Emily Browning talks depression, body image, and career in her first podcast interview |url=https://ohnotheydidnt.livejournal.com/125605240.html}}</ref> She also has spoken on her depression and stated she has been doing therapy ever since being diagnosed.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-20 |title=Emily Browning on Depression, Body Empowerment, and the Apocalypse |url=https://www.listennotes.com/podcasts/broad-ideas-with/emily-browning-on-depression-hcJmgKotCe-/ |access-date=2024-09-04 |website=Listen Notes |language=en}}</ref>

Browning noted that she is [[spiritual but not religious]]: "I like the idea there is something innately magical about human connection. But I don't know, I'm okay with not knowing, and I get pissed off by anyone who claims to know for sure. A dogmatic [[atheist]] is just as annoying as a [[Bible]]-thumping crazy person."<ref>{{Cite interview| first= Emily| last=Browning |interviewer-last=Law |interviewer-first=Benjamin |date=2019-02-23| interviewer-link= Benjamin Law (writer) |title=Dicey Topics: Emily Browning talks religion, politics and bodies |url=https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/tv-and-radio/dicey-topics-emily-browning-talks-religion-politics-and-bodies-20190218-p50yiy.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240727164537/https://www.smh.com.au/entertainment/tv-and-radio/dicey-topics-emily-browning-talks-religion-politics-and-bodies-20190218-p50yiy.html |archive-date=2024-07-27 |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=The Sunday Morning Herald |language=en-AU}}</ref>

{{short description|American actress}} {{Use American English|date=April 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2018}} {{Infobox person | image = PortiaDoubledayTIFFSept09.jpg (cropped).jpg | caption = Doubleday at the [[2009 Toronto International Film Festival]] | name = Portia Doubleday | birth_name = | birth_date = {{birth date and age|mf=yes|1988|6|22}} | birth_place = [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], U.S. | occupation = Actress | years_active = 1998; 2009–present | height = | othername = | parents = [[Frank Doubleday (actor)|Frank Doubleday]]
[[Christina Hart]] | family = [[Kaitlin Doubleday]] (sister) }} '''Portia Doubleday''' (born June 22, 1988) is an American actress. She is best known for her roles as Sheeni Saunders in the film ''[[Youth in Revolt (film)|Youth in Revolt]]'' (2009) and as [[Angela Moss]] in the [[USA Network]] television drama ''[[Mr. Robot]]'' (2015–2019). ==Early life and education == Born and raised in [[Los Angeles]], Portia Doubleday is the younger of two daughters of [[Christina Hart]] and [[Frank Doubleday (actor)|Frank Doubleday]]. She grew up in a show business family: her parents are former professional actors, and her older sister [[Kaitlin Doubleday|Kaitlin]] is also an actress.{{Cite news | last = Ouzounian | first = Richard | title = Portia Doubleday: Michael Cera's transformer | newspaper = [[Toronto Star]] | location = [[Toronto]] | date = January 5, 2010 | url = https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/movies/article/745966--portia-doubleday-michael-cera-s-transformer | access-date = January 7, 2010}} Her mother now works in the entertainment industry as a writer and producer of plays.{{Cite news | last = Stein | first = Ruthe | title = Youth in Revolt's Portia Doubleday making a name for herself | newspaper = [[Houston Chronicle]] | location = [[Houston]] | date = January 6, 2010 | url = http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/ent/6801359.html | access-date = January 7, 2010}} Doubleday attended the [[Los Angeles Center for Enriched Studies]], a [[magnet school]] in west Los Angeles.{{cite news |last=Patti |first=Greco |url=http://www.cosmopolitan.com/entertainment/tv/q-and-a/a47372/kaitlin-portia-doubleday-sisters-interview/ |title=Sisters Kaitlin and Portia Doubleday on "Empire" and "Mr. Robot," Sibling Rivalry, and High School |work=[[Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmopolitan]] |date=October 7, 2015 |access-date=February 29, 2016 }} She played [[soccer]] for 12 years and described herself as a [[tomboy]].{{Cite news | last = Ordoña | first = Michael | title = Brains and beauty in 'Youth in Revolt' | newspaper = [[Los Angeles Times]] | location = Los Angeles | date = January 7, 2010 | url = http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/news/la-et-performance7-2010jan07,0,3951896.story | access-date = January 7, 2010}} ==Career== Doubleday first appeared in a commercial for [[Goldfish (snack)|Goldfish crackers]] at age eight and had a small role in the film ''[[Bram Stoker's Legend of the Mummy|Legend of the Mummy]]'' (1998). Her parents insisted that she finish high school before pursuing a career in acting. After graduating high school, Doubleday was cast in the pilot episode of ''[[United States of Tara]]'', a television series created by [[Diablo Cody]]. Doubleday played 15-year-old Kate, the daughter of [[Toni Collette]]'s character. Doubleday was replaced by [[Brie Larson]] when the series' creative team chose to go in a different direction with the character. She appeared in the short film ''18'' in 2009, about a girl dealing with the end of her mother's life.{{cite news | last = Ordoña | first = Michael | title = Where you've seen Portia Doubleday | newspaper = [[Los Angeles Times]] | location = Los Angeles | date = January 7, 2010 | url = http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/news/la-et-performancebox7-2010jan07,0,5335100.story | access-date = January 7, 2010}} Doubleday starred opposite [[Michael Cera]] in the 2009 teen comedy ''[[Youth in Revolt (film)|Youth in Revolt]]'', based on the 1993 [[Youth in Revolt|novel of the same name]] by [[C.D. Payne]]. Doubleday described her character as "mean" and "really complex" to the ''[[Los Angeles Times]].'' She plays Sheeni Saunders, an imaginative girl with a dreary life who meets Michael Cera's character while on a family vacation. The film was directed by [[Miguel Arteta]] and premiered at the 2009 [[Toronto International Film Festival]]. In 2010, Doubleday starred in the drama ''Almost Kings'' (formerly known as ''Touchback'') directed by Marvin Jarrett (the founder of ''[[Nylon (magazine)|Nylon]]'' magazine). She appeared regularly in the ABC network comedy ''[[Mr. Sunshine (2011 TV series)|Mr. Sunshine]],'' a [[midseason replacement]] for the 2010–2011 season.{{cite web |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/content_display/television/news/e3i3602f61793f3cd8856ce093985a11040 |title=Matthew Perry project a go at ABC |date=January 12, 2010 |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=April 25, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100115084541/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/hr/content_display/television/news/e3i3602f61793f3cd8856ce093985a11040 |archive-date=January 15, 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://livefeed.hollywoodreporter.com/2010/05/abc-2010-fall-schedule.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100520014127/http://livefeed.hollywoodreporter.com/2010/05/abc-2010-fall-schedule.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 20, 2010 |title=ABC's new fall schedule |last=Hibberd |first=James |date=May 18, 2010 |work=The Hollywood Reporter |access-date=May 18, 2010 }} In 2013, she played a brief role in ''[[Her (2013 film)|Her]]'' as a [[sex surrogate]]. In September 2014, it was announced that Doubleday had joined the main cast of the [[USA Network]] [[Television pilot|pilot]] for the TV series ''[[Mr. Robot]]''.{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2014/09/ortia-doubleday-carly-chaikin-mr-robot-pilot-usa-network-833062/|title=Portia Doubleday, Carly Chaikin Join USA Pilot 'Mr. Robot'; Rupert Evans In Amazon's 'Man In The High Castle'|author=|date=2014-09-11|website=Deadline|language=en|access-date=2019-11-21}} Doubleday plays Malek's character's childhood friend and current co-worker, Angela Moss. The first episode of the series premiered on June 24, 2015. She appeared in all four seasons of the show, the final three premiering in July 2016, October 2017, and October 2019 respectively. In November 2018, it was announced that Doubleday had joined the cast of the film ''[[Fantasy Island (film)|Fantasy Island]]'', an adaptation of [[Fantasy Island|the show of the same name]].{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/discussingfilm/status/1062420408958418945?lang=en|title=Maggie Q, Portia Doubleday and Ryan Hansen have joined the cast of Jeff Wadlow's 'FANTASY ISLAND'. (EXCLUSIVE)|last=DiscussingFilm|date=2018-11-13|website=@discussingfilm|language=en|access-date=2019-11-13}} The movie was released on February 14, 2020.{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiewire.com/2019/11/fantasy-island-trailer-blumhouse-horror-1202188708/|title='Fantasy Island' Trailer: Blumhouse Twists Show Into Careful-What-You-Wish-For Horror|last=Lattanzio|first=Ryan|date=2019-11-11|website=IndieWire|language=en|access-date=2019-11-13}} == Personal life == {{as of|2018}}, Doubleday was living in Los Angeles.{{Cite web|url=https://together.nbcuni.com/article/beyond-the-screen-with-portia-doubleday/|title=Beyond the Screen with Portia Doubleday {{!}} NBCUniversal Together|website=together.nbcuni.com|date=April 2, 2018|language=en|access-date=2019-11-13}} ==Filmography== ===Film=== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! '''Tiera Skovbye''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|s|k|oʊ|b|i}} {{respell|SKOH|bee}};<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M0XzPDR_Bzo|title=Tiera Skovbye x MOOD magazine interview|website=[[YouTube]]|date=May 19, 2018}}</ref> born May 6, 1994<ref>{{cite web|author=Tiera Skovbye|url=https://instagram.com/p/BTw1yYghCqW/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/BTw1yYghCqW |archive-date=December 24, 2021 |url-access=registration|title=Waitttt did I just wake up for 50k on my bday?!? YEESSSS thank you guys!!|via=Instagram|date=May 6, 2017|access-date=2017-05-06}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref name="Hello!" />) is a Canadian actress. She began her career as a [[Child actor|child actress]]. She is known for starring in television films such as her role playing [[Elizabeth Berkley]] in [[Lifetime (TV network)|Lifetime's]] ''[[The Unauthorized Saved by the Bell Story]]''; for her recurring roles as [[Families of Archie's Gang#Polly and Chic Cooper|Polly Cooper]] on [[The CW]] series ''[[Riverdale (2017 TV series)|Riverdale]]'', as Robin on the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] television series ''[[Once Upon a Time (TV series)|Once Upon a Time]]''. Skovbye starred as Grace Knight on the [[Global Television Network|Global]] series ''[[Nurses (Canadian TV series)|Nurses]]''.

==Career==
Skovbye's first substantial role was as the 10-year-old Jane on the drama series ''[[Painkiller Jane (TV series)|Painkiller Jane]]'' in 2007. Skovbye has also appeared in a number of [[television film]]s, most notably [[Lifetime (TV network)|Lifetime's]] ''[[The Unauthorized Saved by the Bell Story]]'' in which she played [[Elizabeth Berkley]].<ref name="THR-TUSbtBS">{{cite news |author=Philiana Ng |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/unauthorized-saved-by-bell-tv-713208 |title='Unauthorized Saved by the Bell' TV Movie Heads to Lifetime |newspaper=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=June 19, 2014 |access-date=2015-11-24}}</ref><ref name="V-TUSbtBS">{{cite journal |author=Whitney Friedlander |url=https://variety.com/2014/tv/news/saved-by-the-bell-movie-1201223989/ |title='Saved by the Bell' Movie to Air on Lifetime |journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=June 19, 2014 |access-date=2015-11-24}}</ref>

In early 2017, she began playing the recurring role of Polly Cooper on [[The CW]] teen drama series ''[[Riverdale (2017 TV series)|Riverdale]]''.<ref name="Hello!">{{cite web |author=Erica Cupido |url=http://ca.hellomagazine.com/film/02017030133753/riverdale-tiera-skovbye-interview%20/ |title=Meet Riverdale's Polly: Tiera Skovbye on playing the show's most mysterious character |magazine=[[Hello! (magazine)|Hello! Canada]] |date=March 2, 2017 |access-date=2017-05-01}}</ref><ref name="Cosmo">{{cite web |author=Peggy Truong |url=https://www.cosmopolitan.com/entertainment/tv/a20708446/riverdale-tiera-skovbye-polly-interview/ |title=Tiera Skovbye on 'Riverdale' Fan Theories and Polly's Mysterious Farm |magazine=[[Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmopolitan]] |date=May 17, 2018 |access-date=2018-06-12}}</ref> Skovbye played the recurring role of [[Robin Hood|Robin]], the daughter of [[Wicked Witch of the West|Zelena]] and [[Robin Hood]], and her cursed counterpart, Margot, during the seventh season of ''[[Once Upon a Time (TV series)|Once Upon a Time]]''.<ref name="Once">{{cite web|url=https://www.tvline.com/casting-news/once-upon-a-time-season-7-tiera-skovbye-zelena-daughter-robin-881486/|title=Once Upon a Time Casts Riverdale's Tiera Skovbye as [Spoiler]'s Daughter|author=Matt Webb Mitovich|work=TVLine|date=November 1, 2017|access-date=2017-11-01}}</ref><ref name="Once2">{{cite web|author=Natalie Abrams|url=https://ew.com/tv/2018/05/15/once-upon-a-time-rose-reynolds-tiera-skovbye-series-finale-interview/|title=''Once Upon a Time''{{'}}s Rose Reynolds, Tiera Skovbye on show's final love story|work=Entertainment Weekly|date=May 15, 2018|access-date=2018-06-12}}</ref> In 2018, she appeared in the horror mystery film ''[[Summer of 84]]'', opposite [[Graham Verchere]], [[Judah Lewis]], and [[Rich Sommer]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/news/3446344/mad-men-riverdale-stars-head-back-summer-84/ |title="Mad Men" and "Riverdale" Stars Head Back to the 'Summer of '84' |author=John Squires |work=Bloody Disgusting |date=July 12, 2017 |access-date=2018-12-06}}</ref>

Skovbye starred as Grace Knight on the [[Global Television Network|Global]] drama series ''[[Nurses (Canadian TV series)|Nurses]]'',<ref name="Nurses">{{cite web |author=Debra Yeo |url=https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/television/2019/04/04/here-are-the-actors-starring-in-global-tvs-nurses.html |title=Here are the actors starring in Global TV's Nurses |work=[[Toronto Star]] |date=April 4, 2019 |access-date=2019-07-14}}</ref> which ran from 2020 to 2021.

==Personal life==
Skovbye was born in [[Vancouver]], British Columbia.<ref name="Hello!" /> She has a younger sister, Ali,<ref>{{cite web|author=Tiera Skovbye|url=https://instagram.com/p/2vCK51LoG3/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/2vCK51LoG3 |archive-date=December 24, 2021 |url-access=registration|title=Happy Birthday to my (not so) little sister!|via=Instagram|date=May 16, 2015|access-date=2017-05-06}}{{cbignore}}</ref> who is also an actress, and who co-stars on the Netflix series ''[[Firefly Lane]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2021/feb/03/firefly-lane-katherine-heigl-sarah-chalke-netflix|title=Firefly Lane review – Katherine Heigl's sickly-sweet Netflix soap|website=[[TheGuardian.com]]|date=February 3, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hallmarkchannel.com/campfire-kiss/cast/ali-skovbye|title=Campfire Kiss – Cast – Ali Skobye|publisher=Hallmark Channel|access-date=2018-06-12|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170716142238/http://www.hallmarkchannel.com/campfire-kiss/cast/ali-skovbye|archive-date=2017-07-16}}</ref>

'''Camila Carraro Mendes'''<ref name="Biography">{{cite web|title=Camila Mendes|url=https://www.biography.com/actor/camila-mendes|website=Biography (A&E Networks)|date=July 17, 2020|access-date=July 26, 2021|archive-date=July 26, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726063312/https://www.biography.com/actor/camila-mendes|url-status=live}}</ref> ({{IPAc-en|k|ə|ˈ|m|iː|l|ə|_|ˈ|m|ɛ|n|d|ɛ|z}}; {{IPA|pt-br|ˈmẽdʒis|lang}}; born June 29, 1994)<ref name="Biography"/><ref>{{cite tweet |user=CamilaMendes |number=880895769250811905 |title=thank you for all the birthday wishes and making 23 feel more interesting than it is❤️ |date=June 29, 2017 |access-date=July 17, 2017 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/CQlmD |archive-date=May 7, 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref> is an American <!--Do NOT add Brazilian, please read WP:ETHNICITY.--> actress and producer. She made her acting debut portraying [[Veronica Lodge]] on [[The CW]] teen drama series ''[[Riverdale (2016 TV series)|Riverdale]]'' (2017–2023), for which she won a [[Teen Choice Award]] in 2017.

Mendes transitioned her career to film, taking on supporting roles in ''[[The New Romantic]]'' (2018), ''[[The Perfect Date]]'' (2019), and ''[[Palm Springs (2020 film)|Palm Springs]]'' (2020). She has since played leading roles in the [[crime thriller]] film ''[[Coyote Lake (film)|Coyote Lake]]'' (2019), [[Dark humor|black comedy]] film ''[[Do Revenge]]'' (2022), the romantic comedies ''[[Upgraded (film)|Upgraded]]'' (2024), ''[[Música (2024 film)|Música]]'' (2024), and the [[sword-and-sorcery]] film ''[[Masters of the Universe (2026 film)|Masters of the Universe]]'' (2026).

==Career==
[[File:KJ Apa, Lili Reinhart & Camila Mendes (33697264831).jpg|thumb|left|[[KJ Apa]], [[Lili Reinhart]] and Mendes at the [[WonderCon]] in 2017]]
Mendes's first acting job was a commercial for [[IKEA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://daman.co.id/camila-mendes-shines-in-the-new-tv-series-riverdale-based-on-archie-comics/|work=[[Da Man]]|title=Camila Mendes Shines in the New TV Series "Riverdale" Based on Archie Comics|date=February 8, 2017|access-date=March 20, 2017|archive-date=July 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170701191834/http://daman.co.id/camila-mendes-shines-in-the-new-tv-series-riverdale-based-on-archie-comics/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2016, Mendes was cast as "silver-tongued high school sophomore" [[Veronica Lodge]] in [[The CW]]'s teen drama series ''[[Riverdale (2017 TV series)|Riverdale]]'' (2017–2023), a subversive take on the [[Archie Comics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2016/02/riverdale-archie-comics-pilot-veronica-camila-mendes-cw-1201710249/|title='Riverdale' CW Pilot Finds Veronica|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=February 26, 2016|access-date=February 26, 2016|archive-date=February 27, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160227231916/http://deadline.com/2016/02/riverdale-archie-comics-pilot-veronica-camila-mendes-cw-1201710249/|url-status=live}}</ref> For her performance, she won the [[Teen Choice Awards|Teen Choice Award for Choice Scene Stealer]] in 2017.<ref name=":0" /> Mendes was represented by the Carson Kolker Organization, later changing to [[Creative Artists Agency|CAA]].<ref name="HR" />

Mendes made her feature film debut as Morgan in ''[[The New Romantic]]'', which premiered at the [[SXSW Festival]] in March 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2018/02/the-new-romantic-clip-sxsw-jessica-barden-carly-stone-1202303577/ |title='The New Romantic' Clip: A Struggling College Graduate Becomes A Sugar Baby In SXSW Comedy |last=Ramos |first=Dino-Ray |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=February 27, 2018 |access-date=May 20, 2018 |archive-date=February 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210212021118/https://deadline.com/2018/02/the-new-romantic-clip-sxsw-jessica-barden-carly-stone-1202303577/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In the same month, Mendes joined the cast of the romantic comedy ''[[The Perfect Date]]''.<ref name="standinthr">{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/riverdale-star-camila-mendes-matt-walsh-star-stand-1097772 |title='Riverdale' Actress Camila Mendes, Matt Walsh to Star in 'The Stand-In' |last=Galuppo |first=Mia |date=March 27, 2018 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=May 20, 2018 |archive-date=September 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928102938/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/riverdale-star-camila-mendes-matt-walsh-star-stand-1097772 |url-status=live }}</ref> The film was released on [[Netflix]] on April 12, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://us.hola.com/celebrities/2019032622388/camila-mendes-the-perfect-date/|title=Camila Mendes stars in Netflix's 'The Perfect Date'|last=Torres|first=Alejandra|date=March 26, 2019|website=HOLA USA|access-date=March 28, 2019|archive-date=March 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327130414/https://us.hola.com/celebrities/2019032622388/camila-mendes-the-perfect-date/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2019, the film ''Coyote Lake'' premiered, in which Mendes is the lead. In 2020, she appeared in the critically acclaimed sci-fi/comedy ''[[Palm Springs (2020 film)|Palm Springs]]'', which premiered at the [[Sundance Film Festival]] and was released that July on [[Hulu]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Potts |first1=Mark |title=Andy Samberg, Camila Mendes and Cristin Milioti talk new movie 'Palm Springs' |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/story/2020-01-27/abcs-of-palm-springs-sundance |website=The Los Angeles Times |date=January 27, 2020 |access-date=July 12, 2020 |archive-date=July 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200712082437/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/story/2020-01-27/abcs-of-palm-springs-sundance |url-status=live }}</ref> She subsequently headlined the Netflix [[thriller film]] ''[[Dangerous Lies (2020 film)|Dangerous Lies]]'', released that same year.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Schaffstall|first=Katherine|date=May 1, 2020|title='Riverdale' Star Camila Mendes on More Mature Role in "Dangerous Lies': "It Felt Nice to Graduate"|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/camila-mendes-dangerous-lies-interview-1292860/|magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=March 27, 2023|archive-date=March 27, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230327210527/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/camila-mendes-dangerous-lies-interview-1292860/|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Javier  Galán Gil''' (born 19 November 1994) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays a [[left-back]], [[left wing-back]] or [[left winger]] for [[La Liga]] club [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta]].

==Career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Badajoz]], [[Extremadura]], Galán represented CD San Roque Badajoz, CP Don Bosco and CP Flecha Negra as a youth.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elperiodicoextremadura.com/noticias/deportes/javi-galan-mejora-rooney_982829.html|title=Javi Galán mejora a 'Rooney'|trans-title=Javi Galán improves to 'Rooney'|publisher=El Periódico de Extremadura|language=es|date=8 December 2016|accessdate=21 May 2017}}</ref> On 20 June 2013, after scoring 12 goals for the latter's ''Juvenil A'' squad, he moved to [[CD Badajoz]].<ref name="Hoy">{{cite web|url=http://www.hoy.es/20130620/deportes/futbol/badajoz-1905-ficha-javier-201306201848.html|title=El Badajoz 1905 ficha a Javier Galán, alias 'Rooney'|trans-title=Badajoz 1905 sign Javier Galán, alias 'Rooney'|publisher=Hoy|language=es|date=20 June 2013|accessdate=12 October 2016}}</ref>

Galán made his senior debut on 15 September 2013, playing the last 30 minutes in a 1–0 home win against CD Solana for the ''Regional Preferente'' championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cdbadajoz.com/cdb1905/index.php/temporada-2013-2014/2015-07-11-18-47-36/matchreport/6-2013-2014-regional-preferente/1008|title=Jornada 1 – Domingo, 15. Septiembre 2013 – 18:00 h|trans-title=Matchday 1 – Sunday, 16 September 2013 – 18h|publisher=CD Badajoz|language=es|accessdate=12 October 2016}}</ref> He scored his first senior goal fourteen days later, netting the last in a 4–1 home routing of EF Emérita Augusta.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cdbadajoz.com/cdb1905/index.php/temporada-2013-2014/2015-07-11-18-47-36/matchreport/6-2013-2014-regional-preferente/1024|title=Jornada 3 – Domingo, 29. Septiembre 2013 – 17:00 h|trans-title=Matchday 3 – Sunday, 29 September 2013 – 17h|publisher=CD Badajoz|language=es|accessdate=12 October 2016|archive-date=13 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013145757/http://www.cdbadajoz.com/cdb1905/index.php/temporada-2013-2014/2015-07-11-18-47-36/matchreport/6-2013-2014-regional-preferente/1024|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Galán helped the ''Blanquinegros'' in their promotion to [[Tercera División]] during his first campaign.

===Córdoba===
On 9 July 2015, Galán joined [[Córdoba CF]], being assigned to [[Córdoba CF B|the reserves]] also in the fourth tier.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cordobadeporte.com/futbol-cordobes/alejandro-roser-esteve-monterde-javier-galan-fichajes-para-el-b|title=Alejandro Roser, Esteve Monterde y Javier Galán, fichajes para el B|trans-title=Alejandro Roser, Esteve Monterde and Javier Galán, signings for the B|publisher=Córdoba Deporte|language=es|date=9 July 2015|accessdate=12 October 2016|archive-date=21 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321213918/https://cordobadeporte.com/futbol-cordobes/alejandro-roser-esteve-monterde-javier-galan-fichajes-para-el-b|url-status=dead}}</ref> Upon arriving, he became an immediate first choice for the B's.

Galán made his professional debut on 12 October 2016, starting as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left back]] in a 2–1 [[Copa del Rey]] away win against [[Cádiz CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/copa-rey/2016/10/12/57fe91f7e5fdea885f8b4639.html|title=El Córdoba muestra mejores condiciones en el Carranza|trans-title=Córdoba show much better conditions at the Carranza|publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=12 October 2016|accessdate=12 October 2016}}</ref> He made his [[Segunda División]] debut on 4 December, starting in a 2–1 win at [[CF Reus Deportiu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/2016/12/04/58448214268e3e23098b4669.html|title=El 'efecto Carrión' lo traslada el Córdoba a la Liga en Reus|trans-title=The 'Carrión effect' moves to the league in Reus|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=4 December 2016|accessdate=4 December 2016}}</ref>

On 12 December 2016, Galán renewed his contract until 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cordobacf.com/noticia/marc-vito-esteve-monterde-y-javi-galan-renuevan-con-el-cordoba-cf|title=Marc Vito, Esteve Monterde y Javi Galán renuevan con el Córdoba CF|trans-title=Marc Vito, Esteve Monterde and Javi Galán renew with Córdoba CF|publisher=Córdoba CF|language=es|date=12 December 2016|accessdate=17 December 2016}}</ref> Five days later he scored his first professional goal, netting the first in a 2–1 win at [[Real Oviedo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/2016/12/17/58558784e2704e9d158b4667.html|title=El Córdoba cierra el año derrotando al Real Oviedo en su "fortín"|trans-title=Córdoba end the year defeating Real Oviedo in their "fortress"|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=17 December 2016|accessdate=17 December 2016}}</ref>

Galán was an undisputed starter during the [[2017–18 Segunda División|2017–18 campaign]]; converted to a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left back]] by manager [[Jorge Romero Sáez|Jorge Romero]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportball.es/javi-galan-reconversion-cordoba-cf/|title=Javi Galán: una reconversión acertada del Córdoba CF|trans-title=Javi Galán: a correct conversion of Córdoba CF|publisher=SportBall|language=es|date=30 March 2018|accessdate=19 October 2018}}</ref> he went on to score two goals in 40 appearances as his side narrowly avoided relegation.

===Huesca===
On 29 January 2019, Galan moved to [[La Liga]] side [[SD Huesca]] on a three-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sdhuesca.es/noticia/javi-galan-un-zurdo-para-la-sd-huesca|title=Javi Galán, un zurdo para la SD Huesca|trans-title=Javi Galán, a left-footed to SD Huesca|publisher=SD Huesca|language=es|date=29 January 2019|accessdate=31 January 2019}}</ref> He made his debut in the top tier on 1 February, starting in a 4–0 home routing of [[Real Valladolid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/primera-division/cronica/2019/02/01/5c54bf62ca4741eb2d8b460b.html|title=El 'nuevo' Huesca sí puede|trans-title=The 'new' Huesca can do it|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=1 February 2019|accessdate=2 February 2019}}</ref>

Galán immediately became a regular starter for the side, suffering relegation in [[2018–19 La Liga|his first season]] but immediately bouncing back as champions in [[2019–20 Segunda División|his second]]. He scored his first goal in the top tier on 6 February 2021, netting the opener in a 1–2 home loss to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].

===Celta===
On 31 July 2021, after [[2020–21 La Liga|suffering another relegation]] with Huesca, Galán signed a five-year contract with [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta de Vigo]] in the top tier.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rccelta.es/equipo/actualidad/javi-galan-fichaje-de-gran-nivel-para-el-lateral-zurdo-del-rc-celta/|title=Javi Galán, fichaje de gran nivel para el lateral zurdo del RC Celta|trans-title=Javi Galán, high standard signing for the left back of RC Celta|publisher=Celta Vigo|language=es|date=31 July 2021|accessdate=31 July 2021}}</ref>

=== Atlético Madrid ===
On 3 July 2023, Galán signed a contract until June 2026 with fellow La Liga club [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-03 |title=Club Atlético de Madrid - Welcome, Javi Galán! |url=https://en.atleticodemadrid.com/noticias/welcome-javi-galan |access-date=2023-07-06 |website=Club Atlético de Madrid |language=en}}</ref>

==== Real Sociedad (loan) ====
On 24 January 2024, Atlético Madrid sent Galán on loan to fellow La Liga club [[Real Sociedad]] until the end of the [[2023–24 Real Sociedad season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 January 2024 |title=Agreement for the loan of Javi Galán |url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/en/news/details/agreement-for-the-loan-of-javi-galan |access-date=25 January 2024 |publisher=Real Sociedad |language=en}}</ref>

=== Osasuna ===
On 24 December 2025, Galán joined fellow La Liga club [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], signing a contract until the end of the [[2025–26 La Liga|2025–26 season]], for a fee of €500.000, which could rise to €1 million in case of a contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 December 2025 |title=Osasuna alcanza un acuerdo con el Atlético de Madrid para la incorporación de Javi Galán |trans-title=Osasuna reaches an agreement with Atlético Madrid for the signing of Javi Galán |url=https://www.osasuna.es/javi-galan-incorporacion-osasuna |access-date=24 December 2025 |publisher=[[CA Osasuna]] |language=es}}</ref>

=== Return to Celta ===
On 30 June 2026, Galán returned to Celta, joining on a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2026 |title=Javi Galán returns to Celta to reinforce the left flank |url=https://rccelta.es/en/equipo/actualidad/javi-galan-returns-to-celta-to-reinforce-the-left-flank/ |access-date=30 June 2026 |publisher=[[RC Celta de Vigo]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Galán is physically likened to England international forward [[Wayne Rooney]], with his nickname being ''Rooney'' during his youth career and Badajoz.<ref name="Hoy"/>
