'''Jucimar José Teixeira''' (born 20 May 1990), commonly known as '''Alemão''', is a Brazilian [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right back]] for [[Maringá Futebol Clube|Maringá FC]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Oliveira dos Brejinhos]], [[Bahia]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://jornalnovafronteira.com.br/botafogo-contrata-jogador-nascido-em-oliveira-dos-brejinhos/|title=Botafogo contrata jogador nascido em Oliveira dos Brejinhos|trans-title=Botafogo sign player born in Oliveira dos Brejinhos|publisher=Jornal Nova Fronteira|language=pt|date=16 September 2016|accessdate=10 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161110235407/http://jornalnovafronteira.com.br/botafogo-contrata-jogador-nascido-em-oliveira-dos-brejinhos/|archive-date=10 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Alemão made his debut as a senior with [[Clube Atlético Taboão da Serra|Taboão da Serra]] in 2009, and subsequently served loan stints at German club [[VfL Nagold]], [[Serrano Sport Club|Serrano-BA]], [[Nacional Atlético Clube (SP)|Nacional-SP]] and [[Associação Atlética Flamengo|Flamengo-SP]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://extra.globo.com/esporte/botafogo/lateral-direito-alemao-supera-infancia-dura-vira-jogo-no-botafogo-20261493.html|title=Lateral-direito Alemão supera infância dura e vira o jogo no Botafogo|trans-title=Right back Alemão overcomes rough childhood and turns things around at Botafogo|publisher=Extra|language=pt|date=9 October 2016|accessdate=10 November 2016}}</ref> In January 2014, he joined [[União Agrícola Barbarense Futebol Clube|União Barbarense]] after his contract with ''CATS'' expired.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sbnoticias.com.br/noticias/119564/uniao-barbarense-apresenta-lateral-direito-alemao-ex--flamengo-de-guarulhos/|title=União Barbarense apresenta lateral-direito Alemão, ex-Flamengo de Guarulhos|trans-title=União Barbarense present right back Alemão, formerly of Flamengo de Guarulhos|publisher=SBNotícias|language=pt|date=27 January 2014|accessdate=10 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111060951/http://www.sbnoticias.com.br/noticias/119564/uniao-barbarense-apresenta-lateral-direito-alemao-ex--flamengo-de-guarulhos/|archive-date=11 November 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 4 December 2014 Alemão moved to [[Independente Futebol Clube|Independente]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.futebolinterior.com.br/futebol/Independente-SP/noticias/2014-12/Independente-acerta-com-Alemao-e-Romarinho-para-a-Serie-A2-Paulista|title=Independente acerta com Alemão e Romarinho para a Série A2 do Paulista|trans-title=Independente sign Alemão and Romarinho for the Série A2 of Paulista|publisher=Futebol Interior|language=pt|date=4 December 2014|accessdate=10 November 2016}}</ref> becoming an undisputed starter for the side in their first [[Campeonato Paulista Série A2]] ever. In May 2015, he signed for [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série B|Série B]] club [[Clube Atlético Bragantino|Bragantino]].

Alemão made his professional debut on 16 May 2015, starting in a 1–0 home win against [[Paysandu Sport Club|Paysandu]]. He became a regular starter for the club during [[2015 Campeonato Brasileiro Série B|the campaign]], appearing in 26 matches.

On 15 September 2016, Alemão was loaned to [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] club [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] until the end of the year, with a buyout clause.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/noticia/2016/09/achou-o-lateral-botafogo-faz-acordo-com-bragantino-para-contratar-alemao.html|title=Achou o lateral! Botafogo faz acordo com Bragantino para contratar Alemão|trans-title=Full back found! Botafogo agree deal with Bragantino to sign Alemão|publisher=Globo Esporte|language=pt|date=15 September 2016|accessdate=10 November 2016}}</ref> He made his debut in the category on 1 October, starting in a 2–0 home win against [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]].

On 28 December 2016, Alemão was bought outright by ''Bota'' for a fee of [[Brazilian real|R$]] 600,000 (for 60% of his federative rights) and signed a three-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/rj/futebol/noticia/2016/12/botafogo-aceita-pagar-o-bragantino-vista-e-encaminha-compra-de-alemao.html|title=Botafogo aceita pagar Bragantino à vista e acerta compra de Alemão|trans-title=Botafogo accept paying Bragantino all at once and complete transfer of Alemão|publisher=Globo Esporte|language=pt|date=28 December 2016|accessdate=16 January 2017}}</ref>

However, a couple of weeks later on January 20, 2017, the contract with Botafogo was withdrawn and he signed with [[Sport Club Internacional]] on a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/rs/futebol/times/internacional/noticia/2017/01/inter-anuncia-contratacao-do-lateral-direito-alemao-por-tres-temporadas.html|trans-title=Inter announce signing of right-back Alemão for three seasons|title=Inter anuncia contratação do lateral-direito Alemão por três temporadas|language=pt|date=20 January 2017|work=[[Rede Globo]]}}</ref> He joined <ref>{{cite web|url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/pr/futebol/times/parana-clube/noticia/parana-clube-confirma-lateral-alemao-e-zagueiro-marcio-e-mira-mais-tres-reforcos.ghtml|title=Paraná Clube confirma lateral Alemão e zagueiro Márcio e mira mais três reforços|trans-title=Paraná Clube confirms German side and defender Márcio and aims for three more reinforcements|language=pt|date=9 January 2018|first1=Fernando|last1=Freire|first2=Thiago|last2=Ribeiro|work=[[Rede Globo]]}}</ref>  For the 2019 season, he joined [[Figueirense FC|Figueirense]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/sc/futebol/times/figueirense/noticia/alemao-teixeira-confirma-saida-do-figueirense.ghtml|title=Alemão Teixeira confirma saída do Figueirense|trans-title=Alemão Teixeira confirms departure from Figueirense|language=pt|date=3 September 2019|work=NSC Total}}</ref> Late in 2020, he signed with [[Esporte Clube Água Santa|Água Santa]] for the [[Copa Paulista]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://m.futebolinterior.com.br/noticias/copa-paulista-agua-santa-anuncia-lateral-direito-alemao|title=Copa Paulista: Água Santa anuncia reforço para o setor defensivo: "Clube de tradição"|trans-title=Copa Paulista: Água Santa announces reinforcement for the defensive sector: "Clube de tradition"|language=pt|date=2 September 2020|work=Futbol Interior}}</ref>

'''Sergio''' "'''Sergi'''" '''Segura García''' (born 30 August 1995) is a Spanish [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left back]] for [[CD Guadalajara (Spain)|CD Guadalajara]].

==Club career==
Segura was born in [[Villarreal]], [[Province of Castellón|Castellón]], [[Valencian Community]], and was a [[CD Castellón]] youth graduate. In 2014 he joined [[CD Leganés]], being initially assigned to [[CD Leganés B|the reserves]] in [[Divisiones Regionales de Fútbol in the Community of Madrid|the regional leagues]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.futmadrid.com/noticia/sergi-segura-debuto-con-el-c-dot-d-leganes-b.html|title=Sergi Segura debutó con el C.D. Leganés "B"|trans-title=Sergi Segura debuted with C.D. Leganés B|publisher=Fut Madrid|language=Spanish|date=18 October 2014|accessdate=1 December 2016}}</ref>

Segura made his first-team debut on 29 November 2016, starting in a 1–3 home loss against [[Valencia CF]] for [[2016–17 Copa del Rey|the season]]'s [[Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2016_17/copa/dieciseisavos/ida/leg_val/|title=El Valencia se agarra a la Copa|trans-title=Valencia hold on to the Cup|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|last=Callero|first=Borja Luis|language=Spanish|date=29 November 2016|accessdate=1 December 2016}}</ref> He left the club in the following year, and moved to [[Segunda División B]] side [[CDA Navalcarnero]].

In 2021, after two seasons at [[CF Pozuelo de Alarcón]], Segura signed for [[Segunda División RFEF]] side [[CD Guadalajara (Spain)|CD Guadalajara]]. He agreed to a deal with [[Mérida AD]] of the [[Primera Federación]] on 15 June 2024,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hoy.es/deportes/futbol/primera-rfef/primera-nueva-cara-merida-sergi-segura-20240615191348-nt.html|title=La primera nueva cara del Mérida es la de Sergi Segura|trans-title=Mérida's first new face is Sergi Segura|publisher=[[Hoy (Extremadura)|Hoy]]|language=es|date=15 June 2024|accessdate=30 July 2026}}</ref> but returned to the fourth division the following 24 January, with [[CE Sabadell FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cesabadellfc.com/es/sergi-segura-nuevo-jugador-del-ce-sabadell/|title=Sergi Segura, nuevo jugador del CE Sabadell|trans-title=Sergi Segura, new player of CE Sabadell|publisher=CE Sabadell FC|language=es|date=24 January 2025|accessdate=30 July 2026}}</ref>

On 14 July 2026, after achieving two consecutive promotions with the ''Arquelinats'', Segura returned to Guadalajara on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdguadalajara.es/sergi-segura-regresa-al-club-deportivo-guadalajara/|title=Sergi Segura regresa al Club Deportivo Guadalajara|trans-title=Sergi Segura returns to Club Deportivo Guadalajara|publisher=CD Guadalajara|language=es|date=14 July 2026|accessdate=30 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Alok Achkar Peres Petrillo''' ({{IPA|pt-BR|aˈlɔki}}; born 26 August 1991), known mononymously as '''Alok''', is a Brazilian [[musician]], [[Disc jockey|DJ]], and [[record producer]] who is best known for his 2016 single "[[Hear Me Now (Alok song)|Hear Me Now]]".<ref>{{cite web|title=Oito motivos que fazem de Alok o DJ mais top do momento|url=http://musica.uol.com.br/listas/oito-motivos-que-fazem-de-alok-o-dj-mais-top-do-momento.htm|website=[[Universo Online]] | access-date=January 20, 2017|language=pt|date=January 12, 2017}}</ref> Since 2021, Alok was ranked the 4th best DJ in the world by ''[[DJ Mag]]'' for 4 consecutive years.<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://djmag.com/top100dj?year=2022 |title=Top 100 DJs 2022 |magazine=[[DJ Mag]] |access-date=17 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://djmag.com/top100dj?year=2021 |title=Top 100 DJs 2021 |magazine=[[DJ Mag]] |access-date=January 15, 2022}}</ref> In 2025, he achieved his highest placement to date, being named the third-best DJ in the world by the same publication.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-23 |title=Alok {{!}} Top 100 DJs 2025 {{!}} DJMag.com |url=https://djmag.com/top100djs/2025/3/alok |access-date=2025-10-01 |website=DJ Mag |language=en}}</ref>

Alok has become one of the most prominent icons in the Brazilian [[Electronic music|electronic scene]], with honors and awards, such as "Best DJ in Brazil" by House Mag in 2014 and 2015,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Top 50 DJs - RANKING 2015|url=http://www.housemag.com.br/www/top50djs.html|website=Housemag}}</ref> and being the only Brazilian in the top 25 in the world the following year by ''[[DJ Mag]]'' magazine.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Top 100 DJs 2016 {{!}} DJMag.com.|url=https://djmag.com/top100dj|website=DJ Magazine}}</ref> In 2017, he was elected by ''Forbes'' Brasil as one of the most influential people under the age of 30 in the country.<ref>{{Cite web|title=91 Brazilian highlights under the age of 30|url=http://www.forbes.com.br/listas/2017/03/91-destaques-brasileiros-abaixo-dos-30-anos/|website=Forbes Brazil|date=March 21, 2017 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Petrillo was born in [[Goiânia]], Brazil, the son of DJs Swarup and Ekanta, who are also pioneers of [[Psychedelic trance|psytrance]] in the country and creators of the Universo Paralello, electronic music festival in [[Bahia]].<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|url=https://www.musicnonstop.com.br/falamos-com-os-pais-e-irmao-djs-de-alok-em-entrevista-exclusiva/|title=Família que toca unida... Falamos com o irmão e os pais DJs de Alok em entrevista exclusiva com a família Petrillo – music non-stop|date=February 15, 2016|newspaper=music non-stop|language=pt-BR|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref>

His name came after his parents travelled to [[India]], where they met with spiritual guru [[Rajneesh|Osho]], who indicated that their child should be called Alok, which in the [[Sanskrit language]] means "light".<ref>{{cite web|last=Angel|first=Rozze|title=Alok Petrillo o DJ STAR|url=https://issuu.com/dropsmag/docs/dropsmag_56_digital|work=Drops Mag|publisher=issuu|access-date=January 27, 2017|date=April 25, 2016|pages=46–47|language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ff.garena.com/chars/intro/en/146/|title=Free Fire Bio}} Garena contracted with Alok for FreeFire. Also the Sanskrit translation for 'Alok' is  'light'</ref>

== Career ==
Alok began his career at the age of 12 along with his [[fraternal twin]] brother Bhaskar Petrillo.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.opopular.com.br/editorias/magazine/considerado-o-dj-n%C3%BAmero-1-do-pa%C3%ADs-o-goiano-alok-petrillo-%C3%A9-atra%C3%A7%C3%A3o-da-festa-da-fantasia-sunrise-1.1066535|title=Considerado o DJ número 1 do País, o goiano Alok Petrillo é atração da Festa da Fantasia Sunrise|last=Lima|first=Gabriela|date=April 9, 2016|newspaper=Jornal O Popular|language=pt-BR|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref> At age 19 he pursued a solo career, becoming one of the most prominent icons in the Brazilian electronic scene, with honors and awards, such as "Best DJ in Brazil" awarded by House Mag for two consecutive times (in the years 2014 and 2015)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.housemag.com.br/www/top50djs.html|title=House Mag {{!}} A revista brasileira de música eletrônica.|website=House Mag|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref> and the only Brazilian in the top 25 world DJ ranking by [[DJ Mag]]azine in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://djmag.com/top100dj|title=Top 100 DJs 2016 {{!}} DJMag.com|website=djmag.com|access-date=December 14, 2016}}</ref>

At age 10 he began to learn to play, along with Bhaskar.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://musicaeletronicabrasileira.com/index.php/men-rod-entrevistas/178-alok|title=Alok Petrillo – Revelação da Música Eletrônica Brasileira em 2014|website=musicaeletronicabrasileira.com|access-date=December 14, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018190725/http://musicaeletronicabrasileira.com/index.php/men-rod-entrevistas/178-alok|archive-date=October 18, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2004, Petrillo and his brother visited the rehearsal studio of their father Swarup's band. According to Ekanta, his sons were interested in how the remixes were made. DJs Zumbi and Pedrão, family friends, taught the brothers to mix songs. Each one learned a specialty, one on the keyboard and the other on the guitar. Shortly thereafter, Dick Trevor installed the [[Logic Pro]] music editing program on Swarup's computer, bringing the brothers closer to producing music.<ref name="auto" />

Petrillo and his brother attended the performances that their parents did at psytrance paries and soon created their first project, Logica.<ref name="auto" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.breaktudo.com/mathix-acaba-de-lancar-novo-single-ouca-fuck-you-bitch/|title=Mathix acaba de lançar novo single, ouça "Fuck You Bitch" {{!}} BreakTudo|date=July 6, 2017|work=BreakTudo|access-date=July 8, 2017|language=pt-BR|archive-date=December 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171225202828/http://www.breaktudo.com/mathix-acaba-de-lancar-novo-single-ouca-fuck-you-bitch/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Petrillo is also the founder of [[UP Club Records]], a record label specializing in discovering new inborn talent in [[electronic music]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.phouse.com.br/up-club-alok-lanca-propria-gravadora/|title=UP CLUB: Alok lança própria gravadora|website=www.phouse.com.br|access-date=December 14, 2016|date=May 28, 2015|archive-date=October 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171018133914/http://www.phouse.com.br/up-club-alok-lanca-propria-gravadora/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In November 2019, Alok Petrillo became a character of [[Garena Free Fire]] under his name Alok and Song released Vale Vale with Zafrir.<ref>{{Cite news|title=DJ Alok becomes Garena Free Fire's resident DJ|url=https://www.pocketgamer.com/articles/081450/dj-alok-becomes-garena-free-fires-resident-dj/|last=Bald|first=Cameron|date=November 5, 2019|access-date=August 14, 2021|work=[[Pocket Gamer]]}}</ref> in August 2021, according to in-game info from Garena Free Fire Alok is the most used character in game. Petrillo along with [[Dimitri Vegas & Like Mike]] & [[Kshmr|KSHMR]] released "Reunion" on Controversia & [[Smash The House]] for Free Fire's 4th anniversary.<ref>{{Citation|title=Alok, Dimitri Vegas & Like Mike, KSHMR, ZAFRIR – Reunion (Free Fire 4th Anniversary Theme Song)| date=20 August 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vgFTUPbjxZI|language=en|access-date=2021-08-22}}</ref>

==Record label==
On 3 July 2019, Alok released a song called "The Wall" along with American DJ Sevenn as the first release from his record label Controversia, a label he created in partnership with [[Spinnin Records]] to release Brazilian bass music.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alok, Sevenn – The Wall | date=3 July 2019 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sYeQMOykeVs&list=PLkiL2bBp1220dNXOZrdxf2TJ4whEx5nD7&index=190|via=[[YouTube]]|language=en|access-date=2019-07-03}}</ref>

'''Jared Abrahamson''' (born November 19, 1987<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jared Abrahamson, Acteur.trice |url=https://www.cineserie.com/persons/380533/ |access-date=November 1, 2025 |website=CinéSérie |language=fr-FR}}</ref>) is a Canadian actor. He is known for his performance in the 2016 film ''[[Hello Destroyer]]'', for which he was nominated for a [[Canadian Screen Award]] for [[Canadian Screen Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] and won the award for Best Actor in a Canadian Film at the [[Vancouver Film Critics Circle Awards 2016]], and for portraying Trevor Holden in the sci-fi series ''[[Travelers (TV series)|Travelers]].''

==Early life and education==
Jared Abrahamson is originally from [[Flin Flon]], Manitoba, Canada, a mining town of 5,500. Abrahamson spent two years working underground there as a miner before studying acting at the [[Vancouver Film School]].<ref name="viffmma">{{cite web |last=Crawford |first=Julie |date=September 14, 2016 |title=VIFF: Vancouver actor's unlikely journey from mines to MMA to movies |url=http://www.vancourier.com/entertainment/movies/viff-vancouver-actor-s-unlikely-journey-from-mines-to-mma-to-movies-1.2343621 |work=[[Vancouver Courier]]}}</ref>

==Career==
Abrahamson is known for his performance in the 2016 film ''[[Hello Destroyer]]'', for which he was nominated for a [[Canadian Screen Award]] for [[Canadian Screen Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/entertainment/canadian-screen-awards-nominations-1.3938015|title=''Orphan Black'', ''Schitt's Creek'', ''Kim's Convenience'' up for Canadian Screen Awards|date=January 17, 2017|work=[[CBC News]]}}</ref> and won the award for Best Actor in a Canadian Film at the [[Vancouver Film Critics Circle Awards 2016]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.vancourier.com/entertainment/movies/vancouver-film-critics-circle-takes-a-shine-to-hello-destroyer-manchester-by-the-sea-1.7711765|title=Vancouver Film Critics Circle takes a shine to ''Hello Destroyer'', ''Manchester by the Sea''|last=Crawford|first=Julie|date=January 17, 2017|work=[[Vancouver Courier]]}}</ref>

He portrayed Trevor Holden in the [[Showcase (Canadian TV channel)|Showcase]] and [[Netflix]] series ''[[Travelers (TV series)|Travelers]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.nytimes.com/2016/12/28/arts/television/review-in-travelers-some-serious-time-sharing.html|title=Review: In ''Travelers'', Some Serious Time-Sharing |last= Genzlinger |first= Neil |date=December 28, 2016|work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>

He was named one of the [[Toronto International Film Festival]]'s Rising Stars of 2016, alongside [[Grace Glowicki]], [[Mylène Mackay]] and [[Sophie Nélisse]].<ref>{{cite web |url= http://www.tribute.ca/tiff/index.php/2016/08/03/tiff-announces-2016-rising-stars/#.WH7z37kb0o0|title=TIFF announces 2016 Rising Stars!|work=[[Tribute (magazine)|Tribute]] |date= August 3, 2016}}</ref>

Abrahamson has also appeared in the television series ''[[Awkward (TV series)|Awkward]]'' and ''[[Fear the Walking Dead]]'', ''[[Letterkenny (TV series)|Letterkenny]]'', and the films ''[[The Submarine Kid]]'' and ''[[Never Steady, Never Still]]''.

Recorded November 15, 2022}} }} '''Thomas Jonathan Ossoff''' ({{IPAc-en|'|ɒ|s|ɔ:|f|audio=En-us-Ossoff.ogg}} {{Respell|OSS|off}}; born February 16, 1987) is an American politician who has served as the [[Seniority in the United States Senate|senior]] [[United States Senate|United States senator]] from [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] since 2021.{{efn|Despite being sworn in at the same time as fellow Georgia Senator [[Raphael Warnock]], Ossoff is the senior senator because his surname precedes Warnock's alphabetically.}} He is the [[List of youngest members of the United States Congress|youngest incumbent U.S. senator]], and a member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]]. Raised in [[Metro Atlanta]], Ossoff graduated from [[Georgetown University]] and the [[London School of Economics]]. He worked as a national security staffer and legislative assistant for U.S. representative [[Hank Johnson]] and afterward was managing director of an investigative documentary production company. He first ran for Congress in a [[2017 Georgia's 6th congressional district special election|2017 special election]], narrowly losing a seat that had long been considered a [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] stronghold. Ossoff was first elected to the U.S. Senate in [[2020–21 United States Senate election in Georgia|2021]], defeating Republican incumbent [[David Perdue]] in a runoff. Ossoff was elected alongside [[Raphael Warnock]] on [[2020–21 United States Senate special election in Georgia|the same day]], which was critical in securing a [[117th United States Congress|50–50 Senate majority]] for Democrats, with vice president [[Kamala Harris]] serving as the tie-breaking vote.{{Cite web |date=2021-01-06|title=Democrats retake the Senate with Georgia sweep|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/01/06/warnock-celebrates-runoff-win-455308|access-date=|website=POLITICO|language=en}} Ossoff is the [[List of youngest members of the United States Congress|youngest person]] elected to the Senate since [[1980 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|1980]], the first senator born in the 1980s, and the first [[Millennials|millennial]] United States senator. Alongside Warnock, he is one of only two Democrats to represent Georgia in the United States Senate since [[Zell Miller]] left office in 2005.{{TOC limit|3}} == Early life and education == Ossoff was There's also the Ossoff who works with Republicans, advancing the interests of Georgia's farmers and military bases."{{Cite web |date=2025-05-05 |title=Balancing Trump criticism and bipartisanship, Democrat Jon Ossoff walks a fine line in Georgia |url=https://apnews.com/article/georgia-senate-2026-jon-ossoff-democrat-dde4e55d7d2e12e6fc166f436a83ea8c |access-date=2025-05-08 |website=AP News |language=en}} === Abortion === Ossoff supports [[United States abortion-rights movement|abortion rights]].{{cite news|last1=Bluestein|first1=Greg|date=May 21, 2017|title=Abortion debate divides candidates in Georgia's 6th District race|url=https://www.ajc.com/news/state--regional-govt--politics/abortion-debate-divides-candidates-georgia-6th-district-race/AwjZ8WkOxxhUQNf50lC1hP/|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|access-date=August 21, 2020}} He pledged to support only those judges who would uphold ''[[Roe v. Wade]]'', and he also supports [[Planned Parenthood]].{{Cite web |date=January 7, 2021 |title=Senators-elect Rev. Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff Solidify Reproductive Rights Majority in Congress |url=https://www.plannedparenthoodaction.org/pressroom/senators-elect-rev-raphael-warnock-and-jon-ossoff-solidify-reproductive-rights-majority-in-congress |website=Planned Parenthood}} In response to the [[Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization|June 2022 overturning of ''Roe v. Wade'']], Ossoff stated that the [[Supreme Court of the United States|U.S. Supreme Court]] "stripped American women of autonomy over their most personal health care decisions."{{cite web |last1=Ossoff |first1=Jon |title=Sen. @ossoff statement on Dobbs v. as he weighs US Senate run |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/politics/ossoff-sharpens-populist-message-with-pledge-end-broken-college-debt-system/UpTyUMmhxMvHp0y0wRm2RM/ |access-date=January 13, 2021 |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |date=April 14, 2019}} Ossoff says that as a member of the Senate he will push for "nationwide legalization" of cannabis, stating that it "is much less |url=https://www.marijuanamoment.net/georgias-senate-runoffs-could-decide-federal-marijuana-policy-in-2021-heres-where-the-candidates-stand/|work=Marijuana Moment|access-date=January 13, 2021}} === |url=https://www.cbs46.com/jon-ossoff-d/article_dd53da9e-0414-11eb-9bee-cfd38a28f388.html |title=Jon Ossoff on the Issues |publisher=[[WANF|WGCL-TV]] |date=October 1, 2020 |access-date=December 15, 2020 |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108060739/https://www.cbs46.com/jon-ossoff-d/article_dd53da9e-0414-11eb-9bee-cfd38a28f388.html |url-status=dead }} His news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/pb/blogs/right-turn/wp/2017/04/17/the-georgia-special-election-shows-why-trump-may-sink-the-gop/|title=The Georgia special election shows why Trump may sink the GOP|last=Rubin|first=Jennifer|author-link=Jennifer Rubin (columnist)|date=April 17, 2017|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} In 2020, Ossoff opposed [[Defund the police|defunding the police]] and [[Abolish ICE|abolishing]] [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement]] (ICE). === Economy and financial regulation === Ossoff supported increasing economic relief for businesses and households affected by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite news|title=Ossoff on relief bill: 'The bottom line is that $600 is a joke'|publisher=[[WXIA-TV]]|url=https://www.11alive.com/article/news/politics/elections/ossoff-covid-relief-response/85-454fa38d-4af5-4efb-951d-2c8d0e565db6}} Ossoff voted for the [[Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act]].{{Cite web |title=U.S. Senate: U.S. Senate Roll Call Votes 117th Congress – 1st Session |url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1171/vote_117_1_00314.htm |access-date=2024-11-21 |website=Senate.gov}} === Environment === He accepts the [[scientific consensus on climate change]], and has said that "climate change is a threat to our security and prosperity".{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/powerpost/trump-looms-over-georgia-special-election-a-proxy-battle-for-2018/2017/06/10/a9fddce4-4ddd-11e7-9669-250d0b15f83b_story.html |first=Karen |last=Tumulty |title=Trump looms over Georgia special election, a proxy battle for 2018|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=June 10, 2017|access-date=June 12, 2017}} He supports U.S. participation in the [[Paris Agreement]]. David Perdue embodies "Trumpism in a nutshell"|work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]]|url=https://www.axios.com/2020/11/10/jon-ossoff-georgia-senate-runoffs-axios-on-hbo |access-date=November 11, 2020}} In 2022, Ossoff blocked a proposed [[titanium]] mine in the [[Okefenokee Swamp]] after the [[United States Fish and Wildlife Service|U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service]] warned of severe potential damage to the wildlife refuge. The mine was proposed by Twin Pines Minerals LLC in 2018.{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2022/06/04/okefenokee-mine-blocked/ |title=Army Corps blocks strip mine near Okefenokee wetlands after opposition | first=Hamza |last=Shaban |newspaper=Washington Post |date= June 4, 2022}} === Foreign policy === [[File:Συνάντηση ΥΠΕΞ Ν. Δένδια με Γερουσιαστές ΗΠΑ C. Murphy & J. Ossoff (Αθήνα, 06.09.2021) 01.jpg|thumb|Ossoff and U.S. Senator [[Chris Murphy]] meet with Greek [[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Greece)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] [[Nikos Dendias]] on September 6, 2021.]] ==== Afghanistan ==== [[File:Jon Ossoff greets Yoon Suk Yeol.jpg|thumb|Ossoff greets [[President of South Korea|South Korean President]] [[Yoon Suk Yeol]] in 2023.]] Ossoff resisted criticizing President [[Joe Biden]] for the [[Withdrawal of United States troops from Afghanistan (2020–2021)|withdrawal of troops]] from Afghanistan in August 2021, as other Democratic politicians had at the time, instead stating he was focused on "supporting the [[United States Department of State|State Department]] and the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] as they work with limited time to expedite the evacuation" of stranded Americans and American-allied Afghans.{{cite web|url=https://www.ajc.com/politics/politics-blog/the-jolt-jon-ossoff-toes-party-line-on-afghanistan/VDEYI5T6ZVBEZOHSN2NFYBYELA|title=The Jolt: Jon Ossoff avoids Biden bashing on Afghanistan|first1=Patricia|last1=Murphy|first2=Greg|last2=Bluestein|first3=Tia|last3=Mitchell|work=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|date=August 24, 2021}} Ossoff condemned the subsequent [[2021 Kabul airport attack|airport attack]] in [[Kabul]], which killed 13 American military personnel, stating: "I condemn this cowardly and despicable terrorist attack."{{cite web|url=https://www.wtoc.com/2021/08/26/ga-leaders-respond-kabul-bombing-that-killed-american-troops/|title=Ga. leaders respond to Kabul bombing that killed American troops|author=WALB News Team|publisher=WALB|date=August 26, 2021}} ==== China ==== Ossoff was part of a bipartisan visit to China led by Senate Majority Leader [[Chuck Schumer]] in October 2023, where they met with [[General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party]] [[Xi Jinping]] in Beijing. The delegation also met Director of the [[Office of the Central Foreign Affairs Commission]] [[Wang Yi]], [[Chairman of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress]] [[Zhao Leji]], and [[Party Secretary of Shanghai]] [[Chen Jining]].{{Cite news |last1=Wang |first1=Amber |last2=Han |first2=Bochen |date=9 October 2023 |title=US senators defy backlash at home to test China's engagement first-hand |url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3237169/us-senators-defy-backlash-home-test-chinas-engagement-first-hand |access-date=19 December 2024 |work=[[South China Morning Post]]}} ==== Israel ==== In 2020, Ossoff said he is committed to "the security of Israel as the homeland for the Jewish people" and to strengthening the [[US-Israel alliance|U.S.–Israel alliance]].{{cite web |title=Position Paper on U.S.-Israel Relations |url=https://jewishdems.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/2020-7-Ossoff-Israel-Paper.pdf |website=Jewish Democratic Council of America |date=July 2020 |access-date=2 June 2026}} Ossoff led a group of 25 Democratic senators who called for an immediate ceasefire in a joint statement during the [[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wjcl.com/article/led-by-georgias-jon-ossoff-25-plus-senators-call-for-immediate-ceasefire-in-middle-east/36446423|title=Led by Georgia's Jon Ossoff, 25-plus senators call for immediate ceasefire in Middle East|work=CNN|publisher=WJCL|date=May 17, 2021}} The statement said: "Israel has the right to defend itself from [[Hamas]]' rocket attacks, in a manner proportionate with the threat its citizens are facing." Ossoff has stated Israel's situation holds high importance to him due to him having [[Orthodox Judaism|Orthodox]] relatives in the country, saying he wishes for "a future where all people in the region live in peace, live in prosperity, and have equal rights."{{cite web|url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/unlike-fellow-dems-jewish-senator-ossoff-favors-tight-lipped-approach-on-israel/|title=Unlike fellow Dems, Jewish senator Ossoff favors tight-lipped approach on Israel|first=Jacob|last=Magib|work=The Times of Israel|date=September 20, 2021}} On November 20, 2024, Ossoff was among 19 senators who supported resolutions proposed by Senator [[Bernie Sanders]] which would have blocked [[United States support for Israel in the Gaza war|U.S. military aid to Israel]] amidst the [[Gaza war]]. The resolutions failed to pass but were designed to show Democratic opposition to President Biden's and the United States' support for Israel in the Gaza war.{{cite news |title=19 Senators Vote Against More U.S. Weapons For Israel In Rebuke To Biden |first=Akbar Shahid |last=Ahmed |work=[[HuffPost]] |date=November 20, 2024 |access-date=November 21, 2024 |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/senate-vote-against-israel-weapons_n_673e5dfae4b0045528dbd05c}}{{cite news |title=Nineteen Senate Democrats vote to block U.S. aid to Israel |first1=Marc |last1=Rod |first2=Emily |last2=Jacobs |work=[[The Jewish Journal of Greater Los Angeles|Jewish Insider]] |date=November 20, 2024 |access-date=November 21, 2024 |url=https://jewishinsider.com/2024/11/nineteen-senate-democrats-vote-to-block-u-s-aid-to-israel/}} In April 2025, Ossoff voted against a pair of resolutions from Sen. Bernie Sanders to withhold billions of dollars in offensive weapons sales and other military aid to Israel.{{Cite web |last=Neukam |first=Stephen |date=2025-04-03 |title=15 Senate Dems vote to cancel billions in Israeli military aid |url=https://www.axios.com/2025/04/03/senate-democrats-cancel-military-aid-israel |access-date=2025-04-05 |website=Axios |language=en}} Ossoff has publicly acknowledged the importance of the [[Israel–United States relations|U.S.-Israel relationship]] as "ironclad," but does not believe in the position of unconditional American support.{{Cite web |last=Bookman |first=Jay |date=2025-02-20 |title=Bookman: Ossoff chose principle over politics voting against some weapons for Israel |url=https://georgiarecorder.com/2025/02/20/bookman-ossoff-chose-principle-over-politics-voting-against-some-weapons-for-israel/ |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=Georgia Recorder |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Rod |first=Marc |date=2024-11-22 |title=Georgia's only Jewish state legislator slams Ossoff, Warnock for votes against Israel aid |url=https://jewishinsider.com/2024/11/esther-panitch-georgia-jon-ossoff-raphael-warnock-israel-gaza-arms/ |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=Jewish Insider |language=en-US}} In July 2025, Ossoff voted to prohibit a sale of 20,000 fully automatic rifles to Israel.{{cite web|url=https://www.senate.gov/legislative/LIS/roll_call_votes/vote1191/vote_119_1_00454.htm|title=Roll Call Vote 119th Congress - 1st Session|website=Senate.gov|access-date=2026-06-22}}{{Cite web |last=Thakker |first=Prem |date=2025-07-30 |title=In a First, Majority of Democratic Senators Vote to Stop Arming Israel |url=https://zeteo.com/p/breaking-in-a-first-majority-of-democratic |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=Zeteo |language=en-US}} ==== Iran ==== Ossoff has criticized the [[2026 Iran war]].{{Cite news |last=Mackey |first=Robert |date=April 18, 2026 |title=Jon Ossoff calls out 'Mar-a-Lago mafia' amid presidential bid rumors |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/18/jon-ossoff-fiery-speech-presidential-rumors |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=[[The Guardian]]}} He said the war caused "skyrocketing inflation" and "massive damage to our reputation." In March 2026, he voted for a [[War Powers Resolution]] designed to limit President Trump's, or any other president's, ability to use military force in Iran unless congressional authorization was obtained.{{Cite news |last=Gómez |first=Martín González |last2=Yourish |first2=Karen |last3=Parlapiano |first3=Alicia |date=March 4, 2026 |title=How Every Senator Voted on the Iran War Powers Resolution |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/03/04/us/iran-war-powers.html |access-date=July 20, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} === Government reform === Ossoff has called for the repeal of "wasteful, anti-competitive special interest subsidies that make it hard for entrepreneurs to raise capital, enter the market, create jobs, and compete with larger firms who have lobbyists in Washington." He has said the government funds "$16 billion in duplicate programs. That can be cut," an assertion that [[PolitiFact]] rated "Mostly True."{{Cite news|url=https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2017/apr/27/jon-ossoff/checking-jon-ossoff-16-billion-government-waste/ |first=Louis |last=Jacobson |date=April 27, 2017 |title=Checking Jon Ossoff on $16 billion in government waste|publisher=[[PolitiFact]]|access-date=June 17, 2017}} Ossoff supports [[Statehood movement in the District of Columbia|statehood for the District of Columbia]] and for [[Statehood movement in Puerto Rico|Puerto Rico]].{{cite news |last=Talev |first=Margaret |date=November 10, 2020 |title=Jon Ossoff: Georgia opponent Sen. David Perdue embodies "Trumpism in a nutshell" |work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |url=https://www.axios.com/jon-ossoff-georgia-senate-runoffs-axios-on-hbo-08be103c-ff01-40b7-98b9-e3d694d62b21.html |access-date=November 11, 2020}}{{dead link|date=June 2025}} Ending stock trading by members of Congress was a theme of Ossoff's 2020 campaign. === Healthcare === Ossoff supports the [[Affordable Care Act|Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act]] (also known as Obamacare). His health care policy includes three principles: "One, no American should suffer or die from preventable or treatable illness. Two, no one should go broke because they get sick. And three, no business should go under or lay off employees because it can't keep up with health insurance premiums."{{cite news|last=Bluestein|first=Greg|date=April 17, 2017|title=How top Sixth District contenders stack up on healthcare, taxes and transportation|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/politics/how-top-sixth-district-contenders-stack-healthcare-taxes-and-transportation/CTbfYqjU8PFZzc0NICj18H/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170421003349/http://politics.blog.ajc.com/2017/04/17/how-top-sixth-district-contenders-stack-up-on-healthcare-taxes-and-transportation/|archive-date=April 21, 2017}} He does not support pushing for a [[single-payer health care]] system, such as [[Medicare for All]]. He opposed both the March 2017 and May 2017 versions of the [[American Health Care Act of 2017|American Health Care Act]], the House Republican bill that would have repealed the Affordable Care Act.{{Cite news|first1=Elise|last1=Viebeck|first2=David|last2=Weigel|author-link2=David Weigel|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/powerpost/gop-candidate-now-embracing-trump-in-georgias-6th-district-runoff/2017/04/30/28a89bb0-2c5f-11e7-b605-33413c691853_story.html|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=April 30, 2017|title=GOP candidate now embracing Trump in Georgia's 6th District runoff}} He said that the May 2017 version was worse than the earlier one "because it does even less to protect those with [[pre-existing condition]]s."{{cite news|first=Greg|last=Bluestein|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/politics/6th-district-rift-over-the-house-healthcare-plan-tom-price-old-turf/WVVQblWFJTRe6iWdexKljJ/ |title=A 6th District rift over the House healthcare plan in Tom Price's old turf|date=May 4, 2016|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722202652/https://www.ajc.com/blog/politics/6th-district-rift-over-the-house-healthcare-plan-tom-price-old-turf/WVVQblWFJTRe6iWdexKljJ/ |archive-date=July 22, 2019 |url-status=live }} Ossoff told the ''[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]'' that he supported [[tax credit]]s for small businesses related to health care.{{Cite news|first1=Robert|last1=Farley |first2=Eugene|last2=Kiely|url=http://www.factcheck.org/2017/04/trump-distorts-ossoffs-record/|title=Trump Distorts Ossoff's Record|date=April 18, 2017|publisher=[[FactCheck.org]]}} In 2026, Ossoff declared support for "a strong Public Option that’s comprehensive & affordable for all and insist that people who prefer private insurance can always keep it."{{Cite web | title=Jon Ossoff on X: "*All* Americans should have affordable, quality health care. I'll support a strong Public Option that's comprehensive & affordable for all — and insist that people who prefer private insurance can always keep it. Universal coverage, lower costs, more choice, better health." / X | url=https://x.com/ossoff/status/1291459912372027394 | access-date=2026-08-16 | website=x.com}} === Immigration === Ossoff supports [[Immigration reform in the United States|comprehensive immigration reform]] that would both strengthen enforcement along the [[United States-Mexico border|Mexican border]] and provide a [[path to citizenship]] for some [[Illegal immigration to the United States|undocumented immigrants]]. Following the [[murder of Laken Riley]], a Georgia nursing student who was killed by an undocumented immigrant, Ossoff criticized [[Donald Trump]] for his efforts to derail the passage of a [[Bipartisan Border Bill|bipartisan border security bill]].{{cite web |last1=Elliot |first1=Richard |title=How Laken Riley's killing is shaping the immigration debate on both sides of the aisle |url=https://www.wsbtv.com/news/local/atlanta/how-laken-rileys-killing-is-becoming-hot-button-issues-with-both-sides-aisle/GH3DX4QSMFBZVKKI3VMT5JMJUQ/ |website=[[WSB-TV]] |access-date=2026-08-26 |date=2024-02-26}} In 2025, Ossoff was one of 12 Democratic senators who joined all Republicans in voting for the [[Laken Riley Act]].{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5095996-senate-passes-laken-riley-act/|title=Senate passes Laken Riley Act in first move after Trump inauguration|work=The Hill|first=Al|last=Weaver|date=January 20, 2025|accessdate=January 20, 2025}} === LGBTQ rights === Ossoff describes his support for the [[LGBT|LGBTQ]] community as "unwavering".{{cite news|last1=Bauer|first1=Sydney|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/feature/nbc-out/georgia-senate-race-holds-far-reaching-implications-especially-lgbtq-americans-n1251264|title=Georgia Senate race holds far-reaching implications — especially for LGBTQ Americans|publisher=[[NBC News]]|date=December 16, 2020|access-date=March 12, 2021}} He also supports the [[Equality Act (United States)|Equality Act]], which would prohibit discrimination on the basis of sex, gender identity, and sexual orientation.{{cite news|last1=Bauer|first1=Sydney|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/feature/nbc-out/lgbtq-georgians-hopeful-following-warnock-ossoff-senate-victories-n1253485|title=LGBTQ Georgians hopeful following Warnock, Ossoff Senate victories|publisher=[[NBC News]]|date=January 9, 2021|access-date=March 12, 2021}} === First Trump administration === Ossoff has been sharply critical of President [[Donald Trump]], criticizing what he calls Trump's "divisive approach to government"{{Cite news|first=Cristiano |last=Lima|url=https://www.politico.com/story/2017/04/georgia-ossoff-special-election-237307|title=Georgia Democrat rebuffs Trump: 'I don't have great personal admiration' for him|work=[[Politico]]|date=April 17, 2017}} and saying: "I have great respect for the office. I don't have great personal admiration for the man himself."{{Cite news|url=https://thehill.com/blogs/blog-briefing-room/news/329242-george-dem-on-trump-i-dont-have-great-personal-admiration-for/|title=Georgia Dem Ossoff: 'I don't have great personal admiration' for Trump|last=Greenwood|first=Max|work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|date=April 18, 2017}} After Trump sent out a [[Twitter|tweet]] the day before Ossoff's primary on April 19, 2017, calling him a "super Liberal Democrat" who wanted to "protect criminals, allow [[illegal immigration]] and raise taxes", Ossoff dismissed Trump's claims and called him "misinformed".{{Cite news|first=Alex|last=Seitz-Wald|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/storyline/democrats-vs-trump/trump-rips-top-democrat-jon-ossoff-georgia-special-election-n747361|title=Trump takes to Twitter to blast leading Dem as 'super Liberal'|publisher=[[NBC News]]|date=April 17, 2017}} [[FactCheck.org]] found that Trump's claim was a distortion, and that there was no evidence that Ossoff had ever advocated for any broad-based tax hikes. Nevertheless, Ossoff said that he would be willing to work with Trump on issues of mutual interest, such as infrastructure spending. After [[Donald Trump's disclosure of classified information to Russia|Trump's disclosure of classified information to Russia]], Ossoff said of impeachment that "I don't think we're there."{{cite news|first=Greg |last=Bluestein|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/politics/ossoff-trump-impeachment-don-think-there/OLqymNW4d7cYaus054rfiK/ |title=Ossoff on Trump impeachment: 'I don't think we're there'|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=May 30, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201221153828/https://www.ajc.com/blog/politics/ossoff-trump-impeachment-don-think-there/OLqymNW4d7cYaus054rfiK/ |archive-date=December 21, 2020 |url-status=live }} He called for "a full and transparent and independent assessment of what [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections|level of interference there was by Russian intelligence services in the U.S. election]]. And overseers in Congress and any [[Special counsel|independent counsel]] or commission to do so should follow those facts wherever they lead." Ossoff voted to convict Trump during his [[Second impeachment of Donald Trump|second impeachment]] on the charge of [[Sedition|incitement of insurrection]] following the [[2021 United States Capitol attack]], joining all Democrats and seven Republicans.{{cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/interactive/2021/02/politics/senate-who-voted-impeachment/|title=How each senator voted in Trump's second impeachment trial|first1=Christopher|last1=Hickey|first2=Janie|last2=Boschma|first3=Sean|last3=O'Key|publisher=CNN|date=February 13, 2021}} === Voting rights === Ossoff supports passage of the [[John Lewis Voting Rights Act]].{{Cite news|last=Lewis|first=Sophie|date=December 1, 2020|title=Barack Obama narrates new Jon Ossoff ad ahead of Georgia runoff: 'Vote like our lives depend on it, because they do'|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/barack-obama-jon-ossoff-campaign-ad-georgia-run-off-senate-election/|publisher=[[CBS News]]}}{{cite tweet |last=Ossoff |first=Jon |user=ossoff |date=November 16, 2020 |number=1328390660337135617 |title=We can pass the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Act. But only if we win the Senate. |access-date=January 4, 2021}} Following passage of Georgia's [[Election Integrity Act of 2021]], signed into law by Republican governor [[Brian Kemp]] and passed by the Republican-led state legislature, several businesses, from the [[Major League Baseball]] organization to the production of the [[Will Smith]] film ''[[Emancipation (2022 film)|Emancipation]],'' boycotted the state in protest.{{cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2021/04/12/985974670/mlbs-move-out-of-georgia-is-the-latest-in-a-line-of-political-boycotts|title=MLB's Move Out Of Georgia Is The Latest In A Line Of Political Boycotts|first=Domenico|last=Montanaro|publisher=NPR|date=April 12, 2021}} In an interview with [[CNN]], Ossoff expressed his displeasure with the bill, while also saying he didn't support the corporate boycotts, stating Georgians "rely upon and hope for and welcome jobs, investment and opportunity."{{cite web|url=https://transcripts.cnn.com/show/ampr/date/2021-04-15/segment/01|title=Confronting Violence; Afghanistan Peace Negotiations; Interview With Sen. organizational players|url=http://m.indians.mlb.com/news/article/213994026/indians-extend-internal-camp-invitations-to-eight-organizational-players/|work=MLB.com|access-date=February 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170204085400/http://m.indians.mlb.com/news/article/213994026/indians-extend-internal-camp-invitations-to-eight-organizational-players/|archive-date=February 4, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

Rodríguez was rated as the Indians #3 first base prospect entering the 2018 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thesportsdaily.com/2019/07/29/top-10-indians-milb-1b-for-2019-looking-for-the-next-bobby-bradley-brb11/|title=Top 10 Indians MiLB 1B for 2019: Looking for (The Next) Bobby Bradley ||date=July 29, 2019}}</ref> He played in 107 games split between Akron and the Triple–A [[Columbus Clippers]], hitting .228/.308/.416 with 15 home runs and 62 RBI. Rodríguez elected free agency following the season on November 2, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.baseballamerica.com/stories/minor-league-free-agents-2018/|title=Minor League Free Agents 2018|work=Baseball America|first=Matt|last=Eddy|date=November 6, 2018|accessdate=November 8, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190624231938/https://www.baseballamerica.com/stories/minor-league-free-agents-2018/|archive-date=June 24, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> 

Rodríguez re-signed with the Indians on a minor league contract on February 27, 2019. In 78 games for Double–A Akron, he batted .199/.281/.376 with 12 home runs and 42 RBI. Rodríguez elected free agency following the season on November 4.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.baseballamerica.com/stories/minor-league-free-agents-2019/|title=Minor League Free Agents 2019|author=Matt Eddy|website=[[Baseball America]]|date=November 7, 2019|accessdate=November 8, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191107151148/https://www.baseballamerica.com/stories/minor-league-free-agents-2019/|archive-date=November 7, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===York Revolution===
On March 17, 2020, Rodríguez signed with the [[York Revolution]] of the [[Atlantic League of Professional Baseball]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.atlanticleague.com/stats/transactions/|title = Atlantic League Professional Baseball: Transactions}}</ref> He did not play a game for the team because of the cancellation of the ALPB season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and became a free agent after the year. On February 22, 2021, Rodríguez re-signed with the Revolution for the 2021 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/big-arm-big-stick-launch-revolutions-2021-signings/n-5669104|title=Big Arm, Big Stick Launch Revolution's 2021 Signings|date=February 22, 2021}}</ref> In 16 games with York, Rodríguez slashed .371/.467/.597 with 3 home runs and 18 RBI.

===Toros de Tijuana===
On July 4, 2021, Rodríguez signed with the [[Toros de Tijuana]] of the [[Mexican Baseball League|Mexican League]].<ref name=stats125>{{cite web
|url=http://www.milb.com/milb/stats/stats.jsp?t=l_trn&lid=125|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905082652/http://www.milb.com/milb/stats/stats.jsp?t=l_trn&lid=125|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 5, 2015|title=Stats|website=[[Minor League Baseball]]}} </ref> On July 11, Rodríguez was granted his release by Tijuana after going 4-for-20 in 6 games with the team.<ref name=stats125/>

===York Revolution (second stint)===
On July 16, 2021, Rodríguez re-signed with the [[York Revolution]] of the [[Atlantic League of Professional Baseball]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.atlanticleague.com/stats/transactions/|title = Atlantic League Professional Baseball: Transactions}}</ref> Rodríguez was named the Revolution player of the year after batting .316 with 25 home runs and 81 RBI in 91 games with the team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.yorkdispatch.com/story/sports/baseball/york-revolution/2021/10/20/after-dominant-season-rodriguez-named-york-revolution-player-of-year/6109237001/|title = Slugging first baseman named York Revolution Player of Year after dominant season at plate}}</ref> He became a free agent following the season. 

On February 7, 2022, Rodríguez signed with the Revolution for the 2022 season.<ref>{{Cite tweet|user=yorkrevolution|number=1491050780325183492|title=ICYMI: The first of this year's player signings were announced last night via Revs Hot Stove Weekly, presented by @ShipleyEnergy on @WOYK1350! First baseman @RealNRod25 and third baseman Carlos Franco will both be making their return to the 2022 Revolution squad! 🔥💪⚾️|date=8 February 2022|language=en|access-date=8 February 2022}}</ref> He played in 124 games for York, slashing .249/.414/.477 with 26 home runs and 82 RBI.

On February 7, 2023, Rodríguez re-signed with York for the 2023 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Forney Finalizes Coaching Staff, Re-Signs Nellie to Kick off 2023 signings|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/forney-finalizes-coaching-staff-re-signs-nellie-to-kick-off-2023-signings/n-5922425|access-date=2023-02-07|website=oursportscentral.com|date=February 7, 2023 |language=en}}</ref> His 2023 numbers were very similar to those from the previous season: he hit .253/.367/.496 with 24 home runs and 82 RBI in 124 games.

===Pericos de Puebla===
On October 1, 2023, Rodríguez signed with the [[Pericos de Puebla]] of the [[Mexican Baseball League|Mexican League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pericos tiene nuevos peloteros|url=https://cronicapuebla.com/deportes/pericos-tiene-nuevos-peloteros|access-date=March 20, 2024|website=cronicapuebla.com|date=October 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In 51 games for Puebla, he batted .262/.357/.429 with four home runs and 16 RBI. Rodríguez was released by the Pericos on July 17, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LMB: Movimientos en listas de reserva - 17 de julio de 2024|url=https://www.milb.com/mexican/news/lmb-movimientos-en-listas-de-reserva-17-de-julio-de-2024|access-date=July 18, 2024|website=[[Minor League Baseball]]|language=en}}</ref>

===Hagerstown Flying Boxcars===
On July 26, 2024, Rodríguez signed with the [[Hagerstown Flying Boxcars]] of the [[Atlantic League of Professional Baseball]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Transactions|url=http://baseball.pointstreak.com/transactions.html?leagueid=174&seasonid=33927|access-date=July 26, 2024|website=baseball.pointstreak.com|language=en}}</ref> In 44 games for the team, he batted .205/.322/.371 with six home runs and 21 RBI. Rodríguez became a free agent following the season.

===Columbus Pirates===
On August 3, 2025, following the Westerville Expos-Columbus Pirates MSBL game, Rodríguez agreed to terms with the Pirates to participate in the 2025 MSBL Fall Classic in West Palm Beach, FL. Rodriguez will wear #21 for the Pirates, saying "21 on Pirates jersey will always be special!"

==Personal life==
Rodríguez's father, Nelson, was born in the [[Dominican Republic]] and played professional baseball, reaching Double-A with the [[Pittsburgh Pirates]]' organization.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.news-herald.com/news/captains-nellie-rodriguez-determined-to-get-to-big-leagues-to/article_13dbbc12-117c-565c-bf3e-66e0c3d184d3.html |access-date=May 5, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200505234524/https://www.news-herald.com/news/captains-nellie-rodriguez-determined-to-get-to-big-leagues-to/article_13dbbc12-117c-565c-bf3e-66e0c3d184d3.html |title= Captains' Nellie Rodriguez determined to get to big leagues to honor father|work=The News-Herald |archive-date=May 5, 2020 |url-status=live |last1=Glasier |first1=David S. }}</ref>

He began playing guitar around age 11 after receiving a First Act guitar from Walmart. Inspired by the guitar-heavy sound of Beatles albums such as Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band and Abbey Road, particularly the three-guitar-solo section of "The End," he developed an early affinity for John Lennon's playing. Having rarely seen anyone play guitar, Welles initially believed melodies were produced by rapidly turning the tuning pegs, causing him to break several strings. About a year and a half later, he discovered how fretting worked after watching his father press the low E string against the fretboard. Soon afterward, an older neighbor named Harlen Nichols began giving him informal lessons, teaching him songs such as "Camptown Races" with homemade tablature drawn on notecards. Nichols also taught Welles how to tune his instrument and introduced him to older styles of music while playing a 1960s Gibson Hummingbird. As a teenager he began recording songs which he sold on burned CDs. His musical influences growing up included the folk, country, classic rock, and [[Motown]] genres, as well as [[the Beatles]], [[Bob Dylan]], and [[Nirvana (band)|Nirvana]].{{Cite news |last=Peisner |first=David |date=February 12, 2025 |title=Jesse Welles, a Folk Musician Who 'Sings the News,' Is Turning the Page |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/12/arts/music/jesse-welles-middle.html |access-date=March 19, 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} In 2016, Welles lived for a while in an abandoned building turned art commune in the mountains around [[Fayetteville, Arkansas|Fayetteville]]. He formed the band Dead Indian in 2012, along with Dirk Porter and Simon Martin. Kelly made a total of 23 appearances for the Gold Coast in the [[2019 NRL season]] as the club endured a horror year on and off the field. During the halfway mark of the season, head coach [[Garth Brennan]] was sacked by the club after a string of poor results. The Gold Coast managed to win only 4 games for the entire season and finished last claiming the [[Wooden spoon (award)|Wooden Spoon]].{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/jul/14/gold-coast-titans-sack-coach-garth-brennan/|title=Gold Coast Titans sack coach Garth Brennan|website=The Guardian|date=14 July 2019 }} ===2020=== During the 2020 [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and under new NRL biosecurity measures Kelly refused to vaccinate against the flu. He was stood down from the Titans after the [[Queensland Government]] stood by the flu vaccination measures previously agreed to by the NRL that 100% of players would be vaccinated prior to the competition restarting. He was given a last minute reprieve from suspension after agreeing to vaccinate. ===2021=== Kelly played 21 games for the Gold Coast in the [[2021 NRL season]] including the club's elimination final loss to the [[Sydney Roosters]]. ===2022=== In round 24 of the [[2022 NRL season]], Kelly was sent off for a dangerous tackle in the Gold Coast's 36-26 spoon bowl match victory over [[Newcastle Knights|Newcastle]].{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/nrl/nrl-premiership/nrl-2022-gold-coast-titans-vs-newcastle-knights-rabbitohs-live-stream-live-blog-supercoach-scores-videos-aj-brimson-anthony-milford/news-story/1c325d09b4a8aa19627169bcd5b8bd2b/|title=Gutsy 12-man Titans hold on to beat Knights and avoid wooden spoon|website=www.foxsports.com.au|date=28 August 2022 }} Kelly played a total of 17 games for the Gold Coast in the 2022 season scoring seven tries as the club finished 13th on the table.{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/nrl/nrl-premiership/nrl-2022-gold-coast-titans-season-review-justin-holbrook-tino-faasuamaleaui-david-fifita-toby-sexton-jayden-campbell-kieran-foran-jamal-fogarty/news-story/271373bd289c9c920124d2847fde6d5e/|title=Titans' million-dollar man goes missing as Holbrook rues costly mistake: Brutal Review|website=www.foxsports.com.au|date=8 September 2022 }} ===2023=== Kelly played a total of 21 matches for the Gold Coast in the [[2023 NRL season]] and scored six tries as the club finished 14th on the table.{{cite web|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/au/rugby-league/news/nrl-2023-gold-coast-titans-season-review/nel398u2vn7faognqvwnq7g4#:~:text=Did%20the%20Titans%20over%2Ddeliver,out%20of%20the%20finals%20picture./|title=NRL 2023: Gold Coast Titans season review|website=www.sportingnews.com|date=5 September 2023 }} ===2024=== In round 6 of the [[2024 NRL season]], Kelly who was not a noted kicker, converted a goal from the side line to take the Gold Coast's match against [[Canberra Raiders|Canberra]] into golden point extra-time.
