[[Laisha Michelle Oseguera González]] (sister)
[[Abigael González Valencia]] (uncle) | family = | callsign = | awards = | website = | module = | module2 = | module3 = | module4 = | module5 = | module6 = | signature = | signature_size = | signature_alt = | footnotes = Convicted in the [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia]] for murder, drug trafficking and firearm charges }} '''Rubén Oseguera González''' ({{IPA|es|ruˈβen oseˈɣeɾa ɣonˈsales}}; born 14 February 1990), commonly referred to by his alias '''El Menchito''' ({{IPA|es|menˈtʃito}}), is a Mexican-American convicted drug lord and former high-ranking member of the [[Jalisco New Generation Cartel]] (CJNG), a criminal group based in [[Jalisco]]. He is the son of [[Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes]] ("El Mencho"), Mexico's formerly most-wanted man at the time of his death in 2026. Under his father, he allegedly worked as the CJNG's second-in-command and managed international drug trafficking operations. Oseguera González was first arrested in January 2014 in Jalisco, but was released in October for lack of evidence and re-arrested immediately as he walked out of prison. He was then released again in December after a judge considered the evidence against him as insufficient. In June 2015, Oseguera González was arrested again, released a month later, and re-arrested as his release order was made official. His legal case has highlighted the growing tensions and deficiencies between prosecutors and judges in Mexico. In 2017, the [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia]] charged Oseguera González with international drug trafficking. According to the indictment, Oseguera González was responsible for shipping narcotics to the U.S. from Mexico between 2007 and 2017, and of using violence to further his criminal activities. Mexico's [[Secretariat of Foreign Affairs (Mexico)|Secretariat of Foreign Affairs]] approved his extradition request in 2018, and Oseguera González's motions to prevent his transfer to the U.S. have been denied. In Mexico, he was facing trial for money laundering and illegal possession of military-exclusive firearms. After several appeals, Oseguera González was extradited to the U.S. in February 2020 and convicted by a Washington D.C.-based court in September 2024. On 7 March 2025 Oseguera González was sentenced to life imprisonment. ==Early life and career== Rubén Oseguera González was born on 14 February 1990, in [[San Francisco County]], California. He also holds [[Mexican nationality law|Mexican citizenship]]. He has several aliases, including "Rubén Garibay González", "El Junior", "El Rubencito", "El Rojo", "El Niño", and "El Menchito". His last nickname is a [[Spanish nouns#Diminutives, augmentatives and suffixes|diminutive]] of his father's nickname El Mencho, which comes from the [[Phonology#CITEREFAnderson2021|phonetic derivation]] of his name Nemesio. His mother, [[Rosalinda González Valencia]], is the sister of [[Abigael González Valencia]], a former leader of the [[Milenio Cartel]] and [[Los Cuinis]]. His father, [[Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes]] (alias "El Mencho"), was the leader of the [[Jalisco New Generation Cartel]] (CJNG) until his death in 2026 and was one of Mexico's most-wanted men. Oseguera González has two sisters, Jessica Johana and Laisha. According to Mexican government sources, Oseguera González acted as the CJNG's second-in-command, just below his father. He was allegedly responsible for managing the CJNG's operations in buying and selling narcotics from South America to Mexico. He was also accused of coordinating stolen gasoline sales in [[Jalisco]], leading a group of hitmen who killed people who refused to work with the CJNG, overseeing a line of hitmen responsible for protecting CJNG's turf in Jalisco and [[Colima]] from rival gangs like the [[Knights Templar Cartel]] and [[Los Zetas]], and managing the CJNG's financial assets. ==2014 arrest== Since 2013, Mexican authorities were investigating a public telephone booth line and two cellphones linked with high-ranking leaders of the CJNG. According to intelligence reports, one of the mobile lines received a call from the public booth line from a neighborhood Jardines Universidad in [[Zapopan|Zapopan, Jalisco]], prompting an investigation. The [[Mexican Army]] asked the [[Criminal Investigation Agency (Mexico)|Criminal Investigation Agency]] (AIC) branch of the [[Attorney General of Mexico|Office of the General Prosecutor]] (PGR) to investigate the neighborhood and the two mobile lines more closely. The Army began to dispatch [[Undercover operation|undercover]] agents to monitor the neighborhood. On the evening of 29 January 2014, one of the mobile phones was located through [[geolocation]] at a neighborhood in Zapopan before it went out of service. The Army and the Navy decided to send a [[Cuerpo de Fuerzas Especiales|Special Forces]] unit from [[Mexico City]] to Zapopan to investigate the incident. At 3:30 a.m. CT on 30 January, the Special Forces unit raided a residence in neighborhood Patria Universidad and discovered Oseguera González sleeping there. As the authorities took down the doors, Oseguera González woke up from the loud noise and jumped from his bed, ran to his backyard, and climbed the back wall to reach his neighbor's property. However, the Special Forces unit successfully surrounded the premises and reduced Oseguera González's escape options. He eventually submitted and was arrested in his neighbor's backyard. Two of his henchmen surrendered at the door without resisting arrest. Two others, who were renting a nearby house, fled on foot but were arrested too. Oseguera González reportedly offered the officers who detained him around [[Mexican peso|MXN]]$17 million to let him go. Authorities confirmed that they confiscated between MXN$10 to $16 million and US$500,000 at the crime scene, as well as 4 assault rifles, 9 handguns, a grenade, and several rounds of ammunition. Former Attorney General of Mexico [[Jesús Murillo Karam]] confirmed to the press that no gunshots were fired in the operation. Oseguera González was flown that day to Mexico City and taken to the [[SEIDO]], Mexico's anti-organized crime investigatory agency, where he gave his statement and was interrogated by law enforcement. Government sources confirmed that he had no pending formal investigations or arrest warrants issued against him in Jalisco. On 1 February, Oseguera González was taken to [[Federal Social Readaptation Center No. 1]] (also known as "Altiplano"), a maximum-security prison in [[Almoloya de Juárez]], [[State of Mexico]]. Authorities confirmed that he was arrested because of pending charges of money laundering, drug trafficking, and illegal possession of weapons of military-exclusive use. Oseguera González pleaded not guilty and claimed that he worked in construction and was a car salesperson since he was 16 years old. He also claimed that he inherited properties from his mother after she bought them when he was younger and put them under his name. In response to the military operation that resulted in Oseguera González's arrest, CJNG gunmen hijacked three buses and set them on fire throughout the [[Guadalajara Metropolitan Area]]. No deaths or injuries were reported. The U.S. consulate in Guadalajara sent a warning to U.S. citizens in the city and asked them not to travel in the southern part of the urban area, including the main roads leading to the [[Guadalajara International Airport]]. Once the attacks concluded, the Mexican government asked civilians to remain calm and resume their daily activities. Authorities stated that they would remain on alert throughout the Guadalajara area for other violent responses from organized crime. ===Releases=== On 16 October 2014, Oseguera González was released from Altiplano, but he was re-arrested immediately as he walked out of prison by members of the AIC. He was released because a judge from the State of Mexico absolved him from the following crimes: illegal possession of firearms, having weapons of military-exclusive use, use of resources from illicit origins, and crimes against public health. Once in custody, he was then taken to the SEIDO installations and imprisoned there for two months while the PGR worked on getting his jurisdiction to open a trial against him. On 18 December, he was sent to the [[Federal Social Readaptation Center No. 2]] (also known as "Puente Grande"), a maximum-security prison in Jalisco. On 26 December, Oseguera González was released from prison again after a judge concluded that there was insufficient evidence against him for the charges of drug trafficking, overseeing the CJNG's financial operations, and leading a group of hitmen.{{efn|Another source states that a judge ordered his release on 1 January 2015.}} ==2015 arrest== On 23 June 2015, Oseguera González was arrested again by the Mexican Army and the [[Federal Police (Mexico)|Federal Police]] in the Lomas de Altamira neighborhood in Zapopan, Jalisco, this time along with his brother-in-law [[Julio Alberto Castillo Rodríguez]]. The operation lasted about 20 minutes and no shots were fired. The officers entered the private neighborhood in several vehicles at around 2:15 a.m. CT and subdued the entrance guard. They then shot the security cameras with paintball guns to obscure them, destroyed several others, and asked the guard to cut the electricity power in the vicinity. As they were in the entrance booth of the neighborhood, the telephone rang but none of them answered. The guard was then asked to kneel down while the officers entered the neighborhood and apprehended Oseguera González, who was inside a vehicle with Rodríguez Castillo. Authorities confiscated several weapons, including 2 customized [[AR-15 variant|AR-15]] assault rifles engraved with the insignias "CJNG 02 JR" and "Menchito". According to government sources, Oseguera González was trying keep a low profile and had undergone a [[Rhinoplasty|nose surgery]] to alter his identity.{{efn|Another source stated that it was unclear if Oseguera González had done the surgery to alter his appearance.}} He travelled without bodyguards to avoid attracting attention from law enforcement. The government officially confirmed his identity through DNA and physical tests, and photo evidence. At the time of his arrest, he was wanted for organized crime involvement, using resources from illicit origins (money laundering), and kidnapping. The government alleged that when Oseguera González was released from prison the year before, he rejoined the CJNG and began managing their international drug trafficking operations. Once in custody, he was sent to Mexico City and transferred to the SEIDO installations, where he gave his formal declaration. As Oseguera González arrived at the SEIDO via helicopter, a [[Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk|Black Hawk]] Federal Police helicopter with snipers guarded the premises. On 27 June, a federal judge in [[Toluca]] issued an arrest warrant for Oseguera González. He was then transferred to Altiplano prison. Oseguera González's defense argued that their client was detained on illegal grounds because some of the charges he was arrested for were absolved by a judge before, add thus consisted [[double jeopardy]]. The PGR countered this argument by saying that the judge's actions did not mean an absolution from the charges imposed. ===Release and re-arrest=== On 1 July 2015, a federal judge from the State of Mexico ordered Oseguera González's release after concluding that the evidence against him was insufficient and that his [[due process]] had been violated. The judge stated that when Oseguera González was arrested in June, the officers did not have an arrest warrant against him and entered his private property without legal authorization. He also stated that the detainee was in custody for 9 hours and [[Right to counsel|without a lawyer]] before he was sent to the justice department. When the judge considered that authorities had failed to prove that Oseguera González was involved in organized crime, he was released. This was the third time he had been released in less than a year. However, as Oseguera González was walked out of Altiplano, he was re-arrested by the PGR, who had a pending arrest warrant against him. According to government sources, he was wanted for organized crime involvement and for participating in the disappearance of two individuals in [[Tepalcatepec|Tepalcatepec, Michoacán]]. He was sent again to the SEIDO installations by helicopter and escorted by an armed Blackhawk helicopter. On 3 July, a federal court approved the PGR's request to keep Oseguera González under a 40-day preventative detention while authorities work on gathering more evidence against the defense. The request was carried out as part of an investigation by the SEIDO against Oseguera González for his alleged participation in kidnapping. Oseguera González's defense, however, responded by issuing a [[Recurso de amparo|writ of amparo]] in hopes of preventing their client from being detained without charges being filed. A judge denied the defense's request to remove their client's preventative detention on 16 July. On 12 August, a federal judge approved the PGR's request to extend Oseguera González's preventative detention for 40 additional days in order to allow authorities to continue working on gathering evidence against the defense. Later that day, the PGR decided to remove his preventative detention after considering that they had found enough evidence against him. On 13 August, he was issued an arrest warrant and transferred to Altiplano prison on organized crime and bribery charges. The kidnapping charges were suspended. Oseguera González was also investigated for his alleged participation in the murder of four people at a restaurant in Zapopan on 17 May 2013. According to the detainees, Oseguera González planned the attack. ==Imprisonment and legal status== On 28 August 2015, a federal court issued an arrest warrant against Oseguera González and charged him with illegal possession of firearms, using ammunition of exclusive military use, having five weapons of exclusive military use, and organized crime involvement.{{efn|A detainee in possession of at least five weapons of exclusive use from the Mexican Armed Forces is charged with ''acopio de armas''.}} In October, Oseguera González was transferred from Altiplano to [[Federal Social Readaptation Center No. 3]] (also known as "Noreste") in [[Matamoros, Tamaulipas]]. He issued a writ of amparo after claiming that he endured mistreatment and torture. That same month, the PGR opened another case and issued another arrest warrant to charge Oseguera González for acting as the CJNG's second-in-command and ordering homicides against rival drug members. They also stated that he was responsible for coordinating international drug trafficking shipments. The evidence presented to the court consisted of intelligence reports gathered by law enforcement and lawyers. On 4 November, a federal court charged Oseguera González with drug trafficking along with five other suspected CJNG members. Oseguera González issued another writ of amparo in early 2016 to request a transfer back to Altiplano. In February 2016, however, he was transferred to [[Federal Social Readaptation Center No. 3|Federal Social Readaptation Center No. 13]] in [[Miahuatlán de Porfirio Díaz|Miahuatlán de Porfirio Díaz, Oaxaca]]. His defense responded by preparing a writ of amparo for the supposed violations against their client. On 30 June, the PGR via a federal judge in Toluca issued an arrest warrant against Oseguera González and charged him with illegal possession of firearms, using ammunition of military-exclusive weapons, being in possession of at least five military-exclusive weapons, and organized crime involvement. On 22 August, the writ of amparo for mistreatment and torture issued months before was struck down by a judge after he spoke with the prison staff, who denied their involvement in such violations. On 10 November, a judge approved Oseguera González's request to receive a [[conjugal visit]]. The defendant claimed that he was limited by the prison staff from speaking to his lawyers in the past. The judge did not comment on this matter. On 21 February, a court approved Oseguera González's writ of amparo and invalidated his formal imprisonment for organized crime charges. The judge concluded that the charges had several flaws and the evidence presented was insufficient. According to the court, Oseguera González's organized crime charges were based on the testimonies of two Federal Police officers, who described to investigators that he was part of the leadership structure of the CJNG. The judge did not consider this evidence sufficient because the police did not establish how or where they got this information. The PGR submitted the weapons seized during Oseguera González's arrests, and a cap with the insignias of the CJNG that Oseguera González had in his possession when he was taken into custody, as evidence of his alleged involvement in organized crime. They also mentioned his biological relationship with his father and the fact that two alleged members of the CJNG told investigators that Oseguera González worked below him as evidence. The judge did not agree that the weapons and the cap proved Oseguera González's militancy in the CJNG. The judge also dismissed the two testimonies of the alleged CJNG members because they gave conflicting assertions when investigators showed them a picture of Oseguera González and asked them to identify him. Oseguera González was not released from prison because he had four additional pending charges that were not invalidated by the court. On 9 March 2018, a penal court judge tried to have Oseguera González transferred from Oaxaca to the Puente Grande. In July 2019, Oseguera González was transferred to the Federal Social Readaptation Center No. 15, a maximum-security prison in [[Chiapas]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.milenio.com/policia/cartel-jalisco-generacion-trasladan-menchito-cefereso|title=Trasladan a 'El Menchito' a penal de máxima seguridad en Sonora|date=6 September 2019|work=[[Milenio]]|language=es}} Authorities did this after suspected organized crime members uploaded a video on social media warning of Oseguera González's plot to escape from prison.{{Cite news|url=https://www.eloccidental.com.mx/policiaca/el-menchito-habria-sido-traslado-a-otro-penal-tras-advertencia-de-fuga-cjng-3949914.html|title='El Menchito' habría sido traslado a otro penal, tras advertencia de fuga|last=Ibal|first=Eilzabeth|date=25 July 2019|work=El Occidental|publisher=[[Organización Editorial Mexicana]]|language=es}} On 29 August 2019, a federal judge absolved Oseguera González of organized crime involvement and ordered his immediate release. However, he was kept in custody for two additional charges: money laundering and illegal possession of military-exclusive firearms.{{Cite news|url=https://www.milenio.com/policia/el-menchito-con-un-pie-en-corte-de-eu|title='El Menchito', con un pie en corte de EU|last=Mosso|first=Rubén|date=9 September 2019|work=[[Milenio]]|language=es}} On 6 September 2019, Oseguera González was transferred to the Federal Social Readaptation Center No. 11 in [[Hermosillo|Hermosillo, Sonora]]. The [[Secretariat of Security and Civilian Protection (Mexico)|Secretariat of Security and Civilian Protection]] (SSPC) confirmed that Oseguera González stay in Sonora was temporary, and confirmed that the U.S. had an outstanding extradition request against him.{{Cite news|url=https://www.milenio.com/policia/cartel-de-jalisco-nueva-generacion-el-menchito-podria-ser-extraditado|title=Estancia de 'El Menchito' en Sonora es temporal; EU busca extradición: SSP|last=Larios|first=Felipe|date=7 September 2019|work=[[Milenio]]|language=es}} == Extradition process == === Approval process === On 3 February 2017, the [[United States District Court for the District of Columbia]] issued an arrest warrant against Oseguera González. The [[Drug Enforcement Administration]] (DEA) stated that he had been involved in importing and distributing narcotics from Mexico to the U.S. since 2011. The DEA stated that Oseguera González had several other aliases, including "Rubencito", "El Rojo", "El Ruso", and "El Niño". According to the report, the [[United States Department of Justice]] was going to seize all of Oseguera González assets in the U.S. that were a result of his drug proceeds. With the arrest warrant, the U.S. government could formally request his [[extradition]] to the U.S. On 4 October 2018, Mexico's [[Secretariat of Foreign Affairs (Mexico)|Secretariat of Foreign Affairs]] (SRE) approved Oseguera González's extradition to the U.S. He issued a writ of amparo to prevent his extradition. On 16 October 2018, the [[United States Department of State]], [[United States Department of the Treasury|Treasury]], and Justice announced a joint law enforcement measure against the CJNG, and publicized previously sealed indictments charging Oseguera González. The report stated that between 2007 and February 2017, Oseguera González was responsible for importing and distributing narcotics in the U.S. from Mexico, and of using firearms during and to retaliate for his alleged drug trafficking activities. The U.S. government confirmed that the extradition of Oseguera González was pending. In July 2019, Oseguera González's writ of amparo issued against the SRE's extradition approval was denied. His defense argued that Oseguera González was not the person the U.S. government was looking for, and that he was not the son of Oseguera Cervantes. This statement was provided by the defense and support by one of their witnesses. In addition, Oseguera González's defense argued that extraditing him to the U.S. would be unconstitutional because the charges he faces in the U.S. could carry life imprisonment, a conviction length that does not exist in Mexico. === Extradition and convictions === On 21 February 2020, Oseguera González was extradited to the U.S. He arrived at [[Washington Dulles International Airport|Dulles International Airport]] in Washington, D.C. and appeared before a judge that day to face his outstanding charges.{{Cite news|last=Haynes|first=Danielle|url=https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2020/02/21/Mexican-cartel-leader-El-Menchito-extradited-to-US/4441582309211/|title=Mexican cartel leader 'El Menchito' extradited to Mexican cartel figure handed over to U.S. amid surge of extraditions|date=21 February 2020|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|last2=Jouvenal|first2=Justin}} On 20 September 2024, Oseguera González was International Drug Trafficking and Firearms Offenses|publisher=U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency|date=24 September 2024|accessdate=21 November 2024}} On 7 March 2025, Oseguera González received a sentence |url=https://www.bop.gov/inmateloc/ |access-date=11 November 2025 |website=www.bop.gov}} == Impact of United States jailing on CJNG leadership == At the time of his father's death in February 2026, it [[Moriah College]] | occupation = [[Entrepreneur]] }} '''Benjamin Pasternak''' (born September 6, 1999) is an [[Australians|Australian]] technology entrepreneur. He is best known as the co-founder of [[Simulate (company)|Simulate]],{{Cite web |title=Ben Pasternak Biography {{!}} Booking Info for Speaking Engagements |url=https://www.allamericanspeakers.com/celebritytalentbios/Ben+Pasternak/447350 |access-date=2023-05-22 |website=www.allamericanspeakers.com}} an American [[food technology]] company. Previously, Pasternak founded Monkey, a [[Social networking service|social networking]] app that enabled [[teenagers]] to [[video chat]] with like-minded people.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2017/01/16/meet-monkeys-teen-age-founders|title=Meet Monkey's Teen-Age Founders|last=Bethea|first=Charles|magazine=The New Yorker|date=9 January 2017|access-date=6 October 2019|language=en|issn=0028-792X}} He also founded the [[cryptocurrency]] project Believe, which has been the subject of investor litigation. Pasternak was named as one of the world's most influential teenagers by [[Time (magazine)|Time]] in 2016.{{Cite web|title=The 30 Most Influential Teens of 2016|url=https://time.com/4532104/most-influential-teens-2016/|access-date=2021-05-29|website=Time|language=en|archive-date=26 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626234023/https://time.com/4532104/most-influential-teens-2016/|url-status=dead}} In 2021, he was included in the ''[[Forbes]]'' "30 Under 30" list in the consumer technology category.{{Cite web |title=Ben Pasternak |url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/ben-pasternak/ |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Forbes |language=en}} ==Early life and education== Pasternak was born in [[Sydney]], Australia, to Anna Pasternak and Mark Pasternak. He has a younger brother, Jake, and a younger sister, Maya.{{Cite web|url=https://mashable.com/2016/04/14/raising-teenage-startup-founder/|title=What is it like to raise a 16-year-old startup CEO? In a word: stressful.|last=Bogle|first=Ariel|website=Mashable|date=14 April 2016|language=en|access-date=4 October 2019}} His maternal grandfather is property developer Robert Magid {{Cite web| url=https://www.afr.com/rich-list/why-this-rich-lister-is-winding-back-his-property-empire-20230504-p5d5s6 |title = Why this Rich Lister is winding back his property empire|last=Bailey|first=Michael|website=AFR|date=22 May 2023|language=en|access-date=21 August 2026}}. Pasternak was raised in [[Vaucluse, New South Wales|Vaucluse]] in [[Eastern Suburbs (Sydney)|Sydney's Eastern Suburbs]].{{Cite web |title=Mark and Anna Pasternak sell Vaucluse home prior to auction - realestate.com.au |url=https://www.realestate.com.au/news/mark-and-anna-pasternak-sell-vaucluse-home-prior-to-auction/ |access-date=2022-07-06 |website=www.realestate.com.au |language=en}} He was educated at [[Moriah College]] and [[Reddam House]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/technology/is-this-15yearold-australian-the-next-mark-zuckerberg-20141008-10rrzm.html|title=Is this 15-year-old Australian the next Mark Zuckerberg?|last=Francis|first=Hannah|date=8 October 2014|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|language=en|access-date=4 October 2019}} Pasternak started developing [[software]] at the age of 15. He designed his first publicly launched [[mobile app]], ''Impossible Rush'', while bored in science class at school.{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/teens-invent-app-impossible-rush-ben-pasternak_n_5955392|title=This Teen Invented An App That Overtook Tinder, Twitter On The App Charts|last=Mosbergen|first=Dominique|date=9 October 2014|website=HuffPost|language=en|access-date=4 October 2019}} He showed the idea to his online friend Austin Valleskey, an [[iOS]] [[engineer]] from [[Chicago]], and the pair subsequently developed the game. The game went on to be downloaded millions of times and peaked at No. 16 on the [[App Store (iOS)|US App Store (iOS)]] top charts.{{Cite web|url=https://www.businessinsider.com.au/these-two-teenagers-have-briefly-beaten-tinder-and-vine-in-the-app-store-with-an-app-they-coded-while-bored-at-school-2014-10|title=These Two Teenagers Have Briefly Beaten Tinder And Vine In The App Store With An App They Coded While Bored At School|last=Heber|first=Alex|date=9 October 2014|website=Business Insider Australia|language=en|access-date=6 A few months after declining the offers, he dropped out of high school at the age of 15 and moved to [[New York City]] to accept [[venture capital]] funding for his first company.{{cite acquires Monkey to expand video chat for dating and friend discovery|last=Johnson|first=Khari|date=6 February 2018|work=Venture Beat|access-date=11 June 2023}} === Simulate === In early 2018, The company's mission is to upgrade the world to a positive food system. Its first product, Nuggs, is a plant-based [[chicken nugget]] substitute.{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/company/nuggs/about/|title=NUGGS: About {{!}} LinkedIn|access-date=14 July 2019}}{{Cite web|title=Nuggs rebrands as Simulate with new cash, a new CTO and an expanded line of faux-meat foods|url=https://techcrunch.com/2020/07/09/nuggs-rebrands-as-simulate-with-new-cash-a-new-cto-and-an-expanded-line-of-faux-meat-foods/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=TechCrunch|language=en-US}} Simulate's Nuggs launched in July 2019.{{Cite web|last=Berenstein|first=Nadia|title=Can This 19-Year-Old Tech Whiz Make Nuggets — And An Animal-Free Lifestyle — Go Viral With NUGGS?|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/nadiaberenstein/2019/07/10/can-this-baby-tech-whiz-make-nuggets--and-an-animal-free-lifestyle--go-viral-with-nuggs/|access-date=2021-01-17|website=Forbes|language=en}} ===Clout – Believe=== In January 2025, Pasternak presented his Web3 startup Clout, which focused on social media-related blockchain applications. The platform enabled the creation of cryptocurrency tokens associated with individual users who met certain follower thresholds on the app. Pasternak launched a token under the ticker $Pasternak.{{Cite web |date=14 May 2025 |title=LaunchCoin increased 200 times in one day. Why is Believe so powerful after its name change? |url=https://www.panewslab.com/en/articles/4i0c5wir |url-status=live |access-date=14 April 2026 |website=Panewslab}} In May 2025 Pasternak rebranded Clout to Believe.The company switched its focus to launching tokens for [[Meme coin|memecoins]] and startups similar to their own token, newly renamed from $Pasternak to $Launchcoin.{{Cite web |last=Loke |first=Choon Khei |date=26 May 2025 |editor-last=Lim |editor-first=Vera |title=What Is Believe? Launching Memecoins via X Replies |url=https://www.coingecko.com/learn/what-is-believe-token-launchpad |url-status=live |access-date=23 April 2026 |website=Coingecko}} On October 15, 2025, Pasternak announced another renaming of his token from $Launchcoin to $Believe. This sparked a dispute as the $Believe token had 33% more supply than the $Launchcoin token. The extra supply was given to Pasternak and the Believe team without locking period.{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Finn |date=17 December 2025 |title=Kled Founder’s Tirade Against Ben Pasternak Hammers Final Nail into Believe's Coffin |url=https://solanafloor.com/news/kled-founder-s-tirade-against-ben-pasternak-hammers-final-nail-into-believes-coffin |url-status=live |access-date=24 April 2026 |website=SolanaFloor}}{{Cite web |last=Stephanie |first=Olivia |date=23 April 2026 |title=Believe founder arrest adds fresh pressure to token case |url=https://crypto.news/believe-founder-arrest-adds-fresh-pressure-to-token-case/ |url-status=live |access-date=23 April 2026 |website=crypto.news}}{{Cite web |date=15 April 2026 |title=Ben Pasternak Lawsuit: What Crypto Investors Need to Know About the Believe Token Collapse |url=https://phemex.com/academy/who-is-ben-pasternak-lawsuit-believe-token-collapse |url-status=live |access-date=23 April 2026 |website=Phemex}} In December 2025, allegations were made by Avi Patel, founder of Kled.ai, regarding Pasternak’s handling of his supply of the $Kled company token, including claims of token sales following a prior fee arrangement.{{Cite web |date=16 December 2025 |title=Believe founder Ben Pasternak accused of secretly dumping KLED tokens |url=https://protos.com/believe-founder-ben-pasternak-accused-of-secretly-dumping-kled-tokens/ |url-status=live |access-date=14 April 2026 |website=Protos}}{{Cite web |date=17 December 2025 |title=Kled's founder accuses Believe's founder of continuously selling KLED tokens |url=https://www.rootdata.com/news/469466 |url-status=live |access-date=14 April 2026 |website=Rootdata}} The valuation of $Believe dropped, from the migration date in October to December 17, the publication date of the mentioned accusations, by 90% in total. Court for the Southern District of New York on March 23, 2026.{{Cite web |date=11 January 2026 |title=Burwick Law's Class Action Against Believe Platform Covered by New York Law Journal |url=https://www.burwick.law/insights/burwick-laws-class-action-against-believe-platform-covered-by-new-york-law-journal |url-status=live |access-date=14 April 2026 |website=Burwick Law}} It alleged |url=https://www.theblock.co/post/398532/believe-founder-arrested-strangulation |url-status=live |access-date=23 April 2026 |website=The Block}} == Legal issues == In April 2026, Pasternak was charged '''José María Amo Torres''' (born 9 April 1998) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]] for [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona]].

==Club career==
===Sevilla===
Born in {{ill|Las Pajanosas|es}}, [[Province of Seville|Seville]], [[Andalusia]], Amo joined [[Sevilla FC]]'s youth setup in 2006, aged eight; originally a [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]], he subsequently changed to a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.estadiodeportivo.com/sevilla/2014/11/15/jose-maria-amo-joven-promesa-zaga-sevillista/32724.html|title=José María Amo, joven promesa para la zaga sevillista|trans-title=José María Amo, young pearl for the ''sevillista'' defence|publisher=[[Estadio Deportivo]]|language=es|date=15 November 2014|accessdate=20 March 2017}}</ref> On 4 October 2015, aged only 17, he made his senior debut for [[Sevilla Atlético|the reserves]] by starting in a 1–1 away draw against [[Marbella FC]] in the [[Segunda División B]]. Late in the year, British newspaper ''[[The Guardian]]'' named him as one of the fifty most talented youth soccer players in the world.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2015/oct/07/next-generation-2015-50-of-the-best-young-talents-in-world-football|title=Next Generation 2015: 50 of the best young talents in world football|publisher=[[The Guardian]]|date=7 December 2015|accessdate=15 December 2019}}</ref>

Amo contributed with six appearances during [[2015–16 Segunda División B|the campaign]], as [[Sevilla Atlético]] achieved promotion to [[Segunda División]]. On 15 June 2016, despite having suffered a partially torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]] on the right [[knee]], he renewed his contract until 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sevillafc.es/actualidad/noticias/jose-maria-amo-amplia-su-contrato-hasta-2019|title=José María Amo amplía su contrato hasta 2019|trans-title=José María Amo extends his contract until 2019|publisher=Sevilla FC|language=es|date=15 June 2016|accessdate=20 March 2017}}</ref>

On 21 February 2017, Amo scored two spot-kicks for nine-men [[Sevilla FC (youth)|Sevilla under-19]]s in the Round of 16 of the [[2016–17 UEFA Youth League]], giving his side the lead before they ultimately lost 2–3.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lacolinadenervion.com/sevilla-cae-eliminado-la-youth-league/amp/|title=El Sevilla cae eliminado en la Youth League|trans-title=Sevilla falls eliminated in the Youth League|publisher=La Colina de Nervion|language=es|date=21 February 2017|accessdate=14 December 2019}}</ref> Amo made his professional debut with the B-team on 19 March, coming on as a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Marc Gual]] in a 2–1 away win against [[Real Zaragoza]]; after [[Fabrice Ondoa]] was [[sent off]], he featured as the club's goalkeeper for the last minutes, keeping a clean sheet.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/2017/03/18/58cd9bb6268e3e48638b4611.html|title=El Sevilla Atlético hunde al Zaragoza en el descuento y con un jugador de portero|trans-title=Sevilla Atlético sink Zaragoza in the stoppage time and with a field player as a goalkeeper|publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=19 March 2017|accessdate=19 March 2017}}</ref>

Amo tore his [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] and once again suffered [[cruciate ligament]] damage on his right knee on 10 December 2017, being sidelined for seven months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2017/12/20/segunda/1513801261_544502.html|title=José Amo será entre 7 y 8 meses de baja tras nueva operación|trans-title=José Amo will be 7 to 8 months out after new operation|publisher=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=20 December 2017|access-date=13 August 2018}}</ref> Despite being injured, Amo was nominated for the 2018 [[Golden Boy (award)|Golden Boy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/kylian-mbappe/story/3553868/golden-boy-list-includes-kylian-mbappe-christian-pulisic-diogo-dalot|title=Golden Boy list includes Kylian Mbappe, Christian Pulisic, Diogo Dalot|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=2 July 2018|accessdate=15 December 2019}}</ref>

With the B-team down to eight men, Amo scored his first senior goal on 23 February 2019, netting the winning penalty in the 85 minute of a 2–1 away win against [[Club Recreativo Granada]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sevillafc.es/actualidad/1-2-filial-lleva-tres-puntos-granada-jugar-media-hora-ocho-jugadores|title=1–2: El filial se lleva los tres puntos en Granada tras jugar media hora con ocho jugadores|trans-title=1–2: The reserves get the three points in Granada after playing for half an hour with eight players|publisher=Sevilla FC|language=es|date=23 February 2019|accessdate=19 March 2017}}</ref> On 7 May, after contributing with 26 matches during [[2018–19 Segunda División B|the campaign]], he renewed his contract with the ''Nervionenses'' for one more season;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sevillafc.es/actualidad/noticias/amo-renueva-sevilla-fc-2020|title=Amo sella su continudad en el filal por una temporada más|trans-title=Amo confirms his continuity in the reserves for one further season|publisher=Sevilla FC|language=es|date=7 May 2019|accessdate=20 March 2019}}</ref> ahead of the [[2019–20 Segunda División B|2019–20 season]], he was named [[Captain (association football)|team captain]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sevillafc.es/actualidad/noticias/capitanes-sevilla-atletico-2019-2020|title=El Sevilla Atlético elige a sus cuatro capitanes para la presente temporada|trans-title=Sevilla Atlético choose their four captains for the current season|publisher=Sevilla FC|language=es|date=23 August 2019|accessdate=14 December 2019}}</ref>

===Ponferradina===
On 6 August 2020, [[free agent]] Amo signed for [[SD Ponferradina]] in the second division.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sdponferradina.com/noticias/noticia/jose-maria-amo-nuevo-jugador-de-la-sd-ponferradina|title=José María Amo, nuevo jugador de la SD Ponferradina|trans-title=José María Amo, new player of SD Ponferradina|publisher=SD Ponferradina|language=es|date=6 August 2020|accessdate=8 August 2020}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on 11 January of the following year, netting the equalizer in a 1–1 home draw against [[Girona FC]].

On 3 June 2022, after establishing himself as a starter, Amo renewed his contract with ''Ponfe''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elbierzodigital.com/ponferradina-renueva-amo-paris-adot/446407|title=La Ponferradina renueva a Amo y Paris Adot|trans-title=Ponferradina renew Amo and Paris Adot|publisher=El Bierzo Digital|language=es|date=3 June 2022|accessdate=12 July 2023}}</ref> He remained a first-choice during [[2022–23 Segunda División|the campaign]], as the club suffered relegation.

===Tenerife===
On 12 July 2023, Amo signed a three-year deal with [[CD Tenerife]] also in division two.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticias/jose-maria-amo-nuevo-jugador-del-cd-tenerife|title=José María Amo, nuevo jugador del CD Tenerife|trans-title=José María Amo, new player of CD Tenerife|publisher=CD Tenerife|language=es|date=12 July 2023|accessdate=12 July 2023}}</ref> Regularly used in [[2023–24 Segunda División|his first year]], he suffered another knee injury in July 2024<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/segunda/jose-amo-lesionado-de-gravedad-n/|title=José Amo, lesionado de gravedad|trans-title=José Amo, seriously injured|publisher=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=17 July 2024|accessdate=21 June 2026}}</ref> which prevented him to feature in the entire [[2024–25 Segunda División|2024–25 season]], which ended in relegation.

===Lugo===
On 8 July 2025, Amo was announced at [[Primera Federación]] side [[CD Lugo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cdlugo.com/jose-amo-nuevo-jugador-del-cd-lugo/|title=José Amo, nuevo jugador del CD Lugo|trans-title=José Amo, new player of CD Lugo|publisher=CD Lugo|language=es|date=8 July 2025|accessdate=21 June 2026}}</ref> He was regularly used during [[2025–26 Primera Federación|the campaign]], scoring once in 32 matches.

===Gimnàstic===
On 19 June 2026, Amo agreed to a two-year contract with fellow third division side [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gimnasticdetarragona.cat/jose-amo-sincorpora-al-nastic-aportant-experiencia-i-lideratge-a-la-defensa-grana/|title=José Amo s’incorpora al Nàstic aportant experiència i lideratge a la defensa grana|trans-title=José Amo joins ''Nàstic'' bringing experience and leadership to the ''grana'' defense|publisher=Gimnàstic Tarragona|language=ca|date=19 June 2026|accessdate=21 June 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
The son of a [[mayor]], Amo would have become a [[bullfighter]] had he not become a footballer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/videos/2015/05/14/portada/1431600602_089762.html|title=José María Amo: "De no ser futbolista sería torero"|trans-title=José María Amo: "If I were not a football player, I would be a bullfighter"|publisher=Diario AS|language=es|date=14 May 2015|access-date=14 December 2019|archive-date=15 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191215074038/https://as.com/videos/2015/05/14/portada/1431600602_089762.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Yuri Nascimento de Araujo''' (born 13 April 1996), known as '''Yuri Araújo''', is a Brazilian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|winger]] for Japanese [[J1 League]] club [[Yokohama F. Marinos]].

==Career==
Yuri Araújo joined [[Académico de Viseu F.C.|Académico de Viseu]] from [[Lusitano F.C. (Portugal)|Lusitano FCV]] in 2015, and stayed with the club for ten years except for a stint with [[F.C. Penafiel|Penafiel]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.jornaldocentro.pt/yuri-araujo-de-saida-do-academico-de-viseu-apos-10-anos-de-ligacao-ao-clube/|title=Yuri Araújo deixa Académico de Viseu após oito temporadas no clube|date=26 June 2025|work=Jornal do Centro|language=pt|access-date=26 August 2026}}</ref> Yuri made his professional debut in the [[Segunda Liga]] for Académico de Viseu on 30 August 2015 in a game against [[Clube Oriental de Lisboa|Oriental]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/08/30/portugal/liga-de-honra/academico-viseu-fc/clube-oriental-lisboa/2068693/|title=Game Report by Soccerway|date=30 August 2015}}</ref> During the 2024–25 campaign, he achieved his personal highest goalscoring tally during one season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-betclic/ac--viseu/detalhe/yuri-araujo-atinge-novo-maximo-de-golos?ref=Saber%20Mais_BlocoSaberMais|title=Yuri Araújo atinge novo máximo de golos|date=23 March 2025|work=Record|language=pt|access-date=26 August 2026}}</ref> He left Viseu in 2025 for a career in the [[J.League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diarioviseu.pt/2025/07/13/yuri-araujo-deixou-o-academico-de-viseu-e-vai-agora-jogar-no-japao/|title=Yuri Araújo deixou o Académico de Viseu e vai agora jogar no Japão|date=13 July 2025|work=Diário de Viseu|language=pt|access-date=26 August 2026}}</ref>

It is also Memorial Day. |date=May 27, 2019 |access-date=2024-07-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2r3C3Z-_RDY |title=Steve Hilton Challenges Kamala to Run for California Gov |website=youtube.com |date=May 4, 2025 |access-date=May 4, 2025}}</ref> is an American  right-wing political commentator<ref>{{cite news |url=https://tagesspiegel.de/wirtschaft/fauci-anklagen-twitter-chef-knupft-sich-us-chefvirologen-vor-9015967.html |title='Fauci anklagen': Twitter-Chef knöpft sich US-Chefvirologen vor |work=[[Der Tagesspiegel]] |language=de}}</ref> and [[YouTuber]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://theverge.com/2023/7/13/23794189/twitter-blue-monetization-ad-revenue-sharing-payments |title=Twitter says it will start paying creators this week |last=Sato|first=Mia |work=[[The Verge]] |date=July 13, 2023 |access-date=2023-12-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Benny Johnson's YouTube Statistics |url=https://socialblade.com/youtube/handle/bennyjohnson |access-date=2025-11-21 |website=Social Blade |language=en-US}}</ref> He has contributed to several conservative media outlets such as ''[[Breitbart News]]'', [[Blaze Media|TheBlaze]], ''[[National Review]]'', and ''[[The Daily Caller]]''. Johnson was previously employed with [[BuzzFeed]] but was fired in 2014 due to several instances of [[plagiarism]]. Johnson has also worked for [[Turning Point USA]] and hosted for [[Newsmax TV]].

==Career==
After attending the [[University of Iowa]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dailyiowan.com/2022/09/21/ui-student-arrested-for-disorderly-conduct-disturbing-lawful-assembly-at-event-in-iowa-memorial-union |title=UI student arrested for disorderly conduct, disturbing lawful assembly at event in Iowa Memorial Union |work=Daily Iowan |last=Votzmeyer |first=Colin |date=September 21, 2022 |access-date=July 20, 2024}}</ref> Johnson began contributing opinion pieces to the website [[Breitbart]] in 2010. From 2011 to 2012, Johnson was a full-time employee for conservative website [[TheBlaze]], founded by [[Glenn Beck]].<ref name="wapo">{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/benny-johnson-got-fired-at-buzzfeed-you-will-believe-what-happened-next/2015/06/09/da9fe3f8-e37f-11e4-b510-962fcfabc310_story.html|title=Benny Johnson got fired at BuzzFeed. You will believe what happened next.|last=Terris|first=Ben|date=2015-06-09|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=2017-03-29|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}}</ref> From 2012 to 2014, Johnson was a staff writer at [[BuzzFeed]],<ref>{{cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Betsy |date=2012-12-18 |title=For a Fun Time at D.C. Buzzfeed, Call Benny |url=http://www.adweek.com/digital/for-fun-time-at-d-c-buzzfeed-call-benny/ |accessdate=2017-04-19 |publisher=Ad Week}}</ref> until he was suspended from BuzzFeed when an online investigation exposed plagiarism in his posts. His writings "periodically lifted text from a variety of sources", including ''Yahoo Answers'', Wikipedia, and ''[[U.S. News & World Report]]'', "all without credit".<ref name="fired">{{cite news|last1=Gold|first1=Hadas|last2=Shutt|first2=Jennifer|date=July 26, 2014|url=https://www.politico.com/blogs/media/2014/07/buzzfeed-fires-benny-johnson-for-plagiarism-192886|title=BuzzFeed fires Benny Johnson for plagiarism|work=[[Politico]]|access-date=March 29, 2017}}</ref><ref name="heavy-benny-johnson-suspended-2022">{{Cite web| last = Bucher| first = Chris| title = Benny Johnson Suspended: 5 Fast Facts You Need to Know| work = Heavy Sports| access-date = 2025-02-10| date = 2017-03-21| url = https://heavy.com/news/2017/03/benny-johnson-suspended-ijr-obama-trump-conspiracy-why-buzzfeed-plagiarism/}}</ref> The plagiarized work comprised almost 10 percent of his work; he was subsequently fired from BuzzFeed and apologized for the plagiarism.<ref name="fired" />

[[File:Benny Johnson (12555523704).jpg|thumb|Johnson speaking at the 2014 International Students for Liberty Conference in [[Washington, D.C.]]]]
In September 2014, Johnson became digital director at ''[[National Review]]'' (''NR''). In 2015, Johnson left ''NR'' to join the ''[[Independent Journal Review]]'' (''IJR'') as a creative content contributor.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Gold |first=Hadas |date=3 February 2015 |title=IJReview hires Benny Johnson |work=Politico |url=https://www.politico.com/blogs/media/2015/02/ijreview-hires-benny-johnson-202072 |access-date=2017-03-29}}</ref> A month after his relationship with the ''IJR'' was terminated in October 2017,<ref name="Fischer 2017">{{cite news|url=https://www.axios.com/scoop-benny-johnson-out-at-independent-journal-review-2499102788.html|title=Scoop: Benny Johnson out at Independent Journal Review|last=Fischer|first=Sara |publisher=Axios|date=October 20, 2017|accessdate=October 20, 2017}}</ref> Johnson joined ''[[The Daily Caller]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/media/newsletters/morning-media/2017/11/17/moores-anti-media-campaign-media-deal-frenzy-vanity-fair-panic-wapo-hires-ellison-001382/|title=Moore's anti-media campaign -- Big deal frenzy -- Fixing mass shootings coverage -- Vanity Fair 'panic' -- WaPo expands media desk|first=Michael|last=Calderone|work=Politico|date=2017-11-17|access-date=2017-11-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Nwanevu |first=Osita |date=2017-11-17 |title=Today in Conservative Media: Mike Pence Was Right About Being Alone With Women |url=https://slate.com/news-and-politics/2017/11/today-in-conservative-media-mike-pence-was-right-about-being-alone-with-women.html |access-date=2022-05-08 |website=Slate Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Darcy May 2023">{{cite web |last=Darcy |first=Oliver |author-link=Oliver Darcy |title=Reliable Sources with Oliver Darcy: Tuesday, May 2, 2023 |url=https://view.newsletters.cnn.com/messages/16830831618900b14b13fc586/raw?bt_ee=ZRV3u28jAWCLQjBzWHM5q5MkH6TlkzJRzsU7q8AKW4sSapJMzXTwc9hDaifKmDoDKIgKh6XXLXVXfeRSU6cbgw%3D%3D&bt_ts=1683083161893 |access-date=6 July 2023 |publisher=CNN}}</ref> 

In March 2017, ''IJR'' staffers accused Johnson of plagiarizing an article about then-[[House Republican Conference]] chairwoman [[Cathy McMorris Rodgers]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Mullin |first=Benjamin |date=21 March 2017 |title=Report: Benny Johnson was accused of plagiarism (again) |url=https://www.poynter.org/news/report-benny-johnson-was-accused-plagiarism-again |access-date=2018-10-06 |publisher=Poynter}}</ref> Later in the same month Johnson was suspended by the ''IJR'' after his involvement in an article which asserted that judge [[Derrick Watson]]'s partial blocking of [[Executive Order 13780]] was connected to former president [[Barack Obama]]'s visit to Hawaii. Johnson had been warned that the ''IJR'' could potentially be promoting a conspiracy theory, but assigned the story anyway.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="Darcy">{{Cite news |last=Darcy |first=Oliver |author-link=Oliver Darcy |date=March 21, 2017 |title=Inside the identity crisis at the Independent Journal Review, the outlet that has become a powerhouse in the Trump era |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/independent-journal-review-ijr-identity-trump-2017-3 |accessdate=2020-03-23 |work=[[Business Insider]]}}</ref>

During this time he wrote an article containing the most controversial [[Tweet (social media)|tweet]]s of what he thought was the Boston [[Antifa (United States)|antifa]] [[Twitter]] account, but it was actually a fake account intended to lampoon antifa. Initially an editorial note was added, and the article was later removed.<ref>{{cite news |last=Feldman |first=Brian |date=21 August 2017 |title=How to Spot a Fake Antifa Account |work=Intelligencer |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/2017/08/how-to-spot-a-fake-antifa-account.html |access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Montgomery |first=Blake |date=7 September 2017 |title=Here's A Guide To The Antifa Network That's Trying To Solidify A Nazi-Punching Movement |work=BuzzFeed News |url=https://www.buzzfeednews.com/article/blakemontgomery/antifa-social-media |access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Chiel |first=Ethan |date=22 August 2017 |title=Right Wing Publications Can't Stop Getting Duped By Fake Antifa Accounts |work=GQ |url=https://www.gq.com/story/fake-antifa-accounts |access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref>

In 2019, he became a chief creative officer at [[Turning Point USA]].<ref name="Concha 2019">{{cite web |last=Concha |first=Joe |title=Daily Caller reporter Benny Johnson joining Turning Point USA |website=The Hill |date=2019-02-06 |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/media/428814-daily-caller-reporter-benny-johnson-joining-turning-point-usa |access-date=2019-02-07}}</ref> In 2020, Johnson was a host on [[Newsmax TV]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mediaite.com/tv/newsmaxs-benny-johnson-claims-president-elect-office-is-a-fake-office-made-for-biden-nope-trump-did-it-too/|title=Newsmax's Benny Johnson Claims President-Elect Office Is a 'Fake Office' Made For Biden (Nope, Trump Did It Too)|first=Zachary|last=Petrizzo|publisher=Mediaite|date=2020-11-22|accessdate=2020-12-27}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2020/11/30/939030504/newsmax-rises-on-wave-of-resentment-toward-media-especially-fox-news|title=Newsmax rises on wave of resentment towards media — especially Fox News|first=David|last=Folkenflik|publisher=NPR|date=2020-11-30|accessdate=2020-12-27}}</ref>

In April 2022, ''[[The Verge]]'' published an investigation on Arsenal Media, a conservative boutique co-founded by Johnson. Former employees and contractors described dubious corporate practices, including payments delayed for months, contracts with political campaigns rife with self-dealing, and overworked and underpaid jobs. Johnson has been described as "very abusive, very toxic, screaming at people, like using profanity, vulgarity, making women cry, like pushing them to the edge."<ref>{{Cite web| last = Kelly| first = Makena| title = This firm made Republicans go viral — now it's falling apart| work = The Verge| access-date = 2025-02-10| date = 2022-04-20| url = https://www.theverge.com/2022/4/20/23033650/arsenal-media-group-campaign-marketing-firm-madison-cawthorn-kari-lake-benny-johnson}}</ref>

In August 2024, two Russian state media employees were charged with secretly funding almost $10 million to a Tennessee company for the production of political videos to benefit Russia by influencing the United States. The company's description matches that of [[2024 Tenet Media investigation|Tenet Media]], which had employed Johnson and other right-wing influencers, with him responding that "myself and other influencers were victims in this alleged scheme", with a request being made for him to produce content for a "media startup", and that he had a "standard, arms length deal, which was later terminated."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Suderman |first1=Alan |last2=Swenson |first2=Ali |title=Right-wing influencers were duped to work for covert Russian influence operation, US says |url=https://apnews.com/article/russian-interference-presidential-election-influencers-trump-999435273dd39edf7468c6aa34fad5dd# |access-date=September 5, 2024 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=September 5, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240905023838/https://apnews.com/article/russian-interference-presidential-election-influencers-trump-999435273dd39edf7468c6aa34fad5dd |archive-date=September 5, 2024 |language=en |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=Sarah N. |last2=Goudsward |first2=Andrew |last3=Bing |first3=Christopher |title=US charges employees of Russia's RT network in crackdown on election influence efforts |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-accuse-russia-effort-influence-2024-election-cnn-2024-09-04/ |access-date=September |archive-url=https://archive.today/202409041936/https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-accuse-russia-effort-influence-2024-election-cnn-2024-09-04/ |archive-date=September 4, 2024 |language=en |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2024/09/05/nx-s1-5100829/russia-election-influencers-youtube|title=How Russian operatives covertly hired U.S. influencers to create viral videos|date=September 5, 2024|website=NPR}}</ref><ref>{{cite They’re keeping their millions for now|website=CNN|first1=Jon|last1=Passantino|first2=Sean|last2=Lyngaas|date=September 13, 2024}}</ref>

[[File:AmericaFest 2025 - Benny Johnson 05 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Johnson at [[AmericaFest]] 2025]]
In August 2025, Johnson responded to a [[Truth Social]] post by President [[Donald Trump]] by tweeting a video with the caption: "Here's a [[mass shooting]] and murder in my front lawn, followed by my house being set on fire with my wife and infant child inside." The claim was later proven false; a subsequent profile in ''[[The New York Times]]'', citing police reports and fire department reports, confirmed that the incident had in fact occurred at a neighbor's residence.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news |last=Bensinger |first=Ken |date=Aug 30, 2025 |title=He Plagiarized and Promoted Falsehoods. The White House Embraces Him. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/30/business/media/trump-benny-johnson.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250901001417/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/30/business/media/trump-benny-johnson.html |archive-date=September 1, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref> Johnson had sensationalized details of the episode and falsely presented it as having taken place at his own home.<ref name=":2" />

Following the [[2025 Brown University shooting]], during which Ella Cook, a [[College Republicans]] activist, was killed, Johnson claimed without evidence that Cook was targeted because of her political views. Johnson further shared misinformation falsely identifying a Palestinian [[Brown University]] student as the killer, a theory which was disproven when a different individual, Claudio Neves Valente, was identified as the shooter.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gonzalez-Ramirez|first=Andrea|date=December 15, 2025 |title=MAGA Is Already Spreading Misinformation About the Brown Shooting |url=https://www.thecut.com/article/maga-is-spreading-misinformation-brown-university-shooting.html |work=The Cut|access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Cercone|first=Jeff|date=December 19, 2025 |title=Brown University shooting: Social media users falsely blamed student days before killer was found|url=https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2025/dec/19/social-media/brown-shooting-kharbouch-neves-suspect-false/ |work=[[Politifact]]|access-date=December 19, 2025}}</ref>

In February 2026, Johnson caused further controversy by posting a photo on social media of [[Hillary Clinton]] during her testimony, which representative [[Lauren Boebert]] leaked to him. Boebert's leak of the photo was acknowledged to have violated ethics protocol rules set up by the [[House Oversight and Government Reform Committee]], with a chance of such leaked content being potentially edited with the intent of creating political theatrics.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5757287-hillary-clinton-deposition-boebert-photo/|title=Democrats fume after Boebert leaks deposition photo of Hillary Clinton: 'Clown show'|first=Emily|last=Brooks|publisher=The Hill|date=February 26, 2026|accessdate=February 26, 2026}}</ref><ref name="hillarytestimony">{{cite news|url=https://people.com/hillary-clinton-epstein-deposition-disrupted-lauren-boebert-leaked-photo-11915296|title=Hillary Clinton's Epstein Deposition Disrupted After Lauren Boebert Leaks Photo to MAGA Podcaster|first=Meredith|last=Kile|magazine=People|date=February 26, 2026|accessdate=February 26, 2026}}</ref> As a result, Clinton's testimony was briefly put on hold.<ref name="hillarytestimony" />

Johnson runs three YouTube channels: "Benny Johnson", "Benny On The Block" and "Benny Brews".<ref name="YouTube-1">{{cite web |title=Benny Johnson |url=https://www.youtube.com/@bennyjohnson/about |access-date=May 27, 2025 |website=youtube.com}}</ref> Johnson also hosts a podcast called ''The Benny Show''. His main [[YouTube]] channel, titled "Benny Johnson", has amassed 6.01 million subscribers and 4 billion views as of September 2025.<ref name="YouTube-1" />

==Personal life==
Johnson is married to Katelyn Rieley,<ref name="wapo"/> with whom he has four children as of 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ffcoalition.com/kari-lake-benny-johnson-will-address-faith-freedom-coalitions-road-to-majority-policy-conference-2023/|title=KARI LAKE & BENNY JOHNSON WILL ADDRESS FAITH & FREEDOM COALITION'S "ROAD TO MAJORITY" POLICY CONFERENCE 2023|website=ffcoalition.com|date=June 13, 2023|access-date=July 24, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|user=bennyjohnson|last=Johnson|first=Benny|number=1702776257501360608|title=🚨BOY DAD OFFICIAL🚨 ANNOUNCING Mr. Theodore Johnson.|date=September 15, 2023|access-date=July 24, 2024}}</ref>

On October 10, 2025, Attorney General [[Pam Bondi]] hosted a press conference featuring Johnson and attended by his wife Katelyn, spotlighting the arrest of a man who sent a letter to Johnson's home threatening his life. The arrested individual described in the letter that he hoped for Johnson's "extermination" and that Johnson should be "strangled with an American flag", among other details. Johnson used the press conference to argue that violence, including assassination, has been mainstreamed by the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://abcnews.go.com/US/man-charged-after-allegedly-threatening-wing-podcaster-benny/story?id=126409720|title=Man charged after allegedly threatening right-wing podcaster Benny Johnson|website=[[abcnews.go.com]]|last=Mallin|first=Alexander|date=10 October 2025|accessdate=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/doj-charges-man-letter-threatening-trump-influencer-benny-johnson-rcna236915|title=DOJ charges man with sending threatening letter to pro-Trump influencer Benny Johnson|website=[[NBC News]]|last1=Reilly|first1=Ryan J.|last2=Ebner|first2=Victoria|date=10 October 2025|accessdate=13 October 2025}}</ref>

'''Guilherme António de Souza''', known as '''Alemão''' (born 7 December 1992) is a Brazilian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]], most recently for [[Liga Portugal 2]] club [[Amarante F.C.|Amarante]].

==Club career==
===Tourizense===

Alemão made his league debut for Tourizense against [[C.D. Pinhalnovense|Pinhalnovense]] on 4 September 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2011/09/04/portugal/ii-divisao/gd-tourizense/cd-pinhalnovense/1184258/|title= Tourizense vs Pinhalnovense - 4 September 2011|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club against [[Estrela de Vendas Novas|Estrela Vendas Novas]] on 11 December 2011, scoring in the 16th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2011/12/11/portugal/ii-divisao/gd-tourizense/estrela-de-vendas-novas/1184340/|title= Tourizense vs Estrea Vendas Novas - 11 December 2011|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref>

===Marítimo===

Alemão made his professional debut in the [[Segunda Liga]] for [[C.S. Marítimo B|Marítimo B]] on 31 August 2013 in a game against [[C.D. Feirense|Feirense]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/08/31/portugal/liga-de-honra/cs-maritimo-funchal-ii/cd-feirense/1512246/|title=Game Report by Soccerway|date=31 August 2013}}</ref>

Alemão made his [[Primeira Liga]] debut for [[C.S. Marítimo|Marítimo]] on 4 May 2014 as a late substitute in a 1–1 draw against [[S.C. Braga|Braga]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/05/04/portugal/portuguese-liga-/sporting-braga/maritimo-funchal/1511934/|title=Game Report by Soccerway|date=4 May 2014}}</ref>

===Leixões===

Alemão made his league debut for Leixões against [[S.C. Olhanense|Olhanense]] on 9 August 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/08/09/portugal/liga-de-honra/sc-olhanense/leixoes/1756797/|title= Olhanense vs Leixões - 9 August 2014|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club against [[S.L. Benfica B|Benfica B]] on 1 February 2015, scoring in the 82nd minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/02/01/portugal/liga-de-honra/benfica-b/leixoes/1757365/|title= Benfica II vs Leixões - 1 February 2015|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref>

===Oliveirense===

Alemão made his league debut for Oliveirense against [[UD Sousense|Sousense]] on 21 August 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2016/08/21/portugal/ii-divisao/uniao-desportiva-sousense/ud-oliveirense/2319867/|title= Sousense vs Oliveirense - 21 August 2016|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club against [[C.D. Estarreja|Estarreja]] on 6 November 2016, scoring in the 46th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2016/11/06/portugal/ii-divisao/ud-oliveirense/estarreja/2319906/|title= Oliveirense vs Estarreja - 6 November 2016|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref>

===Ararat-Armenia===

On 23 July 2020, [[FC Ararat-Armenia|Ararat-Armenia]] announced the signing of Alemão.<ref>{{cite web |title=Նոր տրանսֆեր #WelcomeAlemão |url=https://www.facebook.com/araratarmeniafc/photos/a.325603957976435/799689457234547/?type=3&theater |website=facebook.com |publisher=FC Ararat-Armenia Facebook |accessdate=23 July 2020 |language=Armenian |date=23 July 2020}}</ref> He made his league debut for the club against [[FC Ararat Yerevan|Ararat]] on 25 February 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2021/02/25/armenia/premier-league/fc-ararat-yerevan/avan-academy/3340707/|title= Ararat vs Ararat-Armenia - 25 February 2021|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref> Alemão scored his first league goal for the club against Ararat on 15 April 2022, scoring in the 27th minute.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/04/15/armenia/premier-league/avan-academy/fc-ararat-yerevan/3572514/|title= Ararat-Armenia vs Ararat - 15 April 2022|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref>

On 1 June 2024, Ararat-Armenia announced that Alemão had left the club after his contract had expired.<ref>{{cite web |title=Բրազիլացի Ալեմաոյի և "Արարատ-Արմենիա" ֆուտբոլային ակումբի միջև կնքված պայմանագրի ժամկետն ավարտվել է, կողմերը համատեղ որոշում են կայացրել' չերկարաձգել այն։ |url=https://www.facebook.com/photo/?fbid=973174681483316&set=a.536940855106703 |website=facebook.com/araratarmeniafc |publisher=FC Ararat-Armenia Facebook |access-date=1 June 2024 |language=Armenian |date=1 June 2024}}</ref>

===Pyunik===
On 7 July 2024, [[Armenian Premier League]] club [[FC Pyunik|Pyunik]] announced the signing of Alemão.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alemao signs for Pyunik |url=https://fcpyunik.am/en/article/1829 |website=fcpyunik.am |publisher=FC Pyunik |access-date=7 July 2024 |date=7 July 2024}}</ref> On 8 June 2026, Pyunik announced that Alemão had left the club after his contract had expired.<ref>{{cite web |title= We would like to announce that Brazilian defender Alemao has left FC Pyunik following the expiration of his contract with the club |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DZU9m9nFwpD/ |website=instagram.com/pyunik_fc/ |publisher=FC Pyunik Instagram |access-date=8 June 2026 |date=8 June 2026}}</ref>

'''Nia Brodie''' (born '''Coffey''' on June 11, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player with the [[Minnesota Lynx]] of the [[Women's National Basketball Association]] (WNBA). A [[small forward]], she was drafted with the fifth overall pick in the [[2017 WNBA draft]], which is the highest of any [[Northwestern Wildcats women's basketball|Northwestern]] basketball player in school history.<ref name="Thompson">{{cite news |url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/ct-draft-pick-nia-coffey-20170414-story.html |title=WNBA draft pick Nia Coffey (and her puppy) ready to run with the big dogs |last=Thompson |first=Phil |date=April 15, 2017 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=May 6, 2017}}</ref>

Brodie attended [[Hopkins High School]] in [[Minnetonka, Minnesota]] where she was a [[McDonald's All-American]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Armacost |first=Lyndsey |title=Nia Coffey hates to lose, and that's why she never has |url=http://www.insidenu.com/2015/11/2/9658232/nia-coffey-northwestern-profile-feature-winning |access-date=May 7, 2017 |work=[[SB Nation]] |date=November 2, 2015}}</ref>

She is the daughter of former [[NBA]] player, [[Richard Coffey]], and the sister of current NBA player, [[Amir Coffey]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.startribune.com/wnba-draft-pick-nia-coffey-makes-brother-and-gopher-amir-coffey-proud/419448064/ |title=WNBA draft pick Nia Coffey makes brother and Gopher Amir Coffey proud |work=Star Tribune |access-date=August 16, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Brodie entered her first year at Northwestern as the starting [[power forward]]. On November 5, 2013, she made her collegiate debut recording 14 points, 6 rebounds, 4 assists and 2 blocks in a 98–57 win over [[Lewis Flyers|Lewis University]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nusports.com/documents/2013/11/6/stats_20131107aaa.pdf |title=2013 14 box score stats 20131107aaa |website=nusports.com |access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref> At the end of her freshman season she was the first player in Northwestern history to be named first-team all-[[Big Ten]] as a freshman.<ref name="Difference Maker">{{Cite news |url=https://www.northwestern.edu/magazine/spring2017/campuslife/difference-maker-nia-coffey-carries-the-wildcats.html |title=DIFFERENCE MAKER |work=Northwestern |access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>

On January 29, 2015, Brodie registered her career high of 35 points in a 102–99 loss against [[Iowa Hawkeyes women's basketball|Iowa]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/womens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/400596706 |title=No. 20 Iowa women break record for 3s, beat Northwestern |agency=AP|date=January 29, 2015 |access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>

In her junior season, she broke the [[Northwestern Wildcats women's basketball]] record for most rebounds in a season with 344. Which she held until the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nusports.com/sports/womens-basketball/roster/nia-coffey/4931 |title=Nia Coffey |website=nusports.com |access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref> She ended that season as an Honorable Mention for a spot on the WBCA All American Team and on the AP All-American Team.<ref name="Difference Maker"/>

In her senior season, Brodie broke the NU records for most consecutive games scoring in double figures, total rebounds, free throws made, free throw attempts and field goal attempts in a career. She received another Honorable Mention for the AP All American Team.<ref name="record book">{{Cite web |url=https://nusports.com/documents/2021/1/18/2020_21_WBB_Record_Book.pdf |title=2020 21 WBB Record Book |website=nusports.com |access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>

Brodie ended her career as the first Player in NU history to make the All Big Ten First Team (Coaches) in all four years of playing. She also made All Big Ten First Team (Media) in her final three seasons. Brodie led NU in scoring and rebounding for all 4 years of her career.<ref name="record book"/>

==Professional career==

=== WNBA ===

==== San Antonio Stars / Las Vegas Aces ====
On April 13, 2017, Brodie was drafted by the [[San Antonio Stars]] with the 5th pick of the [[2017 WNBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 WNBA draft results |url=https://www.startribune.com/2017-wnba-draft-results/419448834/ |access-date=2024-06-14 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref> This was the highest any NU basketball player had ever been drafted.

She made her debut on May 13, 2017, in the season-opener against the [[New York Liberty]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Liberty 73-64 Stars (May 13, 2017) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/wnba/game/_/gameId/400927392/aces-liberty |access-date=2024-06-14 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

On May 27, 2018, she scored her career high of 23 points in a 98–103 loss against the [[Seattle Storm]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spruill |first=Tamryn |date=2018-05-28 |title=Aces lose to Storm at Mandalay Bay home opener, still win big |url=https://www.swishappeal.com/2018/5/28/17402090/2018-wnba-hoops-happening-basketball-aces-aja-wilson-sparks-chelsea-gray-mystics-kristy-toliver |access-date=2024-06-14 |website=Swish Appeal |language=en}}</ref>

==== Atlanta Dream (first stint) ====
on April 11, 2019, she was traded to the [[Atlanta Dream]] in a three-team trade where the Aces received [[Sugar Rodgers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-04-11 |title=Atlanta Dream Acquire Nia Coffey in Trade – Atlanta Dream |url=https://dream.wnba.com/news/atlanta-dream-acquire-nia-coffey-in-trade/ |access-date=2024-06-14 |website=dream.wnba.com}}</ref>

==== Phoenix Mercury ====
On February 19, 2020, Brodie was traded to the [[Phoenix Mercury]] as part of a three-team trade.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dream.wnba.com/news/dream-acquire-courtney-williams-in-three-team-trade/|title=Dream Acquire Courtney Williams In Three-Team Trade |website=dream.wnba.com |date=February 19, 2019|access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>

On February 10, 2021, Brodie was waived.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spruill |first=Tamryn |date=2021-02-01 |title=Natasha Cloud, Seimone Augustus should be no-brainer signings for any team |url=https://www.swishappeal.com/wnba/2021/2/1/22259629/wnba-rosters-free-agency-dream-sky-sun-wings-fever-aces-sparks-lynx-liberty-mercury-storm-mystics |access-date=2024-06-14 |website=Swish Appeal |language=en}}</ref>

==== Los Angeles Sparks ====
On March 4, 2021, Brodie was signed to the [[Los Angeles Sparks]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sparks.wnba.com/news/sparks-sign-nia-coffey/ |title=Sparks Sign Nia Coffey|website=sparks.wnba.com |date=March 4, 2021|access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>

On June 1, 2021, she recorded a career-high six blocks in a game against the [[Dallas Wings]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nemchock |first=Eric |date=2021-06-08 |title=Coffey, Hines-Allen putting up solid fantasy stat lines at PF position |url=https://www.swishappeal.com/wnba/2021/6/8/22521692/wnba-fantasy-basketball-myisha-hines-allen-nia-coffey-sami-whitcomb-kaila-charles-diamond-deshields |access-date=2024-06-14 |website=Swish Appeal |language=en}}</ref>

That season, Brodie scored a career-high 8.3 PPG and also played a career high in minutes.

==== Atlanta Dream (second stint) ====
On February 1, 2022, Brodie signed a one-year deal with the Dream.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dream.wnba.com/news/dream-bring-back-hayes-coffey-as-key-pieces-to-2022-roster/|title=Dream Bring Back Hayes, Coffey as Key Pieces to 2022 Roster|website=dream.wnba.com |date=February 1, 2022|access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>

On February 1, 2023, Brodie re-signed a second one-year deal with the dream.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dream.wnba.com/news/nia-coffey-and-ad-re-sign-with-atlanta/|title=Nia Coffey and AD Re-Sign with Atlanta|website=dream.wnba.com |date=February 1, 2023|access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>

On February 1, 2024, Brodie re-signed with the dream on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dream.wnba.com/news/atlanta-dream-sign-tina-charles-and-aerial-powers-re-sign-nia-coffey/ |title=Atlanta Dream Sign Tina Charles and Aerial Powers; Re-sign Nia Coffey|website=dream.wnba.com |date=February 1, 2024|access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>

==== Minnesota Lynx ====
On April 12, 2026, Brodie signed with the Minnesota Lynx for the 2026 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://lynx.wnba.com/news/lynx-sign-forward-nia-coffey |title=Lynx Sign Forward Nia Coffey|website=lynx.wnba.com |date=April 12, 2026|access-date=May 8, 2026}}</ref>

=== Overseas ===
Brodie played for Maccabi Ramat Gan of the [[Israeli Female Basketball Premier League]] in the 2017–2018 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nia Coffey joins Maccabi R.Gan |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/495960/Nia-Coffey-joins-Maccabi-R.Gan |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=eurobasket.com}}</ref>

Brodie played for the [[Adelaide Lightning]] of the [[Women's National Basketball League]] (WNBL) in the [[2018–19 WNBL season]].<ref>{{Cite news |last= |date=2018-05-21 |title=Lightning inject WNBA talent into their 2018-19 roster - Adelaide Lightning |url=https://wnbl.basketball/adelaide/news/lightning-inject-wnba-talent-into-their-2018-19-roster/ |access-date=2025-01-31 |work=Adelaide Lightning |language=en-US}}</ref>

Brodie joined [[Arka Gdynia (women's basketball)|Arka Gdynia]] of the [[Basket Liga Kobiet]] in February 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-02-15 |title=Amerykanka Nia Coffey wzmocni Arkę Gdynia. Mecze trójmiejskich koszykarek |url=https://www.trojmiasto.pl/sport/Amerykanka-Nia-Coffey-wzmocni-Arke-Gdynia-Mecz-trojmiejskich-koszykarek-n131891.html |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=trojmiasto.pl |language=pl}}</ref>

Brodie played for [[Çukurova Basketbol]] of the [[Women's Basketball Super League]] from October to November 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nia Coffey agreed terms with Cukurova |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/592553/Nia-Coffey-agreed-terms-with-Cukurova |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=eurobasket.com}}</ref>

In January 2021, Brodie signed with Maccabi Haifa of the Israeli Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nia Coffey joins M.Haifa |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/662538/Nia-Coffey-joins-M.Haifa |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=eurobasket.com}}</ref>

Brodie played for [[Flammes Carolo Basket Ardennes]] of the [[Ligue Féminine de Basketball]] in the 2021–2022 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nia Coffey joins Flammes |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/686279/Nia-Coffey-joins-Flammes |access-date=2025-01-31 |website=eurobasket.com}}</ref>

In January 2025, Brodie signed with the [[Townsville Fire]] of the WNBL.<ref>{{Cite news |last= |date=2025-01-05 |title=Townsville Fire Sign WNBA Star Nia Coffey for Remainder of WNBL Season - Townsville Fire |url=https://wnbl.basketball/townsville/news/townsville-fire-sign-wnba-star-nia-coffey-for-remainder-of-wnbl-season/ |access-date=2025-01-31 |work=Townsville Fire |language=en-US}}</ref>

==National career==
Brodie played for Team USA in the 2013 FIBA Under-19 World Championship for Women. She broke the Team USA record for most free throws without a miss in the U19 tournament with 11.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.usab.com/about/competitive-history-stats#5x5womensteam |title=5x5 Women's U19 World Cup History |website=usab.com |access-date=June 8, 2024}}</ref>
