'''Bobbi Salvör Menuez''' (born 1993) is an American actor and model. They have appeared in films including ''[[Something in the Air (2012 film)|Something in the Air]]'', ''[[The Breakup Girl]]'', and ''[[White Girl (2016 film)|White Girl]]'', and in the [[Amazon Prime Video]] series ''[[I Love Dick (TV series)|I Love Dick]]''.<ref name="Oyster1"/> They have been a [[curator]] at [[MoMA PS1]].<ref name="Oyster1">{{cite magazine |author=Ganley |first=Yasmine |date=November 24, 2016 |title=[Bobbi] Menuez On The Power Of Art |url=http://www.oystermag.com/2016/11/india-menuez-on-the-power-of-art-for-oyster-109/ |accessdate=May 7, 2017 |magazine=[[Oyster (magazine)|Oyster]] |issue=109}}</ref>

==Early life==
Menuez was born in [[Park Slope]], New York City in 1993.<ref name="intmag">{{cite news |date=June 16, 2015 |title=[Bobbi] Salvör Menuez |url=https://www.interviewmagazine.com/art/india-salvor-menuez |accessdate=September 17, 2019 |work=Interview Magazine}}</ref><ref name="lyc">{{cite web |title=India Salvör Menuez |url=https://www.luckyoucollective.com/indiamenuez |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190126043746/https://www.luckyoucollective.com/indiamenuez |archive-date=January 26, 2019 |publisher=Luck You Collective}}</ref> They founded the Luck You artist collective in high school.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Messinger |first=Kate |date=2016-05-17 |title=[Bobbi] Menuez: Act[or], Model, Artist and One of the Most Crucial Links In NYC's Young Creative Community |url=https://www.papermag.com/india-menuez-artist-actress-model-1803753663.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210428205053/https://www.papermag.com/india-menuez-artist-actress-model-1803753663.html |archive-date=2021-04-28 |access-date= |work=PAPER |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Vice1">{{cite web |author=Rory |first=Satran |date=June 20, 2014 |title=Founder of the Luck You Collective, [Bobbi] Salvor Menuez, Thinks [They're] a Witch |url=https://i-d.co/article/founder-of-the-luck-you-collective-india-salvor-menuez-thinks-shes-a-witch/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151129145109/http://i-d.vice.com/en_us/article/founder-of-the-luck-you-collective-india-salvor-menuez-thinks-shes-a-witch |archive-date=November 29, 2015 |access-date=May 7, 2017 |work=[[Vice News]]}}</ref>

==Career==
{{expand section|date=November 2025}}
Menuez starred in a fashion editorial for ''[[Harper's Bazaar]]'' in 2014. The same year, they acted in the film ''Uncertain Terms''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bobbi Salvör Menuez - Actor, Model |url=https://www.tvinsider.com/people/bobbi-salvor-menuez/ |access-date=2025-06-06 |website=TV Insider |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2016, Menuez acted in the film ''[[White Girl (2016 film)|White Girl]]'', three episodes of ''[[Transparent (TV series)|Transparent]]'', and in a recurring role on ''[[I Love Dick (TV series)|I Love Dick]]''.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Oyster1" /> They also modeled for [[Miu Miu]] and [[New York Fashion Week]] and organized a performance art project at the [[MoMA PS1]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Oyster1" /> 

In 2019, they played Gillian in the comedy drama film ''[[Adam (2019 American film)|Adam]]''.<ref name="VF" /> They also acted in one episode of ''[[Euphoria (American TV series)|Euphoria]]''.

Menuez played the primary roles in the music videos for two Leonard Cohen songs published after his death.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bloom |first=Madison |date=2021-11-05 |title=Watch a New Video for Leonard Cohen’s “Puppets” |url=https://pitchfork.com/news/watch-a-new-video-for-leonard-cohens-puppets/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=Pitchfork |language=en-US}}</ref> In "Happens to the Heart" (2019), Menuez walks through a forest while dressed like Cohen, eventually putting on the clothes of a Zen monk and meditating.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Jim |date=2019-11-18 |title=On 'Thanks For The Dance,' Leonard Cohen Gets A Little Help From His Friends |url=https://www.wbur.org/news/2019/11/18/thanks-for-the-dance-leonard-cohen-album |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=www.wbur.org |language=en}}</ref> In "Puppets" (2021), Menuez walks down a city street dressed like Cohen, eventually setting themselves on fire.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ehrlich |first=Brenna |date=2021-11-05 |title=A Mysterious Figure Self-Immolates in the Video for Leonard Cohen's 'Puppets' |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/leonard-cohen-puppets-video-1253331/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2023, they co-starred with [[Amandla Stenberg]] in [[Jacqueline Castel]]'s [[My Animal (film)|''My Animal'']], which had its world premiere at the [[2023 Sundance Film Festival]], on January 22, 2023, in the Midnight section.<ref>{{cite web |last=Anderson |first=Derek |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Sundance Film Festival 2023 Midnight Category Includes Brandon Cronenberg's INFINITY POOL and Kenneth Dagatan's IN MY MOTHER'S SKIN |url=https://dailydead.com/sundance-film-festival-2023-midnight-category-includes-brandon-cronenbergs-infinity-pool-and-kenneth-dagatans-in-my-mothers-skin/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129173137/https://dailydead.com/sundance-film-festival-2023-midnight-category-includes-brandon-cronenbergs-infinity-pool-and-kenneth-dagatans-in-my-mothers-skin/ |archive-date=January 29, 2023 |accessdate=January 30, 2023 |work=Daily Dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Kay |first=Jeremy |date=December 8, 2022 |title=Sundance unveils 2023 line-up |url=https://www.screendaily.com/news/sundance-unveils-2023-line-up/5177239.article |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316072638/https://www.screendaily.com/news/sundance-unveils-2023-line-up/5177239.article |archive-date=March 16, 2023 |accessdate=January 30, 2023 |work=[[Screen International]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In January 2019, they announced on social media that they would be using the name Bobbi, a name they had been using privately for over a year prior to the announcement. Menuez is queer, [[Transgender|trans]], and [[non-binary]], and uses ''they/them'' pronouns.<ref name="VF">{{cite magazine | url=https://www.vanityfair.com/style/2019/01/bobbi-salvor-menuez-adam-name-interview | title= Bobbi Salvör Menuez's Buzz Cut Is a Work of Art |first=Laura|last=Regensdorf|magazine=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] | date=January 30, 2019 | accessdate=March 7, 2019 }}</ref> They married artist Quori Theodor in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andrews |first=Arden Fanning |date=2024-08-19 |title=Bobbi Salvör Menuez and Quori Theodor's "Forest Rave" Wedding Was a Celebration of Community |url=https://www.vogue.com/slideshow/bobbi-menuez-and-quori-theodor-wedding |access-date=2025-06-06 |website=Vogue |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''José Lucas Caetano da Silva''' (born 7 March 1994), commonly known as '''Zé Lucas''', is a Brazilian [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for Dutch club {{ill|VV Prinsenland|nl}}.

==Club career==
Zé Lucas started his career with [[Paraná Soccer Technical Center|PSTC]] of his hometown,<ref name="Mielec Interview">{{cite web|url=http://stalmielec.com/?p=26913 |title=Zé Lucas: Stać nas na sprawienie niespodzianki |date=22 July 2016 |access-date=13 May 2017 |work=Stal Mielec |language=pl}}</ref> before moving to [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] in 2012. In his first year with the [[Laranjeiras]]-based side, he scored the winning goal against [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] to win the youth version of the [[Taça Guanabara]]. He was also top scorer in the whole state of [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/fluminense/noticia/2013/03/heroi-nos-juniores-ze-lucas-festeja-primeiro-titulo-no-flu-indescritivel.html |title=Herói nos juniores, Zé Lucas festeja primeiro título no Flu: 'Indescritível' |date=10 March 2013 |access-date=13 May 2017 |work=Globo Esporte |language=pt}}</ref>

He was loaned to Botafogo in 2014, and spent the whole year with the club's youth team. He went to [[United States|America]] in 2015 to study at university and improve his English, however he was rejected a scholarship as he had already played professionally.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jornalnossodia.com.br/?id=162-22599 |title=Desafio no Gelo - 'Toca no Zé Lucas que é gol' |date=25 August 2016 |access-date=13 May 2017 |work=Nosso Esporte |language=pt}}</ref> As a result of this, he remained with Fluminense, and joined Slovak side [[FC ŠTK 1914 Šamorín|Šamorín]] on loan in 2016, and scored 6 goals as they won the [[3. Liga (Slovakia)#West division|3. Liga]].<ref name="Mielec Interview"/>

Following Fluminense's affiliate link with [[Stal Mielec]] in 2015, Zé Lucas was announced to have permanently joined the Polish side.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stalmielec.com/?p=26437 |title=FKS Stal Mielec oficjalnie rozpoczęła współpracę z brazylijskim Fluminense FC! |date=6 July 2015 |access-date=13 May 2017 |work=Stal Mielec |language=pl}}</ref> He made his debut in a [[2016–17 Polish Cup|Polish Cup]] game against [[Chojniczanka Chojnice]], playing 90 minutes in a 0–2 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stalmielec.com/?p=27780 |title=Ze Lucas: Czuję ulgę, że debiut już za mną |date=12 August 2016 |access-date=13 May 2017 |work=Stal Mielec |language=pl}}</ref>

After two [[I liga|league]] appearances, Zé Lucas returned to Brazil to join [[Campeonato Paulista Segunda Divisão]] side [[Associação Atlética Itararé|Itararé]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.90minut.pl/news/276/news2765308-Ze-Lucas-w-AA-Itarare.html |title=Zé Lucas w AA Itararé |date=9 April 2017 |access-date=13 May 2017 |work=90minut |language=pl}}</ref>

[[Heinz Award]] (2019) }} '''Amanda Ngọc Nguyễn''' (born Oct 1991) is a [[Vietnamese Americans|Vietnamese-American]] social entrepreneur, civil rights activist, and commercial astronaut. In 2014 she founded [[Rise (non-governmental organization)|Rise]], a non-governmental civil rights organization that works to implement a sexual assault survivors' bill of rights. She drafted the [[Sexual Assault Survivors' Rights Act]], a bill that passed unanimously through [[United States Congress|the United States Congress]]. She has also been credited with kickstarting the movement to stop violence against [[Asian Americans]], after her video calling for media coverage went viral in February 2021. In recognition of her work, Nguyen was nominated for the 2019 [[Nobel Peace Prize]] and was named one of the 2022 ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' Women of the Year. She has received several awards, and was credited as a Top 100 Global Thinker by [[Foreign Policy]]. Her memoir, ''Saving Five'', was published in March 2025 and debuted on [[The New York Times Best Seller list|''The New York Times'' Best Seller list]]. Nguyen flew aboard [[Blue Origin]]'s 11th spaceflight under the [[New Shepard]] program. The [[Blue Origin NS-31]] [[sub-orbital]] spaceflight took place on April 14, 2025, making Nguyen the first woman of Vietnamese heritage to fly into space. During the flight, Nguyen conducted scientific experiments, including one related to [[wound dressing]] in [[microgravity]]. ==Early life and education== Amanda Ngọc Nguyễn was born in 1991,{{cite magazine|url=https://www.bustle.com/articles/201015-who-is-amanda-nguyen-the-young-womens-honoree-worked-with-president-obama-to-protect-american-women|magazine=[[Bustle (magazine)|Bustle]]|title=Who Is Amanda Nguyen? The Young Women's Honoree Worked With President Obama To Protect American Women|date=December 20, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017}} in [[California]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thecut.com/2016/10/amanda-nguyen-and-the-sexual-assault-survivors-bill-of-rights.html|work=[[thecut.com|Cut]]|title=This Rape Survivor Just Helped Get a Huge Bill Passed Through the House|date=October 28, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017}} She is the daughter of [[Vietnamese boat people]] who migrated to the United States after the [[Vietnam War]].{{cite web | last=Curry | first=Alicia | title=Amanda Nguyen: Blue Origin astronaut reveals depression after space flight backlash | website=[[BBC News]] | date=30 December 2025 | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd0k0939dd3o | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251231010443/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd0k0939dd3o | archive-date=31 December 2025 | url-status=live | access-date=31 December 2025}} She graduated from [[Centennial High School (Corona, California)|Centennial High School]] of [[Corona, California]] in 2009 and earned a [[Bachelor of Arts]] at [[Harvard University]] in 2013.{{cite web| title = Centennial Alumni, Amanda Nguyen, Named TIME 2022 Women of the Year.|url = https://www.cnusd.k12.ca.us/c_n_u_s_d_c_o_n_n_e_c_t_i_o_n/womenoftheyear |access-date = April 17, 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2016/1/19/sexual-assault-bill-of-rights/|newspaper=[[The Harvard Crimson]]|title=Students Help Draft Sexual Assault Legislation|date=January 19, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017}}{{cite magazine|url=https://www.forbes.com/profile/amanda-nguyen/|magazine=[[Forbes]]|title=Amanda Nguyen|access-date=June 22, 2017}}{{cite web |title=Amanda Nguyen - After serving as the Deputy White House Liaison for the [[United States Department of State|U.S. Department of State]], Nguyen left to work full-time at advocacy organisation Rise in 2016, which she co-founded. web|url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/woman-behind-sexual-assault-survivor-bill-rights|publisher=[[PBS]]|title=The woman behind the sexual-assault survivor 'bill of rights'|date=October 28, years.{{cite web|url=http://www.rollcall.com/news/politics/president-obama-signs-sexual-assault-bill-of-rights|work=[[Roll Call]]|title=How One Victim's Fight Got Sexual Assault Bill to Obama|date=October 7, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017|archive-date=October 8, Rights|date=September 7, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017}} After police officers informed her there was a 15-year [[statute of limitations]] for rape in [[Massachusetts]], she decided she would press charges at a later date when she was ready.{{cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/2016/09/09/493228724/obama-expected-to-sign-sexual-assault-survivors-bill-of-rights-into-law|publisher=[[NPR]]|title=Obama Expected To Sign Sexual Assault Survivors' Bill Of Rights Into Law|date=September 9, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017}} She had a [[rape kit]] performed and discovered that, if she did not report the crime to law enforcement, her rape kit would be destroyed after six months if an extension request was not filed.{{cite news|url=https://www.csmonitor.com/USA/Justice/2016/0321/To-combat-rape-a-bill-of-rights-for-survivors|newspaper=[[The Christian Science Monitor]]|title=To combat rape, a 'bill of rights' for survivors|date=March 21, 2016|access-date=June 22, 2017}} She was also not given official instructions on how to file for an extension. Nguyen considered this system to be broken, partially because the extension request would be an unnecessary reminder of a traumatizing experience. Nguyen met other survivors with similar stories and concluded that the current legal protections were insufficient. === Rise === {{main|Rise (non-governmental organization)}} In November 2014,{{cite web|url=http://www.takepart.com/article/2016/02/28/bill-rights-sexual-assault-survivors|publisher=[[TakePart]]|title=Do We Need a Bill of Rights for Sexual-Assault Survivors?|date=February 28, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017|archive-date=February 29, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160229095019/http://www.takepart.com/article/2016/02/28/bill-rights-sexual-assault-survivors}} Nguyen founded [[Rise (non-governmental organization)|Rise]], a [[nonprofit organisation]] which is aimed to protect the [[civil rights]] of sexual assault and rape survivors.{{cite news|url=http://nytlive.nytimes.com/womenintheworld/2016/02/04/amanda-nguyen-is-taking-the-fight-for-sexual-violence-survivors-civil-rights-all-the-way-to-the-white-house/|newspaper=The New York Times|title=Navigating the broken system was worse than the rape itself|date=February 4, 2016|access-date=June 22, 2017|archive-date=June 27, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170627071022/http://nytlive.nytimes.com/womenintheworld/2016/02/04/amanda-nguyen-is-taking-the-fight-for-sexual-violence-survivors-civil-rights-all-the-way-to-the-white-house/}} Nguyen headed the organization in her spare time{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/society/2016/feb/23/sexual-assault-survivors-rape-kits-us-senate-bill-white-house|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|title=Meet the 24-year-old who could change how the US handles sexual assaults|date=February 23, 2016|access-date=June 22, 2017}}{{cite magazine|url=https://people.com/celebrity/amanda-nguyen-and-rise-profile-passing-sexual-assault-bill-of-rights/|magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]]|title=How a 24-Year-Old Rape Survivor Is Pushing Congress to Change the Way the U.S. Handles Sexual Assault|date=August 30, 2016|access-date=June 22, 2017}} until September 2016. Everyone who works with Rise is a volunteer,{{cite news|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/magazine/2016/04/07/rape-survivors-have-fewer-rights-than-you-think-amanda-nguyen-trying-change-that/7E0yCoVoPBB1DrpnIO2API/story.html|newspaper=[[The Boston Globe]]|title=Rape survivors have fewer rights than you'd think. Amanda Nguyen is trying to change that.|date=April 7, 2016|access-date=June 22, 2017}} and the organization has raised money through [[GoFundMe]]. Nguyen explained that the organization was named Rise to "remind us that a small group of thoughtful, committed citizens can rise and change the world".{{cite web |title=Risers |url=http://www.risenow.us/risers/ |website=RiseNow |publisher=Rise |access-date=November 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181113143723/http://www.risenow.us/risers/ |archive-date=November 13, 2018 }} Nguyen's aim is for Rise to pass a Sexual Assault Survivor Bill of Rights in all 50 U.S. states as well as on the national level. She has also traveled to [[Japan]] where a similar bill was presented.{{cite news|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2016/10/25/sex-assault-bill-author-currier/|newspaper=[[The Harvard Crimson]]|title=Sexual Assault Bill Author Encourages Youth Activism|date=October 25, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017}} ===Sexual Assault Survivors' Rights Act=== {{Main|Sexual Assault Survivors' Rights Act}} In July 2015, Nguyen met with US Senator [[Jeanne Shaheen]] from [[New Hampshire]] to discuss legislation that would protect survivor rights on the federal level. Legislation that Nguyen had helped draft was introduced to [[United States Congress|Congress]] in February 2016 by Shaheen. Nguyen collaborated with [[Change.org]] and comedy website [[Funny or Die]] to draw attention to the legislation and encourage voters to support it.{{cite magazine|url=https://fortune.com/2016/02/25/funny-or-die-sexual-assault/|magazine=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]|title=Here's What a Bunch of 'Supervillains' Think About U.S. Sexual Assault Laws|date=February 26, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017}} Nguyen launched a Change.org petition that called on Congress to pass the legislation. The Funny or Die video and Change.org petition received support from [[Judd Apatow]] and [[Patricia Arquette]] on [[Twitter]]. As of February 28, 2016, the Change.org petition gained 60,000 of the 75,000 requested signatures. By October 2016, there were more than 100,000 signatures.{{cite web|url=http://www.refinery29.com/2016/05/111776/senate-passes-sexual-assault-survivors-bill-of-rights|publisher=[[Refinery29]]|title=Obama Just Signed The Sexual Assault Survivors' Bill Of Rights|date=October 8, 2016|access-date=June 27, 2017}} The bill passed through the [[United States Senate|Senate]] in May and the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] in September. It passed unanimously in both chambers of [[United States Congress|Congress]],{{Cite web |last=General |first=Ryan |date=2018-07-05 |title=Woman Who Drafted 'Sexual Assault Survivor's Bill of Rights' Nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize |url=https://nextshark.com/sexual-assault-bill-nobel-peace-prize |access-date=2024-08-23 |website=NextShark |language=en}}{{Cite web|url=https://belatina.com/rise-amanda-nguyen-force-behind-the-sexual-assault-survivors-rights-act/|title=All Rise for Amanda Nguyen: The Force Behind the Sexual Assault Survivors' Rights Act|last=Nahmad|first=Erica|date=January 29, 2019|website=BeLatina|access-date=November 21, 2019}}{{Cite news |last=Huetteman |first=Emmarie |date=2016-05-25 |title=Advocates Praise Senate Bill on Sexual Assault Victims' Rights |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/25/us/politics/advocates-praise-senate-bill-on-sexual-assault-victims-rights.html |access-date=2024-08-23 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} and was signed into law in October 2016 by [[President of the United States|President]] [[Barack Obama]]. The law protects, among other rights, the right to have the evidence of a rape kit preserved without charge for the duration of the statute of limitations. On October 12, 2017, California governor [[Jerry Brown]] approved a bill titled "Sexual assault victims: rights".{{Cite web|url=http://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=201720180AB1312|title=Bill Text - AB-1312 Sexual assault victims: rights.|website=leginfo.legislature.ca.gov|access-date=September 20, 2018}} ===Other advocacy=== Nguyen has been credited with kickstarting the movement to stop violence against [[Asian Americans]], after her video calling for media coverage went viral on February 5, 2021.{{Cite web|last=Liu|first=Jennifer|date=March 1, 2021|title=How millennial Nobel Prize nominee Amanda Nguyen's viral video sparked coverage of anti-Asian racism|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/03/01/amanda-nguyens-viral-video-raises-awareness-of-anti-asian-racism.html|access-date=April 20, 2021|website=CNBC}}{{Cite magazine|title=Why More Policing Isn't the Answer to a Rise in Anti-Asian Hate Crimes|url=https://time.com/5938482/asian-american-attacks/|access-date=April 20, 2021|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]}} Nguyen had previously spoken out against racism against Asian Americans in the United States. In July 2018, in a now deleted [[Instagram]] post, Nguyen alleged that [[Neiman Marcus]] had refused to sell her the dress she wore to announce her [[Nobel Peace Prize]] nomination due to her race. She wrote, "When I went to buy it at Neiman Marcus they refused to let me buy it. When I asked why, they said they didn’t take cards like mine. (It’s a MasterCard)." She continued, "Neiman Marcus didn’t think that someone who looks like me could afford a dress like that (...) For so many marginalized members of our community, it does not matter how much money we make or how successful we can be – one can be nominated for a Nobel and still experience this racism, sexism, '''Henrique Chagas Moniz de Aragão Gonzaga''' (born 30 April 1993), also credited as '''Henry Zaga''', is a Brazilian actor.

==Early life==

Henrique Zaga was born in Brasília, Brazil's capital city. He is of Afro and Native [[Brazilians|Brazilian]] descent through his mother and Euro Brazillian descent through his father.  

Zaga moved to Los Angeles to pursuit his acting career.

==Career==
Zaga gained recognition early in his career, when he was cast as [[List of Teen Wolf (2011 TV series) secondary characters#Josh Diaz|Josh Diaz]] in the [[MTV]] series ''[[Teen Wolf (2011 TV series)|Teen Wolf]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.correiobraziliense.com.br/app/noticia/diversao-e-arte/2015/05/20/interna_diversao_arte,483739/ator-brasiliense-henry-zaga-integra-nova-temporada-do-seriado-teen-wol.shtml|title=Ator brasiliense Henry Zaga integra nova temporada do seriado 'Teen wolf'|last=Ponce de Leon|first=Diego|website=Correio Braziliense|date=20 May 2015|access-date=27 June 2017|language=pt}}</ref> Gonzaga later appeared in the [[Netflix]] film ''[[XOXO (2016 film)|XOXO]]'', and the series ''[[13 Reasons Why]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.romper.com/p/who-is-brad-on-13-reasons-why-henry-zaga-plays-the-new-character-46664|title=Who Is Brad on ''13 Reasons Why''? Henry Zaga Plays the New Character|last=Jamal|first=Zakiya|website=Romper|date=31 March 2017 |access-date=27 June 2017}}</ref>

In April 2017, he was cast as [[Marvel superhero]] [[Sunspot (Marvel Comics)|Roberto da Costa / Sunspot]] in the [[20th Century Studios|20th Century Fox]] X-Men spin-off film, ''[[The New Mutants (film)|The New Mutants]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2017/film/news/henry-zaga-new-mutants-sunspot-13-reasons-why-1202450778/ |title=''13 Reasons Why'' Actor Henry Zaga to Play Sunspot in ''New Mutants'' |last=Kroll |first=Justin |website=Variety |date=1 June 2017 |access-date=2 July 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://deadline.com/2017/06/new-mutants-henry-zaga-sunsspot-x-men-spinoff-1202106025/ |title=''New Mutants'': Henry Zaga Set to Play Sunspot in ''X-Men'' Spinoff |last=N'Duka |first=Amanda |website=Deadline |date=1 June 2017 |access-date=11 March 2019}}</ref>

On 12 November 2021, it was announced that Zaga would star in the Netflix [[romantic comedy]] film ''Beyond the Universe'' alongside [[Giulia Be]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kroll |first=Justin |date=12 November 2021 |title=Henry Zaga and Giulia Be to Star in Netflix Pic ''Beyond the Universe'' |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |url=https://deadline.com/2021/11/henry-zaga-giulia-be-beyond-the-universe-1234872488/ |access-date=22 November 2023}}</ref> The film was released on 27 October 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |title=''Beyond the Universe'' |work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/beyond_the_universe_2022 |access-date=22 November 2023}}</ref>

In April 2024, it was announced that Zaga had joined the cast of ''[[Warfare (film)|Warfare]]'', a war film written and directed by Ray Mendoza and [[Alex Garland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/04/michael-gandolfini-noah-centineo-henrique-zaga-taylor-john-smith-aidan-bradley-evan-holtzman-ray-mendoza-alex-garlands-warfare-a24-1235880092/|title=Noah Centineo, Michael Gandolfini, Henrique Zaga, Taylor John Smith, Adain Bradley And Evan Holtzman Join Ray Mendoza And Alex Garland's 'Warfare' At A24|first=Justin|last=Kroll|date=10 April 2024}}</ref>

'''Robert James Rallison''' (born May 14, 1996), known online as '''TheOdd1sOut''', is an American [[YouTuber]], cartoonist, animator, author, and voice actor. He is best known for producing [[storytelling|story-time]] [[animations]] on his [[YouTube channel]], which, {{As of|2026|08|post=,|lc=y}} has 20.8 million subscribers and 5.86 billion views. He is also the co-creator and executive producer of the [[Netflix]] animated series ''[[Oddballs (TV series)|Oddballs]]'' (2022–2023), on which he voiced the main character James.

== Early and personal life ==
Robert James Rallison<ref name="T10">{{Cite web|last=Dodgson|first=Lindsay|title=These were the top 10 trending videos on YouTube in 2019|url=https://www.insider.com/top-10-trending-videos-on-youtube-2019-12|access-date=2021-04-20|website=Insider|language=en-US}}</ref> was born in [[Chandler, Arizona]],<ref name="Places of residence">{{Cite web|last=Waltz|first=Adam|date=2018-11-19|title=Chandler Native Finds Success as 'TheOdd1sOut' on YouTube|url=https://kasw.ewscloud.com/positivelyarizona/chandler-native-finds-success-as-theodd1sout-on-youtube/|access-date=2019-11-10|website=YourPHX|archive-date=March 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200309152359/https://kasw.ewscloud.com/positivelyarizona/chandler-native-finds-success-as-theodd1sout-on-youtube/|url-status=dead}}</ref> on May 14, 1996,<ref name="birthday">{{Cite tweet|number=598912380504903680|user=theodd1sout|title=Happy Birthday (to me)|access-date=2022-09-08}}</ref> to a [[Mormon]] family.<ref name=Padilla2021>{{cite interview |last=Rallison |first=James |interviewer=[[Anthony Padilla]] |title=I spent a day with THEODD1sOUT |date=November 12, 2021 |publisher=YouTube |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3pbzyOU7nUM&t=267s |access-date=October 3, 2023}}</ref> His mother is author [[Janette Rallison]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://janetterallison.com/blog/answering-three-questions-about-becoming-a-writer/#comment-246948 |title=Answering three questions about becoming a writer |date=2018-07-18 |website=Janette Rallison & CJ Hill Books |language=en-US |access-date=2022-09-19}}</ref> Rallison is no longer Mormon and never had a desire to go on a mission.<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3pbzyOU7nUM |title=I spent a day with THEODD1sOUT |date=2021-11-12 |last=AnthonyPadilla |access-date=2024-08-10 |via=YouTube}}</ref> He has a twin sister, Faith,<ref>{{Cite AV media|last=Rallison |first=Robert |publisher=TheOdd2sOut |title=Mario Maker Part 2 Ft. My Sister |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qLT8yvyja94 |website=[[YouTube]] |type=[[Video]] |date=2018-11-16 |access-date=2022-09-19}}</ref> and three other siblings: Luke,<ref>{{Cite AV media|last=Rallison |first=Robert |publisher=TheOdd1sOut |title=My Mom's Cruel and Unusual Punishments |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xBkp9fslQE |website=[[YouTube]] |type=[[Video]] |date=2018-03-26 |access-date=2022-09-19}}</ref> Kate,{{Citation needed|date=September 2022}} and Arianna.<ref>{{Cite AV media|last=Rallison |first=Robert |publisher=TheOdd1sOut |title=My Mom's Cruel and Unusual Punishments |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=rvUzuK0ygI4 |website=[[YouTube]] |type=[[Video]] |date=2018-10-05 |access-date=2022-09-20}}</ref>

He attended [[Perry High School (Gilbert, Arizona)|Perry High School]] in [[Gilbert, Arizona]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Del Fosse|first=Sawyer|date=2016-09-29|title=James Rallison: Alumni taking self-made illustrative success to the internet|url=https://phsprecedent.com/entertainment/2016/09/29/james-rallison-alumni-taking-self-made-illustrative-success-to-the-internet/|access-date=2021-01-31|website=The Precedent}}</ref> In 2018, Rallison moved to [[Glendale, California]].<ref name="Places of residence" />

==Career==
===Webcomics===
Rallison's first published illustrated works were [[webcomics]], under the title ''TheOdd1sOut''. He uploaded the first comic strip onto [[Tumblr]] in June 2012, when he was 16.<ref name="auto" /> After 100 comics, he had amassed 100 followers, and it took him about a year to settle into his art style.<ref name="auto">{{Cite news|last=Cappello|first=Nile|date=2018-06-11|title=James Rallison on TheOdd1sOut Comics, Animations & New Book|work=Crixeo|url=https://crixeo.com/theodd1sout-comics/|url-status=dead|access-date=2018-11-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180707020123/https://crixeo.com/theodd1sout-comics/|archive-date=2018-07-07}}</ref> By September 2016 he had written around 400 strips. Rallison described the characters in his comics as "marshmallow people" because of their white, roundish look. His comics tended to focus on lighthearted themes, such as taking famous puns literally, or poking fun at social clichés.<ref name=":1" />

===YouTube===
On August 30, 2014, just over two years after starting his webcomic, Rallison started his YouTube channel as ''theodd1sout comic''. In his animated videos, which feature the same "marshmallow people" as the webcomic,<ref name=":1" /> he talks about his life story, his thoughts, and opinions. His first video was titled "A Book I Made as a Kid", looking at a short story he made while in elementary school.<ref name="Places of residence" /> In March 2016, his channel reached 100,000{{nbsp}}subscribers.<ref>{{Cite AV media|last=Rallison |first=Robert |publisher=TheOdd1sOut |title=100,000 Sprinkles on a Cake (not really) (100,000 Subscriber Special!) |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=hb1SJpliZkQ |website=[[YouTube]] |type=[[Video]] |date=2016-03-15 |access-date=2022-09-25}}</ref><ref>{{Cite tweet|last=Rallison |first=Robert |user=theodd1sout |number=709809880622706689 |title=100,000 subscriber special video is up! I put 100,000 sprinkles (rounded up) on a cake! THANKS, YOU GUYS! |access-date=2022-09-25}}</ref> In April 2016, his channel gained over 278,000{{nbsp}}subscribers, giving him a total of over 400,000{{nbsp}}subscribers.<ref>{{cite web|author=Cohen, Joshua|date=2016-05-20|title=Top 100 Most Subscribed YouTube Channels Worldwide • April 2016|url=http://www.tubefilter.com/2016/05/20/top-100-most-subscribed-youtube-channels-worldwide-april-2016/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905183404/http://www.tubefilter.com/2016/05/20/top-100-most-subscribed-youtube-channels-worldwide-april-2016/|archive-date=2017-09-05|access-date=2017-04-28|work=[[Tubefilter]]}}</ref> In July 2016, his channel reached 1 million subscribers.<ref>{{Cite tweet|last=Rallison |first=Robert |user=theodd1sout |number=759411086835589120 |title=THANKS FOR A MILLION SUBS!!!!!!💯0000 |access-date=2022-09-25}}</ref> At some point, Rallison dropped out of college to make videos full-time.<ref name="Places of residence" />

On December 2, 2017, Rallison created a second channel, TheOdd2sOut, in which non-animation content is uploaded, i.e. gaming. TheOdd2sOut amassed 1 million{{nbsp}}subscribers in April 2018,<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=TheOdd2sOut's YouTube Stats|url=https://socialblade.com/youtube/channel/UC0GLNhtTu7yI8rl6ZZGeezw|access-date=2020-06-29|website=Social Blade}}</ref> and TheOdd1sOut reached 10{{nbsp}}million subscribers in January 2019.<ref>{{Cite AV media|last=Rallison |first=Robert |publisher=TheOdd1sOut |title=10 Million Sprinkle Special |url=https://youtube.com/watch?v=mOEyGEGypvs |website=[[YouTube]] |type=[[Video]] |date=2019-03-02 |access-date=2022-09-25}}</ref>

In early 2026, Rallison downsized his animation team, citing reduced output and work available for the team. While this initially prompted backlash from fans who were under the impression that Rallison fired the entire team without notice, Rallison clarified that he still has an animation team and that all of the animators that were let go were informed in advance and those affected who were working full time were given severance packages.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roy |first1=Sumit |title=Why did TheOdd1sOut reduce his animation team? James Rallison responds as internet debate explodes |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/world/us-streamers/why-did-theodd1sout-reduce-his-animation-team-james-rallison-responds-as-internet-debate-explodes/articleshow/129274829.cms |access-date=April 20, 2026 |work=The Times of India |date=March 8, 2026}}</ref>

====Collaborations====
[[File:Vidcon Animators Panel 2017.jpg|left|thumb|210x210px|Rallison (left) with various other animation [[YouTuber]]s, including [[Domics]] (2nd from right) and [[Jaiden Animations]] (right)]]
Rallison has collaborated with others to produce two songs and their accompanying music videos: "Life is Fun" in July 2018 with [[David "Boyinaband" Brown]];<ref>{{Cite web|last=TheOdd1sOut|date=2018-07-19|title=Life is Fun – Ft. Boyinaband (Official Music Video)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CAb_bCtKuXg|access-date=2019-03-23|website=YouTube}}</ref><ref name="bmi">{{cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Life Is Fun - BMI Repertoire Search|url=https://repertoire.bmi.com/Search/Search?Main_Search_Text=Life%20is%20Fun&Main_Search=Title&Sub_Search=Please%20Select&Search_Type=all&View_Count=0&Page_Number=0|access-date=2021-01-31|website=BMI Repertoire|publisher=[[Broadcast Music, Inc.]]}}</ref> and "Good Person" in December 2020 with [[Joel "Roomie" Berghult]].

His animated character appeared in the credits scene of ''[[YouTube Rewind: The Shape of 2017]]'' and in ''[[YouTube Rewind 2018: Everyone Controls Rewind]]'' where he has a speaking role.<ref>{{Citation|last=YouTube Spotlight|title=YouTube Rewind 2018: Everyone Controls Rewind {{!}} #YouTubeRewind|date=December 6, 2018 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YbJOTdZBX1g|access-date=2019-01-21}}</ref>
In March 2019, Rallison was in [[MrBeast]]'s $200,000 YouTuber Battle Royale video. He was on a team with [[Jaiden Animations]] and [[Anthony Padilla]] and they won the first round.<ref>{{cite web|last=Griffin|first=Louise|date=2019-03-12|title=MrBeast unleashes hell on Caspar Lee, Anthony Padilla and JaidenAnimations in YouTuber Battle Royale|url=https://metro.co.uk/2019/03/12/mrbeast-unleashes-hell-on-caspar-lee-anthony-padilla-and-jaidenanimations-in-youtuber-battle-royale-8893154/|access-date=2019-06-10|publisher=[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]}}</ref> Rallison gave the earnings he made from the YouTuber Battle Royale to [[Team Trees]], a non-profit started by [[MrBeast]] that aimed to plant 20 million trees by the end of 2019.<ref name="teamtrees">{{cite news |last1=Griffin |first1=Louise |title=PewDiePie donates $69,420 to MrBeast's TeamTrees as he brands himself 'boomer' |url=https://metro.co.uk/2019/10/31/pewdiepie-donates-69420-mrbeasts-teamtrees-brands-boomer-11019297/ |access-date=2019-11-06 |work=Metro |date=2019-10-31}}</ref>

===Other work===
Rallison wrote a book titled ''The Odd 1s Out: How to Be Cool and Other Things I Definitely Learned from Growing Up'', which was released in July 2018.<ref name="auto" /> It was ranked No. 12 in the "trade paperback" category on ''[[Publishers Weekly]]''{{'}}s August 13, 2018, bestseller list.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/bookselling/article/77731-this-week-s-bestsellers-august-13-2018.html |title=This Week's Bestsellers: August 13, 2018 |last=Juris |first=Carolyn |date=2018-08-10 |website=[[Publishers Weekly]] |access-date=2019-01-09}}</ref>

[[File:Can't Catch Harry Board Game.jpg|thumb|The Can't Catch Harry board game]]

Rallison also worked on board games ''Can't Catch Harry'' and ''Cafe Chaos'',<ref name="AdultBook">{{Cite web|last=TheOdd1sOut|date=2018-06-16|title=A Book I Made as an Adult|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4bPezggGBa8|access-date=2020-02-11|website=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Out |first=The Odd 1s |title='The Odd 1s Out' Releases New Food Fight Card Game, Cafe Chaos, on Kickstarter |url=https://www.prweb.com/releases/-the-odd-1s-out-releases-new-food-fight-card-game-cafe-chaos-on-kickstarter-895217295.html |access-date=2026-04-11 |website=www.prweb.com |language=en}}</ref> and, on November 22, Rallison announced and released his mobile game named ''TheOdd1sOut: Let's Bounce!''.<ref name="LetsBounce">{{cite news |last1=Gregson-Wood |first1=Stephen |title=TheOdd1sOut: Let's Bounce is a casual game for mobile that sees players bouncing through YouTuber James Rallison's life |url=https://www.pocketgamer.com/articles/084613/theodd1sout-lets-bounce-is-a-casual-game-for-mobile-that-sees-players-bouncing-through-youtuber-james-rallisons-life/ |access-date=2020-11-24 |work=Pocket Gamer}}</ref>

In June 2022, Rallison announced that an animated series, ''[[Oddballs (2022 TV series)|Oddballs]]'', based on his character, would premiere on [[Netflix]] later in the year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Lang |first1=Jamie |title='Oddballs' Series Coming To Netflix From Youtube Creator James Rallison |url=https://www.cartoonbrew.com/series/odballs-series-netflix-james-rallison-youtube-218072.html |website=Cartoon Brew |access-date=2022-06-23 |date=2022-06-23}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Robinson |first1=Jacob |title=Netflix Animated Series 'Oddballs': Coming to Netflix in October 2022 |url=https://www.whats-on-netflix.com/news/netflix-animated-series-oddballs-coming-to-netflix-in-october-2022/ |website=What's on Netflix |access-date=2022-09-17 |language=en |date=2022-09-16}}</ref>

As of December 2022, Rallison's main YouTube channel had over 19.5{{nbsp}}million subscribers, and his secondary channel had over 2.7{{nbsp}}million subscribers.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://socialblade.com/youtube/c/theodd1sout| title=TheOdd1sOut's YouTube Stats (Summary Profile) - Social Blade Stats| newspaper=Socialblade.com| date= | accessdate=2022-12-10}}</ref><ref name=":0"/>

'''Jahvante Jahqwane Sheldon Smart''' ({{Birth date|1996|11|18}} – {{death date|2018|06|30}}), known professionally as '''Smoke Dawg''', was a Canadian rapper from [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]]. He was a part of hip hop collective [[Halal Gang]] alongside [[Mustafa the Poet]], [[Puffy L'z]], [[Safe (musician)|Safe]], and Mo-G who come together with the [[Prime Boys]] to make the [[Supergroup (music)|supergroup]] Full Circle. His debut and only studio album, ''[[Struggle Before Glory]]'', was released posthumously in 2018.

==Career==
===Beginnings: 2012–2014===
Smart began rapping at the age of 16 in 2012. He gained recognition in 2014 with the release of "Still" featuring Halal Gang member MoG, on October 4, 2014. It gained over 1 million views within a month.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/halal-gang-set-the-record-straight/|title=Halal Gang Set the Record Straight|first=Amani Bin|last=Shikhan|date=July 9, 2018}}</ref> Mo-G and Smoke Dawg re-uploaded the song "Still" to YouTube in January 2015. In the video, the two rappers and their friends rap, dance, and laugh in shadowy parking lots, fluorescent-lit apartment corridors, and an empty studio. Although the initial upload was deleted, its re-upload amassed over 4 million views within a year of being online.<ref name="RiriFader">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefader.com/2017/03/06/puffy-lz-riri-halal-gang|title=Watch Puffy L'z New Video For "Riri" And Get To Know Toronto's Halal Gang|website=[[The Fader]]|date=January 29, 2017 }}</ref>

==="Trap House:" 2015–2016===
Smart released the single "Trap House" on July 31, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsweek.com/rapper-smoke-dawg-killed-outside-toronto-nightclub-1004189|title=Drake mourns Smoke Dawg on Instagram after rapper and his friend were fatally shot in Toronto|author=Kelly Wynne|date=July 2, 2018|website=Newsweek.com}}</ref> The single introduced a dance move known as "flippin'" and gained the attention of artists including [[French Montana]], who appeared on the official remix of the single,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/586315-smoke-dawg-trap-house-remix-feat-french-montana-new-song|title=Smoke Dawg – Trap House (Remix) Feat. French Montana|website=HotNewHipHop.com|date=July 30, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/premiere-smoke-dawg-flippin-prod-by-murda/|title=Will Smoke Dawg's "Flippin'" Be Responsible for the Next Big Dance Move? – Noisey|date=November 2, 2015 |publisher=}}</ref> and Toronto artist [[Drake (musician)|Drake]]. Drake went on to include Smart in many of his worldwide tours and he also headlined alongside [[ASAP Ferg]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.ca/2018/07/01/who-was-smoke-dawg-drake-toronto-shooting_a_23472254/|title=Toronto Rapper Smoke Dawg Killed In Downtown Shooting|date=July 1, 2018|website=HuffPost Canada}}</ref> Safe released the single "Hang" in 2015 which saw a feature from Smoke Dawg.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hypebeast.com/2015/7/safe-featuring-smoke-dawg-hang|title=Safe featuring Smoke Dawg – Hang|website=Hypebeast.com|date=July 21, 2015}}</ref> Smart released the single "Overseas" alongside [[Skepta]] in October 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thefader.com/2016/10/17/skepta-smoke-dawg-overseas|title=Listen To Skepta's New Collaboration With Toronto's Smoke Dawg|website=Thefader.com}}</ref> This was Skepta's second work with a Canadian artist, the first being [[Tre Mission]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.factmag.com/2016/10/17/skepta-toronto-smoke-dawg-overseas/|title=Listen to Skepta's collaboration with Toronto's Smoke Dawg, 'Overseas'|website=Factmag.com|date=October 17, 2016}}</ref> The single was produced by Toronto native [[Murda Beatz]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hypebeast.com/2016/10/smoke-dawg-skepta-overseas|title=Smoke Dawg & Skepta Link up for "Overseas" Video|website=Hypebeast.com|date=October 17, 2016}}</ref> Smart also performed at Toronto's first independent hip-hop festival outside of OVO's own offering, 6 Fest. The two-day festival saw Smoke Dawg performing alongside his Halal Gang as well as Pusha T, French Montana and Roy Woods.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/even-without-drake-torontos-6-fest-got-the-showcase-it-deserved/|title=Even Without Drake, Toronto's 6 Fest Got the Showcase It Deserved|first=Jake|last=Kivanc|website=Vice.com|date=October 13, 2016}}</ref>

===''Struggle Before Glory'': 2017–2018===
Smart was named on ''[[Now (newspaper)|Now]]''{{'}}s list of Toronto musicians to watch for in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nowtoronto.com/api/content/c56e345e-e74b-11e6-898e-0aea2a882f79/|title=Toronto musicians to watch in 2017: hip-hop edition|first=Kevin|last=Ritchie|date=January 31, 2017|website=NOW Magazine}}</ref> In February 2017, Smart released the song "Count it Up", having gone to London, UK to shoot the music video.<ref name=billboard>{{Cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/8463539/smoke-dawg-shot-killed-in-toronto-report|title=Smoke Dawg Dead: Rapper Shot, Killed in Toronto|date=July 1, 2018|magazine=Billboard|access-date=March 3, 2020}}</ref> He also headlined in London with supporting acts Nafe Smallz, Drake and Splurgeboys.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://grmdaily.com/smoke-dawg-nafe-smallz-drake-skepta-section-boyz|title=Smoke Dawg brings out Nafe Smallz and Drake at his headline Show in London|website=Grmdaily.com|date=February 17, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ticketarena.co.uk/events/XOYO-Presents-Sm|title=XOYO Presents: Smoke Dawg + Guests, Splurgeboys x PAP, Nafe Smallz + More Tickets | XOYO, London|website=Ticketarena.co.uk}}</ref> Whilst in the UK, Smoke Dawg and Halal Gang affiliate [[Puffy L'z]] dropped a "Fire in the Booth" freestyle with [[Charlie Sloth]] in March 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p04wxsh0|title=BBC Radio 1 – 1Xtra's Rap Show with Charlie Sloth, Fire from Smoke Dawg and Puffy, Fire in the Booth – Smoke Dawg and Puffy L'z (Halal Gang)|website=BBC|date=March 15, 2017 }}</ref> He was also on the [[Boy Meets World Tour]] touring with [[Drake (musician)|Drake]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hiphopdx.com/news/id.42408/title.drake-surprises-audience-at-club-show-in-london|title=Drake Surprises Audience At Club Show In London|date=February 17, 2017|website=Hiphopdx.com}}</ref><ref name=vice>{{cite web |title=Noisey Meets: Smoke Dawg |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/noisey-meets-smoke-dawg/ |website=Noisey |date=December 21, 2017 |publisher=VICE}}</ref> During this month Smart also featured on Jimmy Prime's single "Humana" alongside Donnie.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2017/03/jimmy-prime-smoke-dawg-donnie-humana-video|title=Premiere: Jimmy Prime Turns Up With Smoke Dawg and Donnie in "Humana" Video|website=Complex.com}}</ref> Toronto's most notorious music festival, uTOpia, was held during June 2017 and showcased the new generation of artists in the General Toronto Area. Smoke Dawg, one of the main performers of the festival, brought out Puffy L'z and Mo-G. The event was rated a 7 by ''[[Exclaim!]]'', who described Prime Boys and Halal Gang's performance as playing off of each other's energy, which ultimately brought the night together.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://exclaim.ca/music/article/utopia_music_festival_featuring_jimmy_prime_ramriddlz_smoke_dawg_drew_howard_and_more-mod_club_toronto_on_june_1 | title=UTOpia Music Festival featuring Jimmy Prime, Ramriddlz, Smoke Dawg, Drew Howard and more Mod Club, Toronto ON, June 1|website=Exclaim.ca}}</ref>

In September 2017, Smart was featured in the documentary ''Northside'', which highlighted Toronto's fledgling rap scene.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2017/09/northside-nathan-miller-documentary|title="NORTHSIDE" Is a Must-Watch Documentary on Toronto's Fledging Rap Scene|website=Complex}}</ref> [[Noisey]] released a short film titled ''Noisey Meets Smoke Dawg'' in December 2017. The behind-the-scenes documentary caught up with Smoke Dawg in Toronto where he talked about his rise, the passing of his best friend, and how to break through Toronto's glass ceiling.<ref name=vice/>

Smart announced that he was working on his debut studio album, ''[[Struggle Before Glory]]'', in early 2018. However, before it was released, he was shot and killed on June 30, 2018, in front of a nightclub in [[downtown Toronto]].<ref name="CanadianPress">{{cite news |author1=The Canadian Press |authorlink1=The Canadian Press |title=Toronto police identify rapper Smoke Dawg as one of two killed in shooting |url=https://www.nationalobserver.com/2018/07/03/news/toronto-police-identify-rapper-smoke-dawg-one-two-killed-shooting |accessdate=July 11, 2018 |work=[[National Observer (Canada)|National Observer]] |date=July 3, 2018 |language=en}}</ref> The lead single of the album, "No Discussion", featured AJ Tracey and was produced by Murda Beatz. It was released a month after his death on August 13, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hypebeast.com/2018/8/smoke-dawg-no-discussion-video|title=Smoke Dawg Releases Posthumous Single "No Discussion" Video Featuring AJ Tracey|website=HYPEBEAST|date=August 14, 2018}}</ref> Smoke Dawg's posthumous debut and only studio album, ''Struggle Before Glory'', was released on November 29, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/125368-stream-smoke-dawgs-posthumous-project-struggle-before-glory-ft-giggs-jay-critch-and-more-new-mixtape|title=Stream Smoke Dawg's Posthumous Project "Struggle Before Glory" Ft. Giggs, Jay Critch & More|website=HotNewHipHop|date=November 30, 2018}}</ref> The album was rated 8/10 by ''[[Exclaim!]]''.<ref name=exclaim>{{Cite web | url=http://exclaim.ca/music/article/smoke_dawg-struggle_before_glory |title = Smoke Dawg Struggle Before Glory|website=Exclaim.ca}}</ref> The album features from the likes of Toronto artists [[Puffy L'z]], [[Jimmy Prime]], [[Jay Whiss]] and [[Safe (musician)|Safe]], as well as UK artists [[Fredo (rapper)|Fredo]], [[AJ Tracey]] and [[Giggs (rapper)|Giggs]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://exclaim.ca/music/article/hear_smoke_dawgs_posthumous_struggle_before_glory_lp | title=Hear Smoke Dawg's Posthumous 'Struggle Before Glory' LP|website=Exclaim.ca}}</ref> The album was described as a "sum up of the late rapper's legacy".<ref name=exclaim/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fyimusicnews.ca/articles/2018/08/20/music-news-digest-aug-20-2018|title=Music News Digest, Aug. 20, 2018|date=August 20, 2018|website=FYIMusicNews.ca}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/listen-to-smoke-dawgs-posthumous-album-struggle-before-glory/|title=Listen to Smoke Dawg's Posthumous Album 'Struggle Before Glory'|first=Sharine|last=Taylor|website=Vice.com|date=December 3, 2018}}</ref> Smoke Dawg's younger brother, Young Smoke, provided a tribute on the outro of the album.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2019/02/young-smoke-smokey-world-new-video|title=Young Smoke Proves It's "Smokey World" in New Video|website=Complex.com}}</ref>

===Posthumous appearances and legacy: 2019–present===

Halal Gang affiliate Mustafa the Poet released a short film titled ''Remember Me, Toronto''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.highsnobiety.com/p/drake-remember-me-toronto-film/|title=Drake Features in 'Remember Me, Toronto' Short Film: Watch Here|date=March 18, 2019|website=Highsnobiety}}</ref> The film discusses gun and gang violence, and features over a dozen Toronto-based hip-hop artists. Smart was featured in archive footage of his speech on how he wishes to be remembered.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thebeatofthecapital.com/2019/03/19/drake-featured-in-mustafa-the-poets-short-film-remember-me-toronto/ |title=Drake Featured In Mustafa The Poet's Short Film 'Remember Me, Toronto' | 97.7 WRBJ |publisher=Thebeatofthecapital.com |date= |accessdate=March 22, 2020}}</ref> Smart appeared on [[Puffy L'z]]' debut album ''Take No L'z'', released on July 19, 2019, on the single "Boring" alongside [[Jay Whiss]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://exclaim.ca/music/article/puffy_lz-take_no_lz|title=Puffy L'z Take No L'z|website=exclaim.ca}}</ref> He was also featured on [[Donnie (Canadian rapper)|Donnie]]'s debut album ''From the Beginning to End'', released on November 22, 2019, on the track "Good as it Gets" alongside [[Jimmy Prime]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sidedoormag.com/blog/2019/11/26/donnie-comes-correct-with-solo-album-from-the-beginning-to-end|title=Donnie Comes Correct With Solo Album "From the Beginning To End"|website=Sidedoor Magazine}}</ref> 

Jay Whiss released the single "Mind in a Maze", the lead single for his debut album ''[[Peace of Mind (Jay Whiss album)|Peace of Mind]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/244992-jay-whiss-unleashes-his-debut-album-peace-of-mind-new-mixtape|title=Jay Whiss Unleashes His Debut Album "Peace Of Mind"|website=HotNewHipHop|date=March 4, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.breakingnews.fr/divertissement/jay-whiss-devoile-son-premier-album-peace-of-mind-308668.html|title=Jay Whiss dévoile son premier album "Peace Of Mind"|date=March 4, 2020|website=Vivez l'actualité Avec Breakingnews.fr}} {{Dead link|date=March 2026}}</ref> The song was a tribute to Smoke Dawg, and Whiss has stated that it was his favorite song he ever recorded.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/2020/03/jay-whiss-peace-of-mind-interview|title=Jay Whiss Pops Some Bubbly to Discuss His Major Label Debut|website=Complex}}</ref> Smart was known for his ad-lib "Awhoolay"; in an interview with ''[[Now (newspaper)|Now]]'' newspaper, Puffy L'z stated he uses the ad-lib to keep Smart's name alive.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nowtoronto.com/api/content/c26984f4-ad80-11e9-aece-12f1225286c6/|title=Puffy L'z knows his mission is bigger than music|first=Claudia|last=McNeilly|date=July 24, 2019|website=NOW Magazine}}</ref>

Mustafa the Poet dedicated his 2021 debut album ''[[When Smoke Rises]]'' to Smoke Dawg, who is also featured on the cover art.

==Death==
On June 30, 2018, Smart was killed in a shooting during broad daylight in front of a downtown nightclub in the [[Toronto Entertainment District]] near the corner of [[Queen Street West]] and [[Spadina Avenue]].<ref name="CanadianPress"/> The perpetrators allegedly shot multiple times and fled in a black SUV with tinted windows. Three victims, including Smoke Dawg, were injured. Two were later pronounced dead in hospital.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Yazdani |first1=Tina |title=Friends remember victims of deadly Queen West shooting |date=July 2018 |url=https://toronto.citynews.ca/2018/07/01/victims-deadly-queen-west-shooting/ |publisher=[[CityNews]] |accessdate=July 2, 2018}}</ref> Affiliates of Smoke Dawg posted on social media that Smoke Dawg and 28-year-old [[Prime Boys]] manager Koba Prime (birth name Ernest "Kosi" Modekwe) were killed in the shooting,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ritchie |first1=Kevin |title=Smoke Dawg reportedly killed in shooting on Queen West |url=https://nowtoronto.com/music/features/smoke-dawg-shooting-queen-west/ |website=NOW Magazine |date=July 2018 |publisher=[[Now (newspaper)|Now]] |accessdate=July 1, 2018}}</ref> with the [[Toronto Police Service]] confirming this the following day.<ref>{{cite web |title=Two men killed in Queen Street shooting identified as members of Toronto music scene |date=July 2018 |url=https://www.cp24.com/news/two-men-killed-in-queen-street-shooting-identified-as-members-of-toronto-music-scene-1.3996128 |publisher=CP24 |accessdate=July 2, 2018}}</ref><ref name="Friend">{{cite news |last1=Friend |first1=David  |title=Toronto mayor meets members of hip-hop community to talk gun violence solutions |url=https://www.nationalobserver.com/2018/07/07/news/toronto-mayor-meets-members-hip-hop-community-talk-gun-violence-solutions |accessdate=July 11, 2018 |work=[[National Observer (Canada)|National Observer]] |date=July 7, 2018 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Gangs, guns and Toronto: A primer on this summer's shootings and the stories behind them |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/toronto/article-toronto-gun-violence-gangs-police-explainer/ |accessdate=July 11, 2018 |work=[[The Globe and Mail]] |date=July 5, 2018}}</ref> Mayor [[John Tory]] blamed the shooting on [[gun violence]], and as a result met with the [[6ixBuzz]] team and [[Director X]] to meet with members of the hip-hop community to talk gun violence solutions and raise awareness on the issue.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/john-tory-kardinal-offishall-hip-hop-gun-violence-1.4737713|title=Toronto mayor meets members of hip-hop community to talk gun violence solutions|website=Cbc.ca|access-date=November 27, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/smoke-dawg-shooting-1.4730746|title=Questions swirl around Toronto rapper Smoke Dawg's death|website=Cbc.ca|access-date=November 27, 2021}}</ref><ref name=billboard/>

Abdulkadir Handule, known by the stage name "21Neat", pleaded not guilty to two counts of first-degree murder, but was convicted of two counts of second-degree murder by an Ontario Superior Court jury in February 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/man-found-guilty-of-the-2018-murder-of-rapper-smoke-dawg-in-toronto-3170988 | title=Man found guilty of the 2018 murder of rapper Smoke Dawg in Toronto | website=[[NME]] | date=February 28, 2022 }}</ref><ref name="comp1">{{cite web | url=https://www.complex.com/music/smoke-dawg-murder-charge-toronto | title=Man Found Guilty in 2018 Murder of Toronto Rapper Smoke Dawg and Manager | website=[[Complex Networks]] }}</ref> Handule is currently serving a [[life sentence]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.thestar.com/news/gta/2022/05/27/i-got-a-life-sentence-mother-of-murdered-rapper-smoke-dawg-sobs-in-grief-during-sentencing-hearing.html | title='I got a life sentence': Mother of murdered rapper Smoke Dawg sobs in grief during sentencing hearing | website=[[Toronto Star]] | date=May 27, 2022 }}</ref><ref name="comp1"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Man found guilty of 2nd-degree murder of Toronto rapper Smoke Dawg, brand manager Ernest Modekwe |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/handule-trial-guilty-smoke-dawg-1.6362949 |website=[[CBC News]] |date=2022-02-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925190126/https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/handule-trial-guilty-smoke-dawg-1.6362949 |archive-date=2022-09-25 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://exclaim.ca/music/article/man_found_guilty_of_murder_of_toronto_rapper_smoke_dawg | title=Man Found Guilty of Murder of Toronto Rapper Smoke Dawg | Exclaim! }}</ref>

'''Yonatan Alexis Rodríguez Benítez''' (born 1 July 1993) is a Uruguayan professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for Chilean club [[Deportes Concepción (Chile)|Deportes Concepción]].

==Career==
Rodríguez is from a humble background in [[Montevideo]], one of five children. Whilst playing at Palma De Flores Baby Futbol Club he would sometimes have to go to training without having first had breakfast. Rodríguez came through the ranks at [[Club Sportivo Cerrito]] playing as a defensive midfielder.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/yonathan-rodriguez-el-vaso-de-leche-vacio-el-descenso-a-la-c-y-el-debut-en-primera-a-los-28-anos-20218918450|title=Este artículo lo puede ver en este|website=elobservador.com}}</ref>

He made his debut against [[Boston River]] on 12 October 2013 in a 0–0 draw in the [[Uruguayan Segunda División]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/10/12/uruguay/segunda-division/boston-river/club-sportivo-cerrito/1596635/|title=CERRITO VS. BOSTON RIVER 0-0|website=Soccerway}}</ref> He stayed with the club despite relegation to [[Uruguayan Segunda División Amateur|Uruguayan third division]] in 2014–15. In the third division they played for one season and over the following seasons reached the promotion playoffs on more than one occasion before achieving promotion from the Segunda Division as champions in 2020. Rodríguez made a total of 146 appearances league and scored 9 goals for the senior Cerrito side prior to joining [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] aged 28 in January 2022 on a one-year loan deal. The deal contained a stipulation for a second season should he play a minimum of 60% of their matches.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.futbol.com.uy/Deportes/Nacional-El-volante-Yonathan-Rodriguez-dejo-Cerrito-y-es-nuevo-jugador-de-los-tricolores-uc810746|title=Nacional: Midfielder Yonathan Rodríguez left Cerrito and is a new tricolor player|website=futbol.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elpais.com.uy/amp/ovacion/futbol/nacional-contrato-incorporacion-yonathan-rodriguez-cerrito.html|title=Nacional sorprendió con la incorporación de Yonathan Rodríguez, de Cerrito|website=elpais.com}}</ref>
 
With Nacional he made his debut in the [[Copa Libertadores]], starting all six of their games, as well as making three appearances in the [[Copa Sudamerica]]. He was part of their title-winning [[2022 Uruguayan Primera División season]]. From the first 50 games available to him in all competitions he secured 33 starts plus 3 substitute appearances to ensure an automatic second season with Nacional as stated in his contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elpais.com.uy/amp/ovacion/futbol/minutos-jugo-yona-rodriguez-aseguro-renovacion-contrato-nacional.html|title=Por los minutos que ya jugó, Yona Rodríguez se aseguró la renovación de su contrato en Nacional|website=Elpais.com}}</ref>

In January 2025, he returned to Nacional after spending 2 years in the [[Argentine Primera División]] with [[Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|Gimnasia LP]] and [[Club Atlético Banfield|Banfield]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Yonatan Rodríguez en su vuelta a Nacional: “Cuando llegás al más grande, vas por todo” |url=https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Deportes/Yonatan-Rodriguez-en-su-vuelta-a-Nacional--Cuando-llegas-al-mas-grande-vas-por-todo--uc912451 |access-date=2025-05-13 |website=futbol.com.uy - Montevideo Portal |language=es}}</ref>

On 19 February 2026, Rodriguez signed with Chilean club [[Deportes Concepción (Chile)|Deportes Concepción]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rubio |first1=Jorge |title=Llega a Chile de REFUERZO por inesperado efecto dominó en Uruguay: "No tuve tiempo..." |url=https://redgol.cl/mercado-de-fichajes/deportes-concepcion-mauricio-vera-nacional-montevideo-yonatan-rodriguez-contrato-refuerzo-patricio-almendra |access-date=20 February 2026 |work=RedGol |date=19 February 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

'''Renato Henrique Ferreira Silvestre da Silva''' (born 10 October 1993), known as '''Renato Henrique''', is a Brazilian [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] or a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Porto Vitória Futebol Clube|Porto Vitória]], on loan from [[América Futebol Clube (PE)|América-PE]].

He began his career at [[Clube Náutico Capibaribe|Náutico]], where he played in the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série B]]. He won the [[Campeonato Pernambucano]] with [[Salgueiro Atlético Clube|Salgueiro]] in [[2020 Campeonato Pernambucano|2020]], the first time the title was taken out of the state capital [[Recife]]. In the 2022 edition, with [[Retrô Futebol Clube Brasil|Retrô]], he was the top scorer with seven goals for the runners-up. He was also top scorer in [[Campeonato Pernambucano Série A2|Série A2]] and [[Campeonato Pernambucano Série A3|Série A3]] of the league in 2023 and 2024 respectively, making him the only person to achieve the honour in all three divisions.

==Career==
===Early career and Salgueiro===
Born in [[Recife]] in the state of [[Pernambuco]], Renato Henrique began his career at hometown club [[Clube Náutico Capibaribe|Naútico]], after having been loaned to [[SE Palmeiras|Palmeiras]] as a youth. Following moves to [[Boa Esporte Clube|Boa]] and [[Guarani FC|Guarani-SP]], he signed for [[Desportivo Brasil]] in the [[Campeonato Paulista Série A3]] for 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Desportivo Brasil apresenta o atacante Renato Henrique, ex-Guarani|trans-title=Desportivo Brasil present the forward Renato Henrique, formerly of Guarani|url=https://ge.globo.com/sp/tem-esporte/futebol/noticia/desportivo-brasil-apresenta-o-atacante-renato-henrique-ex-guarani.ghtml |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=GE |date=13 December 2017 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

Renato Henrique returned to his home state in 2019, signing for [[Salgueiro Atlético Clube|Salgueiro]]. He was loaned to [[Decisão Sertânia Futebol Clube|Decisão]] for most of the year, where he won the [[Campeonato Pernambucano Série A2]].<ref name=decisao>{{cite news |last1=Aguiar |first1=Vítor |title=Voltando ao Salgueiro, meia Renato Henrique revela confiança no Decisão para Estadual|trans-title=Returning to Salgueiro, mifielder Renato Henrique reveals confidence in Decisão for the State Championship|url=https://www.pe.superesportes.com.br/app/noticias/futebol/futebol-nacional/2019/11/14/noticia_futebol_nacional,58135/voltando-ao-salgueiro-meia-renato-henrique-revela-confianca-no-decisa.shtml |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=Super Esporte |date=14 November 2019 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> In 2020, he helped Salgueiro to the [[Campeonato Pernambucano]], the first team from outside the state capital Recife to win the title;<ref name=ferro>{{cite news |last1=de Andrade Neto |first1=João |title=Renato, do Retrô, pode ser primeiro bicampeão pernambucano fora do "Trio de Ferro" em 85 anos|trans-title=Renato, of Retrô, culd becme the first two-time Campeonato Pernambucano winner outside the "Iron Trio" in 85 years|url=https://ge.globo.com/pe/futebol/times/retro/noticia/2022/04/29/renato-do-retro-pode-ser-primeiro-bicampeao-pernambucano-fora-do-trio-de-ferro-em-85-anos.ghtml |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=GE |date=29 April 2022 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> he added eight goals in the year's [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série D]] to the three he had scored in the state league.<ref name=luz>{{cite news |title=Hercílio Luz apresenta Renato Henrique: camisa 10 e artilheiro |trans-title=Hercílio Luz present Renato Henrique: number 10 and top scorer|url=https://ge.globo.com/sc/futebol/times/hercilio-luz/noticia/hercilio-luz-apresenta-renato-henrique-camisa-10-e-artilheiro.ghtml |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=GE |date=27 January 2021 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

In January 2021, Renato Henrique moved to [[Hercílio Luz Futebol Clube|Hercílio Luz]] in the [[Campeonato Catarinense]].<ref name=luz/> He spent the second half of the year between [[Esporte Clube Jacuipense|Jacuipense]] of [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série C]] and [[Castanhal Esporte Clube|Castanhal]] in Série D.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fazendinha é passado: Castanhal se reforça com meia ex-Palmeiras para o mata-mata da Série D|trans-title=Fazendinha is in the past: Castanhal strengthen with ex-Palmeiras midfielder for Série D head-to-head |url=https://ge.globo.com/pa/futebol/times/castanhal/noticia/fazendinha-e-passado-castanhal-se-reforca-com-meia-ex-palmeiras-para-o-mata-mata-da-serie-d.ghtml |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=GE |date=7 September 2021 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

===Retrô===
Renato Henrique signed for [[Retrô Futebol Clube Brasil|Retrô]] in 2022. His team reached the final of the year's Campeonato Pernambucano before losing on penalties to Naútico;<ref name=ne>{{cite news |title=Destaque do Retrô, Renato Henrique rompe ligamento do joelho e está fora da temporada|trans-title=Highlight of Retrô, Renato Henrique breaks knee ligament and is out for the season|url=https://ne45.com.br/2022/07/05/destaque-do-retro-renato-henrique-rompe-ligamento-do-joelho-e-esta-fora-da-temporada/ |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=NE 45 |date=5 July 2022 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> had he won, he would have become the first player to win the title twice with teams apart from the Recife-based trio of Naútico, Sport and Santa Cruz since the players of {{ill|Tramways Sport Club|pt|lt=Tramways}} in 1936 and 1937.<ref name=ferro/> He was also the tournament's top scorer with seven goals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Artilheiro do Pernambucano, Renato Henrique deve ficar oito meses sem jogar|trans-title=Pernambucano top scorer, Renato Henrique must be out for eight months|url=https://ge.globo.com/pe/caruaru-regiao/futebol/noticia/2022/07/06/artilheiro-do-pernambucano-renato-henrique-deve-ficar-oito-meses-sem-jogar.ghtml |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=GE |date=6 July 2022 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> In July, he suffered an [[anterior cruciate ligament injury]] of the right knee while playing in the national Série D against [[Globo Futebol Clube|Globo-RN]] and was ruled out for eight months.<ref name=ne/>

In October 2023, Renato Henrique renewed his contract with Retrô, while on loan at [[Vera Cruz Futebol Clube|Vera Cruz]] in the [[Campeonato Pernambucano Série A2]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Domingos |first1=Rayane |title=Retrô anuncia renovação de contrato com o meia Renato Henrique|trans-title=Retrô announce contract renewal of midfielder Renato Henrique|url=https://ne45.com.br/2023/10/17/retro-anuncia-renovacao-com-renato-henrique/ |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=NE45 |date=17 October 2023 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> In the same month, he scored five goals in a 9–1 win over [[1º de Maio Esporte Clube|1º de Maio]]; he had previously scored four for Decisão against Vera Cruz in the second tier in 2019.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rocha |first1=Emerson |title=Autor de 5 gols em goleada de 9 a 1 na Série A2 de PE comemora feito inédito na carreira: "Número expressivo"|trans-title=Author of 5 goals in 9–1 rout in Campeonato Pernambucano Série A2 commemorates unprecedented feat in career: "Expressive number" |url=https://ge.globo.com/pe/petrolina-regiao/futebol/noticia/2023/10/18/autor-de-5-gols-em-goleada-de-9-a-1-na-serie-a2-de-pe-comemora-feito-inedito-na-carreira-numero-expressivo.ghtml |access-date=17 March 2025 |publisher=GE |date=18 October 2023 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> He finished the season as top scorer.<ref name=coleciona>{{cite news |title=Ex-Náutico, atacante coleciona artilharias no futebol pernambucano e ganha destaque|trans-title=Ex-Náutico, striker collects top scorer awards in Pernambuco football and gains prominence|url=https://ge.globo.com/pe/caruaru-regiao/noticia/2025/09/18/ex-nautico-atacante-coleciona-artilharias-no-futebol-pernambucano-e-ganha-destaque.ghtml |access-date=12 January 2026 |publisher=GE |date=18 September 2025 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

===América-PE===
Renato Henrique signed for [[América Futebol Clube (PE)|América-PE]] in October 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Holanda |first1=Felipe |title=América anuncia a contratação de Renato Henrique, ex-Náutico e Retrô|trans-title=América announce signing of Renato Henrique, formerly of Náutico and Retrô |url=https://www.leiaja.com/esportes/2024/10/04/america-contrata-renato-henrique-ex-nautico-e-retro/ |access-date=12 January 2026 |publisher=Leia Já |date=4 October 2024 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> He won the [[Campeonato Pernambucano Série A3]] that year, in addition to being top scorer with nine goals in five games, making him the first person to be top scorer in three divisions of the state league.<ref name=coleciona/>

In 2025, Renato Henrique was loaned to [[Madureira Esporte Clube|Madureira]] in the [[Campeonato Carioca]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ferreira |first1=Ruan |title=América-PE empresta meia Renato Henrique para o Madureira-RJ|trans-title=América-PE loan midfielder Renato Henrique to Madureira-RJ|url=https://ne45.com.br/2024/12/19/america-pe-empresta-renato-henrique/ |access-date=12 January 2026 |publisher=NE45 |date=19 December 2024 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> and then [[North Esporte Clube|North]], who won the [[Campeonato Mineiro Módulo II]]. He finished the year back at América-PE in the Pernambucano A2, scoring his attempt in the penalty shootout loss to [[Associação Acadêmica e Desportiva Vitória das Tabocas|Vitória das Tabocas]] in the final on 1 November.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Costa |first1=Yuri |title=Vitória vence América nos pênaltis, é campeão da Série A2 e retorna à elite do Pernambucano |trans-title=Vitória defeat América on penalties, are champions of Série A2 and return to the Pernambucano elite|url=https://www.folhape.com.br/esportes/vitoria-america-serie-a2-pernambucano/447792/ |access-date=12 January 2026 |work=Folha de Pernambuco |date=1 November 2025 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

Renato Henrique was loaned to [[Porto Vitória Futebol Clube|Porto Vitória]] for the [[Campeonato Capixaba]] at the start of 2026.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bicalho Assis |first1=Enzo |title=De promessa a realidade: Porto Vitória busca seu primeiro título do Capixabão|trans-title=From a promise to reality: Porto Vitória look for their first  ''Capixabão'' title|url=https://www.folhavitoria.com.br/esportes/de-promessa-a-realidade-porto-vitoria-busca-seu-primeiro-titulo-do-capixabao/ |access-date=12 January 2026 |work=Folha Vitória |date=8 January 2026 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>
