'''Zoë Bleu Sidel'''  (born 23 October 1994) is an American actress and [[Wardrobe stylist|fashion stylist]]. The  daughter of actress [[Rosanna Arquette]], she made her acting debut in a minor role in [[Sofia Coppola]]'s ''[[The Bling Ring|Bling Ring]]'' (2013) and had her first lead role as [[Brides of Dracula#In literature|Elisabeta]]/[[Mina Murray]] in [[Luc Besson]]'s ''[[Dracula (2025 French film)|Dracula]]'' (2025).

== Early life, family, and education ==

Zoë Bleu Sidel was born on 23 October 1994 in Los Angeles, California, and grew up between [[Laurel Canyon, Los Angeles|Laurel Canyon]] and [[Big Sur]]. Her mother is actress [[Rosanna Arquette]] and her father is [[restaurateur]] and [[Political science|political scientist]] John Sidel; her parents divorced when she was five.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Weinstock |first=Tish |date=May 11, 2016 |title=why zoë bleu sidel has the world at her feet |url=https://i-d.co/article/why-zo-bleu-sidel-has-the-world-at-her-feet/ |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[i-D]] |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Wonderland |date=June 3, 2016 |title=Zoe Bleu |url=https://www.wonderlandmagazine.com/2016/06/03/zoe-bleu/ |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[Wonderland (magazine)|Wonderland]] |language=en-GB |archive-date=July 24, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210724144700/https://www.wonderlandmagazine.com/2016/06/03/zoe-bleu/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Brunson |first=Courtney |last2=Bevan |first2=Andrew |date=March 20, 2013 |title=Meet The Stars Of The Crillon Ball |url=https://www.teenvogue.com/gallery/crillon-ball-debutantes-2013 |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[Teen Vogue]] |language=en-US |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124234226/https://www.teenvogue.com/gallery/crillon-ball-debutantes-2013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

She is of [[French-Canadian Americans|French-Canadian]] descent through her maternal grandfather, [[Lewis Arquette]], and her grandmother, Brenda Olivia "Mardi" ([[Married and maiden names|née]] Nowak) is of Jewish heritage, the daughter of a Holocaust survivor from [[History of the Jews in Poland|Poland]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoggard |first=Liz |date=August 17, 2006 |title=Patricia Arquette: The not-so-dippy hippie |url=https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/films/features/patricia-arquette-the-notsodippy-hippie-412274.html |access-date=October 21, 2025 |website=[[The Independent]] |language=en |archive-date=September 5, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250905223035/https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/films/features/patricia-arquette-the-notsodippy-hippie-412274.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Her aunt is [[Patricia Arquette]].<ref name=":0" />

Her name means "life" in Greek. She also called herself Zoë Sidel (after her father), Zoë Bleu Sidel, Zoë Bleu Arquette, and Zoë Bleu. And when asked if those names suggest a difficulty in finding her identity, she replied, "Absolutely not, I know very well who I am. But we all have several facets. The current one is Zoë Bleu, which corresponds to my fashion universe, which is a bit wild, a bit eccentric. Zoë is my youth, my childhood."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carriere |first=Christophe |date=July 18, 2025 |title=Zoé Bleu : « Luc Besson a transposé l'action de Dracula à Paris, ma ville préférée au monde ! » |trans-title=Zoé Bleu: “Luc Besson transposed the action of Dracula to Paris, my favorite city in the world!” |url=https://www.parismatch.com/culture/cinema/zoe-bleu-luc-besson-a-transpose-laction-de-dracula-a-paris-ma-ville-preferee-au-monde-254374 |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[Paris Match]] |language=fr |archive-date=September 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250920171529/https://www.parismatch.com/culture/cinema/zoe-bleu-luc-besson-a-transpose-laction-de-dracula-a-paris-ma-ville-preferee-au-monde-254374 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Bleu attended  [[Sarah Lawrence College]], where she studied [[poetry]] and [[art history]], focusing on periods from the [[Renaissance]] to the [[Baroque]], as well as [[Medieval art]] history. At the time, she thought she might one day pursue [[screenwriting]], a dream she still holds, but she didn’t yet feel confident enough to follow that path. Instead, she turned to art to learn about "historical clothing and the [[spectrum of light]] that makes up color."<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Ambroise |first=Laure |date=October 17, 2022 |title=Zoë Bleu : "le cinéma m'aide à rêver" |trans-title=Zoë Bleu: "Cinema helps me dream" |url=https://www.lofficiel.com/pop-culture/zoe-bleu |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[L'Officiel]] |language=fr |archive-date=May 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250524165425/https://www.lofficiel.com/pop-culture/zoe-bleu |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=SSENSE |date=February 21, 2017 |title=Zoe Bleu Sidel's Digital Baroque |url=https://www.ssense.com/en-dk/editorial/fashion/zoe-bleu-sidels-digital-baroque |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[SSENSE]] |language=en}}</ref> In 2012, she became a [[debutante]] at the [[Crillon ball|Crillon Ball]] in Paris.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=AlloCine |title=Zoë Bleu |url=https://www.allocine.fr/personne/fichepersonne-948753/biographie/ |access-date=2025-10-14 |website=[[AlloCiné]] |language=fr}}</ref>

At age 15, Bleu began studying the [[Meisner technique]], whereby actors must react instinctively to their surroundings. She recalled, "You really need to disrobe yourself and shed all your skin to reveal the most horrible part of yourself."<ref name=":0" /> Bleu recalls that her early experiences with acting were deeply shaped by her family. She grew up playing [[List of acting techniques|acting techniques]] games with them, often taking on different characters alongside her mother.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==

Although she had previously appeared in [[Sofia Coppola]]’s ''[[The Bling Ring]]'' (2013) in a minor role.<ref name=":0" /> This was followed be a small [[uncredited role]] in ''[[Mother, May I Sleep with Danger? (2016 film)|Mother, May I Sleep with Danger?]]'' (2016)'','' and ''[[The Institute (2017 film)|The Institute]]'' (2017).

In 2022, she wrote a short ballet film called ''Mandrake.'' She recalled, "It’s inspired by the [[Butoh]] dance theatre, which was created by [[Kazuo Ohno]] [and [[Tatsumi Hijikata]]] in the 1960s in Japan."<ref name=":3" /> That same year, she appeared in ''[[Signs of Love]]''; alongside her mother, she played a [[Deafness|deaf]] woman named Jane.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |last=Allaire |first=Christian |date=June 7, 2022 |title=Let This Rising Actor Be Your New Boho Muse |url=https://www.vogue.com/slideshow/zoe-bleu-bohemian-style-signs-of-love-premiere |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[Vogue (magazine)|Vogue]] |language=en-US |archive-date=October 7, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251007005339/https://www.vogue.com/slideshow/zoe-bleu-bohemian-style-signs-of-love-premiere |url-status=live }}</ref> Prior to the movie, she took [[acting classes]] for a few months, which is something she hadn't done since high school.<ref name=":2" />
Thanks to this [[Supporting character|supporting role]], as Jena, [[Johannes Boesiger]] noticed Bleu and offered her a part in his upcoming film ''Fly Little Bird'' (TBA). She then flew to London, where she learned to sing and formed her own band, ''L’Espiral''. During one of her performances, [[Luc Besson]] happened to be in the audience. The director had no idea who she was and after the concert, Besson invited her to [[audition]] for the role of ''Dracula'' film. Without hesitation, she began preparing her lines and took part in numerous [[screen test]]s. Around the same time, she decided to move to Paris. Upon her arrival, she went straight to the [[Sacré-Cœur, Paris|Sacré-Cœur]] and prayed to "anyone up there [who] is listening" to let her get a job in France, and a few weeks later, Luc called to confirm that she had the role. Besson recalled. It was only once filming began that Besson discovered Bleu’s connection to Arquette, saying "Talent runs in the family, she has the DNA and she’s worked hard."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rivet |first=Solenne |date=July 30, 2025 |title=Zoë Bleu (Dracula) marche sur les pas de sa mère, une célèbre héroïne de Luc Besson |url=https://www.gala.fr/l_actu/news_de_stars/zoe-bleu-dracula-marche-sur-les-pas-de-sa-mere-une-celebre-heroine-de-luc-besson-20250730 |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[Gala (magazine)|Gala]] |language=fr |archive-date=July 30, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250730145358/https://www.gala.fr/l_actu/news_de_stars/zoe-bleu-dracula-marche-sur-les-pas-de-sa-mere-une-celebre-heroine-de-luc-besson-20250730 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2025, the film titled ''[[Dracula (2025 French film)|Dracula]]'' was released in theaters in France on July 30, 2025, with Bleu playing the dual role of Elisabeta/[[Mina Murray]], the tragically deceased wife of Vlad/Dracula, and the young woman he finds in 19th-century Paris.<ref name=":5" />

Her performance in [[Luc Besson]]’s [[Dracula (2025 French film)|Dracula]] is widely noticed. On social media, several sequences from the film go viral and spark trends highlighting, in particular her acting performance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Le nouveau «Dracula» a fait naître un phénomène étrange |url=https://www.watson.ch/fr/!896849080 |access-date=2026-03-14 |website=[[Watson (newspaper)|Watson]] |language=fr}}</ref> The press, which is divided in its overall assessment of the film, unanimously praises her performance as “captivating",<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bradshaw |first=Peter |date=2025-11-25 |title=Dracula review – Luc Besson's romantic reimagining of Gothic classic is ridiculous but watchable |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2025/nov/25/dracula-a-love-tale-review-luc-besson-caleb-landry-jones-christoph-waltz |access-date=2026-03-14 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> alongside those of [[Caleb Landry Jones]], [[Christoph Waltz]], and [[Matilda De Angelis]].<ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.allocine.fr/film/fichefilm-326950/critiques/presse/ |title=Dracula: Les critiques presse |last=AlloCine |language=fr |access-date=2026-03-14 |via=www.allocine.fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dracula (2025) {{!}} Rotten Tomatoes |url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/dracula_2025_2 |access-date=2026-03-14 |website=www.rottentomatoes.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Fashion career ===
In 2016, Bleu walked the runway for her friend David Moses’s label, Moses Gauntlett Cheng, an experience she called "terrifying."<ref name=":6" /> She and her fashion [[collective]] friends Arielle Chiara and Darius Khonsary created ''Nautae'', which is a [[Latin term]] used to describe "a group of sailors."<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":6" /> ''Nautae'' describe as "unique, [[Fantasy couture|fantastical]] clothing from repurposed materials." She credits her love of fashion as what allowed her to feel at ease with her own body image. She explained the motivation: "Because I didn't feel good in my own skin, I wanted to feel good in the clothes I was wearing." Her style is described as dramatic and "otherworldly, something out of a 'gothic fairy tale.'" She is often asked about her outfits: "People always ask me, 'Where are you going? Is there a [[Renaissance fair]] on? What's the occasion?'" and the reason for such style is that: "I like to wear things that are beautiful, it makes me feel beautiful," and described her fashion: "I'm like the child bride, abandoned at the altar, like [[Miss Havisham]]. I have cobwebs in my hair and around my heart."<ref name=":0" /> Later she released her clothing brand Kaka Kouture. In 2018, she released a brand new label called Wherein I Dwell.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ongley |first=Hannah |date=July 16, 2018 |title=zoë bleu and georginia butz's new fashion label blends romance and tragedy |url=https://i-d.co/article/zoe-bleu-sidel-wherein-i-dwell-lookbook-launch/ |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=i-D |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Bleu dated actor [[Jack Kilmer]] in 2013.<ref name=":0" /> In 2023, she began dating actor [[Hopper Penn]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zilio |first=Bernie |date=May 8, 2023 |title=Exclusive {{!}} Sean Penn's son, Rosanna Arquette's daughter confirm romance |url=https://pagesix.com/2023/05/08/sean-penns-son-rosanna-arquettes-daughter-confirm-romance/ |access-date=October 14, 2025 |website=[[Page Six]] |language=en-US |archive-date=September 19, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250919074610/https://pagesix.com/2023/05/08/sean-penns-son-rosanna-arquettes-daughter-confirm-romance/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2016, she spoke about [[Body dysmorphic disorder|struggling with her body image]] recalling "I’m very short and stubby. I used to think, ‘Why won’t my legs stretch?". This  contributed to her decision to turn down her potential first [[Leading actor|leading role]] in [[Gia Coppola]]’s debut film, ''[[Palo Alto (2013 film)|Palo Alto]]'' (2013),  instead she chose to focus on her schoolwork.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Weinstock|first=Tish|date=May 11, 2016|title=why zoë bleu sidel has the world at her feet|url=https://i-d.co/article/why-zo-bleu-sidel-has-the-world-at-her-feet/|access-date=October 14, 2025|website=[[i-D]]|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 2015, she collaborated with [[Ruchira Gupta]] and her organization, [[Apne Aap Women Worldwide]], which supports victims of [[sex trafficking]] in India. Her involvement was  deeply personal, as she is a survivor of [[Child sexual abuse|childhood sexual abuse]], Sidel has stated that her primary goal is to help girls find the strength to speak about their experiences and pursue justice, emphasizing that “addressing it” is the most important step.<ref name=":0" />

''Hispanics in the U.S. Criminal Justice System'' | website = {{url|https://sofiastefani.com}} }} '''Sofía Stefani Espinoza Álvarez''' (born 5 May 1989), also known as '''Sofía Stefani''', is a Mexican author, activist, and [[political analyst]]. Her academic work examines the relationship between migration, inequality, and systems of justice, addressing the institutional mechanisms of social control associated with immigration and criminal justice policies.{{cite web |title=Immigration and the Law |url=https://uapress.arizona.edu/book/immigration-and-the-law |website=University of Arizona Press |date=2018 |access-date=16 August 2026}}{{cite web |title=Sofía Espinoza Álvarez |url=https://uapress.arizona.edu/author/sofia-espinoza-alvarez |website=University of Arizona Press |access-date=16 August 2026}} == Biography == Espinoza Álvarez was born on 5 May 1989 in Múzquiz, a municipality in the Región Carbonífera of Coahuila. In 2011 she earned a bachelor's degree in Criminal Justice from [[Sul Ross State University]] in [[Texas]], where she conducted early research on the sociological dimensions of the U.S. criminal justice system.{{cite web |title=Sul Ross State University – Criminal Justice Program |url=https://srinfo.sulross.edu |website=Sul Ross State University |access-date=7 December 2025}} She subsequently studied law at Universidad de León. In 2018, she began graduate studies in Political Analysis at the [[University of Guanajuato]].{{cite web |title=Political Analysis – University of Guanajuato |url=https://www.ugto.mx |website=University of Guanajuato |access-date=7 December 2025}} == Academic work == Since 2011 Espinoza Álvarez has participated in a research and publication program designed to provide evidence-based analysis on issues affecting Latina and [[Latino (demonym)|Latino]] populations in the United States. She has examined racial, gender, and socioeconomic inequalities in the criminal justice systems of the United States and Mexico, in relation to national and international frameworks of social control, including crime control, drug enforcement, anti-immigrant policy, and counter-terrorism measures.{{cite journal |title=Review of Immigration and the Law |journal=Western Historical Quarterly |url=https://academic.oup.com |access-date=7 December 2025}}{{cite web |title=Ethnicity and Criminal Justice in the Era of Mass Incarceration – Michigan State University |url=https://msu.edu |website=Michigan State University |access-date=7 December 2025}}{{cite web |title=Ethnicity and Criminal Justice – JSRI |url=https://jsri.msu.edu/publications/nexo/vol-xxi/no-1-fall-2017/ethnicity-and-criminal-justice-in-the-era-of-mass-incarceration |website=Michigan State University |access-date=7 December 2025}}{{cite web |title=Latino Studies – Springer Journal |url=https://link.springer.com/journal/41276 |website=Springer |access-date=7 December 2025}} In 2023 [[Academic Influence]] placed Espinoza Álvarez at No. 12 on its ranking "Influential Women in Criminal Justice From the Last 10 Years."{{cite web |title=Influential Women in Criminal Justice From the Last 10 Years |url=https://academicinfluence.com/rankings/people/women-scholars/criminal-justice |website=Academic Influence |first=James |last=Barham |date=28 July 2023 |access-date=16 August 2026}} == Publications == Espinoza Álvarez is the author of four books and academic articles published in specialized journals. Her articles include "Capital Punishment on Trial: Who Lives, Who Dies, Who Decides—A Question of Justice?" (2014) and "Neoliberalism, Criminal Justice, and Latinos: The Contours of Neoliberal Economic Thought and Policy on Criminalization" (2016).Álvarez, S. E.; Urbina, M. G. (2014). "Capital Punishment on Trial: Who Lives, Who Dies, Who Decides—A Question of Justice?" ''Criminal Law Bulletin'' 50 (2): 263–298.{{cite journal |last1=Urbina |first1=Martin Guevara |last2=Espinoza Álvarez |first2=Sofía |title=Neoliberalism, criminal justice and Latinos: The contours of neoliberal economic thought and policy on criminalization |journal=Latino Studies |volume=14 |issue=1 |pages=33–58 |year=2016 |doi=10.1057/lst.2015.55 |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1057/lst.2015.55}} ''NEXO'', the institutional journal of the Julian Samora Research Institute at [[Michigan State University]], and ''Midwest Book Review'' each reviewed her books, describing them as suited for academic libraries and professional collections.{{cite web |last=Vélez Ortiz |first=Daniel |title=Curriculum Vitae |url=https://socialwork.msu.edu/_assets/curriculum-vitaes/Daniel-Velez-Ortiz-CV-2021-03.pdf |website=Michigan State University, School of Social Work |date=April 2021 |access-date=16 August 2026 |quote=Book Review of Latino Police Officers in the United States: An Examination of Emerging Trends and Issues Edited by Martin Guevara Urbina and Sofía Espinoza Álvarez. NEXO Fall 2015.}}{{cite web |last=Martinez |first=Rubén |title=Hispanics in the U.S. Criminal Justice System, 2nd Ed. |url=https://jsri.msu.edu/publications/nexo/vol-xxiii/no-1-fall-2019/hispanics-in-the-u-s-criminal-justice-system-2nd-ed |website=Julian Samora Research Institute, Michigan State University |date=2019 |access-date=16 August 2026}}{{cite web |last=Taylor |first=John |title=Review of Hispanics in the U.S. Criminal Justice System: Ethnicity, Ideology, and Social Control |website=Midwest Book Review |url=https://www.amazon.com/Hispanics-U-S-Criminal-Justice-System/dp/0398092168 |access-date=16 August 2026}} ''Immigration and the Law'' received further attention in two peer-reviewed journals: ''[[Western Historical Quarterly]]'', published by [[Oxford University Press]], described it as bringing together historical, legal, political, and economic perspectives on contemporary migration,{{cite journal |last=Bergland |first=Betty A. |title=Immigration and the Law: Race, Citizenship, and Social Control. Edited by Sofia Espinoza Alvarez and Martin Guevara Urbina |journal=Western Historical Quarterly |volume=50 |issue=4 |page=416 |year=2019 |doi=10.1093/whq/whz074 |url=https://academic.oup.com/whq/article-abstract/50/4/416/5551437|url-access=subscription }} while the ''[[Journal of Borderlands Studies]]'' characterized it as a critical account of the structural racism and social control embedded in immigration law, policy, and enforcement.{{cite journal |last=Palander |first=Jaana |title=Immigration and the law – race, citizenship, and social control |journal=Journal of Borderlands Studies |volume=35 |issue=3 |pages=487–488 |date=18 September 2019 |doi=10.1080/08865655.2019.1665472 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/08865655.2019.1665472|url-access=subscription }} In 2022, BookAuthority ranked ''Hispanics in the U.S. Criminal Justice System'' first on its "20 Best Immigration Law Books of All Time" list.{{cite web |title=Book by Martin Urbina ranked number one |url=https://www.sulross.edu/book-by-martin-urbina-ranked-number-one/ |website=Sul Ross State |website=Google Books |publisher=Google |access-date=7 December 2025 }} == Activism and advocacy == Since 2013, Espinoza Álvarez has worked through Empower Global on migrant-rights advocacy in Mexico and the United States.{{cite web |title=Sofía Espinoza Álvarez |url=https://uapress.arizona.edu/author/sofia-espinoza-alvarez |website=University of Arizona Press |access-date=16 August 2026}} Espinoza Álvarez has written for Univision, ''El Universal'', and ''HuffPost'', and has appeared as a guest analyst on radio and television, covering migration, criminal justice, ethnic disparities, human rights, public policy, diversity, representation, and social justice in Mexico and the United States.{{cite news |title=Piden hijos de migrantes a Obama dar indulto a dreamers |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/articulo/mundo/2016/11/24/piden-hijos-de-migrantes-obama-dar-indulto-dreamers |website=El Universal |date=24 November 2016 |access-date=7 December 2025}}{{cite web |title=Articles by Sofía Espinoza Álvarez |url=https://www.huffpost.com/author/sofía-espinoza-álvarez |website=HuffPost |access-date=7 December 2025}}{{cite web |title=Crimen y castigo o el encarcelamiento masivo en las campañas presidenciales del 2020 |url=https://radiobilingue.org/es/news/crimen-y-castigo-o-el-encarcelamiento-masivo-en-las-campanas-presidenciales-del-2020 |website=Radio Bilingüe |date=2 June 2019 |access-date=16 August 2026}} === Migrant rights and immigration policy === During the 2016 U.S. presidential election cycle, Espinoza Álvarez addressed immigration policy and the protections available to migrant communities ahead of a change in presidential administration. On 31 October 2016, she published an open letter to Democratic presidential candidate [[Hillary Clinton]] in ''HuffPost'', calling for comprehensive immigration reform to be included in Clinton's platform.{{cite web |title=Dear Hillary Clinton: Dreaming in the Times of the Trump Effect |url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/hillary-clinton-the-dream-is-now-for-a-comprehensive_b_581731f0e4b08301d33e0c3e |website=HuffPost |first=Sofía |last=Espinoza Álvarez |date=31 October 2016 |access-date=16 August 2026}} Following the election, Espinoza Álvarez called for President [[Barack Obama]] to use his presidencial pardon power before leaving office as a means of protecting certain immigrants from deportation. She presented this position in a 16 November column for Univision addressing several groups of immigrants, including students, mothers, workers, "dreamers," and beneficiaries of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program.{{cite news |title=Dilema migratorio: Sí se puede perdonar a los dreamers|url=https://www.univision.com/noticias/opinion/dilema-migratorio-si-se-puede-perdonar-a-los-dreamers|website=Univision|access-date=7 December 2025}} The following day, ''Aristegui Noticias'' published an interview with her in she called on civil-society organizations and political actors to support the proposal.{{cite web |title=Indulto de Obama a migrantes impediría que Trump los deportara: activista (Video) |url=https://aristeguinoticias.com/1711/mundo/indulto-de-obama-a-migrantes-impediria-que-trump-los-deportara-activista/ |website=Aristegui Noticias |date=17 November 2016 |access-date=16 August 2026}} On 17 November, Democratic Representatives Zoe Lofgren, Lucille Roybal-Allard, and Luis Gutiérrez formally asked Obama to use his pardon power to protect DACA recipients.{{cite press release |title=Democrats call on President Obama to Protect DREAMers with Pardon |url=https://lofgren.house.gov/media/press-releases/democrats-call-president-obama-protect-dreamers-pardon |publisher=Office of Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren |date=17 November 2016 |access-date=16 August 2026}} On 24 November, organizations of children of immigrants promoted a similar petition, and the request was later reiterated by a group of 64 Democratic members of the House of Representatives.{{cite news |title=What can Obama do to help protect DREAMers from Donald Trump? |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/obama-dreamers-daca-protections-donald-trump/ |work=CBS News |date=8 December 2016 |access-date=16 August 2026}} The White House rejected the proposal's viability, stating that a presidential pardon could not confer legal status on undocumented individuals and that this power belonged to Congress. === Woman´s Rights Advocacy === On 1 April 2016, Espinoza Álvarez created a petition calling for legislation against sexual harassment in public spaces, addressed to Mexico's Secretary of the Interior, a federal senator, and the president of Mexico's National Women's Institute (Inmujeres). She subsequently promoted a second petition proposing a mobile application for the prevention of and alert system for sexual harassment, addressed to the Secretary of the Interior and the director of Mexico City's Laboratory for the City.Both petitions were integrated into the movement associated with the hashtag #NoTeCalles.{{cite web |last=Morales |first=Andrea |title=Campaña #NOteCalles contra el acoso callejero |url=https://rotativo.com.mx/metropoli/queretaro/campana-notecalles-acoso-callejero_531356_102.html |website=Rotativo |date=24 May 2016 |access-date=17 August 2026}} == References == {{Reflist}} {{Authority control|qid=Q27970753}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Espinoza Alvarez, Sofia Stefani}} [[Category:1989 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American criminologists]] [[Category:American academics of Mexican descent]] [[Category:American writers of Mexican descent]] [[Category:21st-century American women writers]] [[Category:American women academics]] [[Category:Activists for Hispanic and Latino American civil rights]] [[Category:Migration studies]] [[Category:Sul Ross State University alumni]]

'''Yuki Ito''' (born 24 October 1996) is a Japanese [[rugby union]] and [[Rugby sevens|sevens]] player. She competed for {{nwrut|Japan}} at the [[2021 Rugby World Cup]].

== Early life and career ==
Ito began practicing [[judo]] at the age of four, and also took part in [[classical ballet]] and [[gymnastics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Special Talk Session Striving to Achieve Success in the Global Arena Athletes of the Sumitomo Electric Group |url=https://sumitomoelectric.com/id/styles/v11/01 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=sumitomoelectric.com |language=en}}</ref> She participated in judo until junior high school.<ref name=":0" /> After graduating from Chikushi High School in 2015, she entered [[Nippon Sport Science University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2015-07-08 |title=2015年度 U20女子セブンズ日本代表候補メンバー・合宿スケジュール｜日本ラグビーフットボール協会 |url=https://www.rugby-japan.jp/news/2015/07/08/10635 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=www.rugby-japan.jp |language=ja}}</ref>

In 2015, she represented Japan's under-20 women's sevens team at the [[Asia Rugby]] U20 Sevens Series tournament in [[Johor Bahru]], [[Malaysia]].<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-08-16 |title=ラグビーリパブリック |url=https://rugby-rp.com/2015/08/16/woman/13332 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=rugby-rp.com |language=ja}}</ref>

==Rugby career==
She competed for {{nwrut|Japan}} in the [[2017 Women's Rugby World Cup qualifying#Asia and Oceania|2017 Rugby World Cup qualification]] rounds for Asia and Oceania in 2016.<ref name=":0" />

Ito joined [[Mie Pearls]] after graduating from [[Nippon Sport Science University]] in 2019.

In 2022, she was selected for the Japanese squad to the delayed [[2021 Rugby World Cup]] in [[New Zealand]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-16 |title=（10月16日更新) 女子日本代表ニュージーランド遠征メンバーのお知らせ｜日本ラグビーフットボール協会 |url=https://www.rugby-japan.jp/news/51520 |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=www.rugby-japan.jp |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-21 |title=Rugby World Cup 2021: Find out who will be playing in New Zealand as squads are named |url=https://www.rugbyworldcup.com/news/754167/rugby-world-cup-2021-squads |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=Women's and Men's Rugby World Cup |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Her younger brother, [[Daisuke Itō (rugby union)|Daisuke]], is also a rugby player.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-01-06 |title=「仲間と運に恵まれた」 桐蔭学園・主将伊藤大に両親声援 {{!}} スポーツ |url=https://www.kanaloco.jp/sports/entry-235550.html |url-status=live |access-date=2025-12-26 |website=カナロコ by 神奈川新聞 |language=ja}}</ref> She joined the Administration Division at Sumitomo Wiring Systems in 2019.<ref name=":0" />

'''Eriko Hirano''' (born 26 April 1992) is a Japanese [[rugby union]] player. She competed for {{nwrut|Japan}} at the [[2017 Women's Rugby World Cup]].

== Early life ==
Originally from [[Ōtsuchi, Iwate]], Hirano started playing rugby in first grade.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2020-11-22 |title=ラグビー女子15人制日本代表・平野恵里子はスペインで来秋のＷ杯へスキルアップ目指す セビージャへの移籍発表：中日スポーツ・東京中日スポーツ |url=https://www.chunichi.co.jp/article/158428 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=中日スポーツ・東京中日スポーツ |language=ja}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2015-03-10 |title=あれから４年 代表候補の平野恵里子 大学卒業「強くなって戻ってきたい」 - スポニチ Sponichi Annex スポーツ |url=https://www.sponichi.co.jp/sports/news/2015/03/10/articles/K20150310009954460.html |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=スポニチ Sponichi Annex |language=ja}}</ref> She lost her home in the [[2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami|Great East Japan Earthquake]] in 2011, which struck ten days after she graduated from Kamaishi High School.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

She graduated from [[Nippon Sport Science University]] in 2015.<ref name=":1" />

==Rugby career==
Hirano was selected to represent Japan in the women's [[Rugby sevens|sevens]] competition at the [[FISU World University Championships|World University Championships]] in 2014.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2020-10-22 |title=平野恵里子選手 ～いちばん新しい釜石ラグビーの🌸～｜🐯なかぴー |url=https://note.com/nakap_kamaishi/n/n53b99b48fcd6 |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=note（ノート） |language=ja-JP}}</ref> She joined Yokohama TKM in 2015.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Navarro |first=Dani |date=2020-11-25 |title=La internacional nipona Eriko Hirano llega al Corteva Cocos. |url=https://rugbysevilla.es/wp/la-internacional-nipona-eriko-hirano-llega-al-corteva-cocos/ |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=Rugby Sevilla |language=es}}</ref>

In May 2016, she made her international debut for the [[Japan women's national rugby union team|Sakura fifteens]] against {{nwrut|Hong Kong}} in the [[2016 Asia Rugby Women's Championship|Asian Women's Championship]].<ref name=":3" /> She scored a try in her side's 39–3 win over {{nwrut|Hong Kong}} in the first game of their home and away series.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-05-07 |title=Seven-try Japan enjoy winning start in Asia Women's Championship |url=https://www.world.rugby/news/157793/seven-try-japan-enjoy-winning-start-in-asia-womens-championship |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=www.world.rugby}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Agars |first=Sam |date=2016-05-07 |title=Hong Kong women outmuscled and outclassed by Japan in regional opener |url=https://www.scmp.com/sport/rugby/fifteens/article/1942134/hong-kong-women-outmuscled-and-outclassed-japan-asia-rugby |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}}</ref>

In 2017, she was selected in {{nwrut|Japan}}'s squad to the [[2017 Women's Rugby World Cup|Women's Rugby World Cup]] in [[Ireland]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> She had a stint in [[Australia]] in 2018, she played for the [[Warringah Rugby Club]] while studying English for six months.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-04-15 |title=Warringah Rugby Club News: Season Openers 2018 |url=https://www.pittwateronlinenews.com/Warringah-Rugby-Club-News-Season-Openers-2018.php |url-status=live |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=www.pittwateronlinenews.com}}</ref>

Hirano joined Spanish club, Corteva Cocos in 2020, in preparation for the [[2021 Rugby World Cup|Rugby World Cup]] in [[New Zealand]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> She later joined Azalea Seven in 2021.

Ollis | birth_name = Michael Harold Ollis | nickname = | birth_date = {{Birth date|1988|9|16}} | birth_place = [[New Dorp, Staten Island]], New York, U.S. | death_date = {{Death date and age|2013|8|28|1988|9|16}} | death_place = [[Forward Operating Base Ghazni]], [[Ghazni Province]], Afghanistan | burial_place = [[Cemetery of the Resurrection]], [[Pleasant Plains, Staten Island]], New York, U.S.{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/staten-island-advance-death-notices-oll/190904799/ |title=Death Notices: Ollis |newspaper=[[Staten Island Advance]] |page=A 15 |date=September 13, 2013 |accessdate=February 8, 2026 |via=newspapers.com}} | allegiance = United States | branch = [[United States Army]] | service_years = 2006–2013 | rank = [[Staff sergeant]] | service_number = | units = Company B, 2nd Battalion, [[22nd Infantry Regiment (United States)|22nd Infantry Regiment]], 1st Brigade Combat Team, [[10th Mountain Division]] | commands = | battles = [[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]] {{KIA}} | awards = {{plainlist| * [[Medal of Honor]] * [[Purple Heart]] * [[Bronze Star Medal|Bronze Star]] * [[Polish Army Medal|Polish Army Gold Medal]] }} | alma_mater = | relatives = }} '''Michael Harold Ollis''' (September 16, 1988 – August 28, 2013) was an American military [[non-commissioned officer]]. He was a [[staff sergeant]] in the [[United States Army|U.S. Army's]] [[10th Mountain Division]], awarded the [[Medal of Honor]] in 2026 for his actions on August 28, 2013, in [[Ghazni Province]], [[Afghanistan]], protecting a Polish army officer, 2nd Lt. Karol Cierpica, during a suicide bombing.{{Cite web |last=Seck |first=Hope Hodge |date=February 4, 2026 |title=Soldier who died shielding Polish ally to receive Medal of Honor |url=https://www.militarytimes.com/news/your-military/2026/02/04/soldier-who-died-shielding-polish-ally-to-receive-medal-of-honor/ |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=Military Times |language=en}} The Medal of Honor was awarded to his parents in a White House ceremony on March 2, 2026, by President Donald Trump.{{Cite web |date=2026-03-02 |title=Trump presents Medal of Honor to parents of Fort Drum soldier who blocked suicide bomber |url=https://www.nny360.com/communitynews/trump-presents-medal-of-honor-to-parents-of-fort-drum-soldier-who-blocked-suicide-bomber/article_fe9cfe7c-5200-5a38-bbab-f6f9432fc619.html |access-date=2026-03-03 |website=NNY360 |language=en}} == Army career == Ollis enlisted in the Army at age 17 after graduation from [[Michael J. Petrides School]] where he attended [[Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps]].{{Cite web |title=Around and About Fort Drum: Staff Sgt. Michael H. Ollis Weapons Training Center |url=https://www.army.mil/article/277712/around_and_about_fort_drum_staff_sgt_michael_h_ollis_weapons_training_center |first=Mike |last=Strasser |website=army.mil |date=July 1, 2024 |access-date=February 5, 2026 |language=en}} He attended basic training at [[Fort Benning]] in Georgia{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/staten-island-advance-ollis/190905727/ |title=Ollis |newspaper=[[Staten Island Advance]] |page=A 29 |date=March 18, 2007 |accessdate=February 8, 2026 |via=newspapers.com}} and his first assignment after training was [[Baumholder]], [[Germany]], with the [[1st Armored Division (United States)|1st Armored Division]]. Ollis was deployed to Iraq in 2008. He was next stationed at [[Fort Campbell]] in Kentucky with the [[101st Airborne Division]] where he completed [[United States Army Air Assault School|Air Assault School]]. He was deployed to [[Kandahar Province]] in Afghanistan during [[Operation Dragon Strike]]. After that deployment, Ollis was transferred to [[Fort Drum]] and the [[10th Mountain Division]]. In 2012, he completed both [[United States Army Airborne School|Airborne School]] and [[Ranger School]]. At the time of his death, Ollis was a member of the 2nd Battalion, 22nd Infantry Regiment, 1st Brigade Combat Team, 10th Mountain Division.{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/staten-island-advance-new-dorp-mourns-it/190906038/ |title=New Dorp mourns its soldier-son |first1=Jullian |last1=Jorgensen |first2=Marjorie |last2=Hack |newspaper=[[Staten Island Advance]] |page=A 12 |date=August 31, 2013 |accessdate=February 8, 2026 |via=newspapers.com}} === Medal of Honor action === Ollis was killed on August 28, 2013, in [[Ghazni Province|Ghazni province]], [[Afghanistan]], while protecting 2nd Lt. Karol Cierpica of the [[Polish Land Forces]] during a [[suicide attack]].{{Cite web |last=Axelrod |first=Scott R. |date=February 4, 2026 |title=Staten Island’s hero soldier, Michael Ollis, will receive the Medal of Honor |url=https://www.silive.com/news/2026/02/staten-islands-hero-soldier-michael-ollis-awarded-medal-of-honor.html |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=silive |language=en}} Cierpica was also wounded in the attack. Ollis and his unit were attempting to repel an attack by 10 [[Taliban]] insurgents and a car bomber who had breached their base's wall.{{Cite web |last=Balsamini |first=Dean |date=September 18, 2013 |title=Report: Staten Island soldier Michael Ollis died while protecting another soldier from a suicide bomber (photos) |url=https://www.silive.com/news/2013/09/army_times_staten_island_soldi.html |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=silive |language=en}} Ollis and Cierpica engaged the insurgents without any [[personal protective equipment]] and armed only with their rifles. Ollis was originally awarded a [[Silver Star]] posthumously for his actions. That award was later upgraded to the [[Distinguished Service Cross (United States)|Distinguished Service Cross]],{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/staten-island-advance-posthumous-militar/190906623/ |title=Posthumous military award for Island hero |first=Caitlin |last=Della Rocca |newspaper=[[Staten Island Advance]] |page=A1 |date=December 24, 2018 |accessdate=February 9, 2026 |via=newspapers.com}} which was formally presented to his parents in June 2019.{{cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/staten-island-advance-a-hero-for-our-gen/190906492/ |title=A hero for our generation |first=Maura |last=Grunlund |newspaper=[[Staten Island Advance]] |page=A1 |date=June 9, 2019 |accessdate=February 9, 2026 |via=newspapers.com}} Rep. [[Nicole Malliotakis]] (R-Staten Island) of [[New York's 11th congressional district]] was among many advocates,{{Cite press release |date=February 3, 2026 |title=Malliotakis Applauds President Trump’s Decision to Award Medal of Honor to Staten Island Hero Michael Ollis |url=http://malliotakis.house.gov/media/press-releases/malliotakis-applauds-president-trumps-decision-award-medal-honor-staten-island |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=malliotakis.house.gov |language=en}} along with the [[American Legion]] and the SSG Michael Ollis Freedom Foundation, for Ollis to be awarded the [[Medal of Honor]].{{Cite web |last=Schogol |first=Jeff |date=February 4, 2026 |title=Soldier who died saving Polish officer in Afghanistan to receive Medal of Honor, family says |url=https://taskandpurpose.com/news/army-michael-ollis-medal-of-honor/ |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=Task & Purpose |language=en-US}} President [[Donald Trump]] approved the Medal of Honor for Ollis on February 3, 2026.{{Cite web |last=Baehr |first=Jasmine |date=February 3, 2026 |title=White House approves Medal of Honor for fallen Army Staff Sgt Michael Ollis after yearslong push |url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/white-house-approves-medal-honor-fallen-army-staff-sgt-michael-ollis-after-years-long-push |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=Fox News |language=en-US}} The Polish Defense Ministry issued a statement February 5, 2026, stating, "In 2013 in Afghanistan, he gave his life, shielding the body of our Capt. Karol Cierpica during a terrorist attack. This story is a symbol of the unbreakable bond that connects Poland and the United States. Our nations serve shoulder to shoulder, defending shared values, freedom and democracy. The heroism of Sergeant Ollis reminds us that the alliance is not just words."{{Cite web |last=Peteley |first=Luke |date=2026-02-05 |title=Poland hails Medal of Honor for Staten Island soldier who gave his life to save one of its own |url=https://www.silive.com/news/2026/02/poland-hails-medal-of-honor-for-staten-island-soldier-who-gave-his-life-to-save-one-of-its-own.html |access-date=2026-02-14 |website=silive |language=en}} == Medal of Honor citation == Staff Sergeant Michael H. Ollis distinguished himself by acts of gallantry and intrepidity above and beyond the call of duty on 28 August 2013, while serving as an Infantryman with Company B, 2d Battalion, [[22nd Infantry Regiment (United States)|22d Infantry Regiment]], 1st Brigade Combat Team, [[10th Mountain Division]] in Afghanistan. On this date, a complex enemy attack involving multiple vehicle-borne improvised explosive devices, suicide vests, indirect fire and small arms fire was launched against [[Forward Operating Base Ghazni]]. Staff Sergeant Ollis ordered his fellow soldiers who were located in a building to move to bunkers to shield themselves from enemy fire. After accounting for his soldiers, he reentered the building to check for any casualties and then moved toward the enemy force that had penetrated the perimeter of the Forward Operating Base. Staff Sergeant Ollis located a Coalition Forces Officer and together they moved toward the point of attack without their personal protection equipment and armed with only their rifles. Upon reaching the attack point he and his comrade linked up with other friendly forces and began a coordinated effort to repulse the enemy from the airfield and adjacent buildings. While under continuous small arms, indirect and rocket propelled grenade fire, Staff Sergeant Ollis and his comrades moved from position to position engaging the enemy with accurate and effective fire. Fighting along the perimeter of the Forward Operating Base, an insurgent came around a corner, whom Staff Sergeant Ollis immediately engaged with three rifle rounds. With complete disregard for his own safety, Staff Sergeant Ollis positioned himself between the insurgent and the Coalition Forces Officer who had been wounded in both legs and was unable to walk. Staff Sergeant Ollis fired on the insurgent and incapacitated him, but as he approached the downed insurgent, the insurgent’s suicide vest detonated and mortally wounded him. Staff Sergeant Ollis’ exceptional courage and complete disregard of personal safety were in keeping with the highest traditions of military service and reflect great credit upon him, his unit, and the United States Army.{{Cite web |title=Michael Harold Ollis {{!}} War on Terrorism (Afghanistan) {{!}} U.S. Army {{!}} Medal of Honor Recipient |url=https://www.cmohs.org/recipients/michael-h-ollis |access-date=2026-05-04 |website=Congressional Medal of Honor Society |language=en}} == Distinguished Service Cross citation == Department of the Army, General Orders No. 2019-32 (October 16, 2019):{{Cite web |title=Michael Ollis |url=https://valor.militarytimes.com/recipient/recipient-90902/ |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=Hall of Valor: Medal of Honor, Silver Star, U.S. Military Awards |language=en-US}}
The President of the United States of America, authorized by Act of Congress July 9, 1918, takes pride in presenting the Distinguished Service Cross (Posthumously) to Staff Sergeant Michael Harold Ollis, United States Army, for extraordinary heroism while engaged in an action against an enemy of the United States while serving as an Infantryman with Company B, 2d Battalion, 22d Infantry Regiment, 1st Brigade Combat Team, 10th Mountain Division (Light), in combat operation in support of [[Operation Enduring Freedom|Operation ENDURING FREEDOM]] on August 28, 2013, in Afghanistan. When a complex enemy attack involving vehicle-borne [[improvised explosive device]]s, [[suicide vest]]s, [[indirect fire]], and [[small arms]] fire against [[Forward Operating Base Ghazni]] began, Staff Sergeant Ollis ordered his fellow Soldiers who were located in a building to move to [[bunker]]s to shield themselves from fire. After accounting for his Soldiers, he reentered the building to check for any casualties and then moved toward the enemy force which had penetrated the perimeter of the forward operating base. Staff Sergeant Ollis located a [[Participants in Operation Enduring Freedom|Coalition Forces]] Officer and together they moved toward the point of attack without their [[personal protection equipment]] and armed only with their rifles. Upon reaching the attack point he and his comrade linked up with other friendly forces and began a coordinated effort to repulse the enemy from the airfield and adjacent buildings. While under continuous small arms, indirect, and [[Rocket-propelled grenade|rocket propelled grenade]] fires. Staff Sergeant Ollis and his comrades moved from position to position engaging the enemy with accurate and effective fire. While fighting along the perimeter of the forward operating base, an insurgent came around a corner and immediately engaged them with small arms fire. With complete disregard for his own safety. Staff Sergeant Ollis positioned himself between the insurgent and the Coalition Forces Officer who had been wounded in both legs and was unable to walk. Staff Sergeant Ollis fired on the insurgent and incapacitated him, but as he approached the insurgent, the insurgent’s suicide vest detonated mortally wounding him. Staff Sergeant Ollis’ actions are in keeping with the highest traditions of the military service and reflect great credit upon himself, the 1st Brigade Combat Team, 10th Mountain Division, and the United States Army.

Ollis Weapons Training Center at [[Fort Drum]], New York, home of the 10th Mountain Division.{{Cite web |title=Around and About Fort Drum: Staff Sgt. Michael H. Ollis Weapons Training Center |url=https://www.dvidshub.net/image/8508839/around-and-about-fort-drum-staff-sgt-michael-h-ollis-weapons-training-center |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=DVIDS |language=en}} The SSG Michael H. Ollis Warrior Grill at [[Camp Kościuszko]], [[Poland]], was also named for him.{{Cite web |title=A Tribute to Sacrifice: The Enduring Impact of SSG Michael Ollis in Poland |url=https://www.dvidshub.net/image/8442200/tribute-sacrifice-enduring-impact-ssg-michael-ollis-poland |access-date=February 5, 2026 |website=DVIDS |language=en}} The Staff Sgt. '''Rodrigo de Olivera Donado''' (born 20 December 1994) is a Uruguayan professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional de Honduras|Liga Nacional]] club [[F.C. Motagua|Motagua]].

== Career ==
De Olivera developed at the [[Danubio F.C.|Danubio]] academy before playing for [[Montevideo Wanderers F.C.|Montevideo Wanderers]] and [[Montevideo City Torque]]. He left Montevideo City Torque for Chilean club [[A.C. Barnechea|Barnechea]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1=González |first1=Christian |title=¿Barnechea City? El rocambolesco acuerdo que convierte a los huaicocheros en ‘partner’ de los dueños del Manchester City |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/barnechea-city-el-rocambolesco-acuerdo-que-convierte-a-los-huaicocheros-en-partner-de-los-duenos-del-manchester-city/PHWSZO4HBRBUBISUPVHFJT33OU/ |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=[[La Tercera]] |date=1 April 2021 |language=Spanish |trans-title=Barnechea City? The bizarre deal that makes the Huaicocheros "partners" with the owners of Manchester City}}</ref>

De Olivera moved to [[Juticalpa F.C.|Juticalpa]] of Honduras in 2023, then playing in the second-tier [[Honduran Liga Nacional de Ascenso|Liga de Ascenso]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Varela |first1=Reniery |title=Rodrigo de Olivera sueña con ser campeón con Juticalpa FC, pero asegura que no son favoritos al título |url=https://vipdeportes.com/rodrigo-de-olivera-suena-con-ser-campeon-con-juticalpa-fc-pero-asegura-que-no-son-favoritos-al-titulo/ |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=VIP Deportes |date=29 November 2023 |language=Spanish |trans-title=Rodrigo de Olivera dreams of becoming a champion with Juticalpa FC, but asserts that they are not favorites for the title}}</ref> He helped Juticalpa avoid relegation from the [[Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional de Honduras|Liga Nacional]] and, after being released by the club, joined league rivals [[Olancho FC|Olancho]] in May 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Suazo |first1=Luis |title=Rodrigo de Olivera encuentra equipo en Liga Nacional tras salvarse del descenso |url=https://www.deportestvc.com/mas/claro-impulsa-el-talento-juvenil-con-una-nueva-edicion-de-la-super-liga-claro-internacional |access-date=7 May 2026 |work={{ill|Deportes TVC|es}} |date=29 May 2025 |language=Spanish |trans-title=Rodrigo de Olivera has found a new club in the National League after avoiding relegation}}</ref> For Olancho, he scored 19 goals in the 2025 [[Apertura]] of the Liga Nacional, breaking a 56-year-old record for goals scored by a foreign player in a split season of the Honduran league and equalling the record for goals scored by any player in the same setting.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Vindel |first1=Christian |title=Rodrigo de Olivera rompe récord de 56 años en Honduras e iguala otro |url=https://www.laprensa.hn/deportes/rodrigo-olivera-historia-rompe-record-56-anos-iguala-otro-liga-nacional-OI28756282 |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=[[La Prensa (Honduras)]] |date=28 December 2025 |language=Spanish |trans-title=Rodrigo de Olivera breaks a 56-year-old record in Honduras and equals another}}</ref> In January 2026 [[F.C. Motagua|Motagua]] announced the signing of De Olivera.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Figueroa |first1=Mario |title=¡Fin de la novela! Motagua oficializa el fichaje del delantero uruguayo Rodrigo de Olivera |url=https://www.diez.hn/liganacionaldehonduras/motagua-oficializa-el-fichaje-del-delantero-uruguayo-rodrigo-de-olivera-CL29115698 |access-date=7 May 2026 |work=[[Diez (Honduras)]] |date=29 January 2026 |language=Spanish |trans-title=The saga is over! Motagua have officially announced the signing of Uruguayan striker Rodrigo de Olivera}}</ref>

'''Olatz Rivera Olmedo''' (born 7 October 1996) is a Spanish [[Referee (association football)|football referee]] from [[Bilbao]] who officiates in the [[Liga F]], Spain's women's top division.<ref>{{cite web |title=La colegiada bilbaina Olatz Rivera dirigirá la final de Copa entre Barça y Atlético de Madrid |trans-title=Bilbao referee Olatz Rivera will officiate the Cup final between Barça and Atlético de Madrid |url=https://www.naiz.eus/en/info/noticia/20260511/la-colegiada-bilbaina-olatz-rivera-dirigira-la-final-de-copa-femenina-entre-barca-y-atletico |website=Naiz |language=es |date=11 May 2026 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> A [[UEFA]] Elite and [[FIFA International Referees List|FIFA international]] referee, she was promoted to UEFA's Elite category in December 2024,<ref>{{cite web |title=La árbitra Olatz Rivera Olmedo asciende a la categoría UEFA Élite |trans-title=Referee Olatz Rivera Olmedo is promoted to the UEFA Elite category |url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/la-arbitra-olatz-rivera-olmedo-asciende-la-categoria-uefa-elite |website=Real Federación Española de Fútbol |language=es |date=20 December 2024 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> making Spain one of only four countries, alongside Portugal, Italy and Romania, to have two women in that category.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olatz Rivera Olmedo asciende a la categoría UEFA Élite |trans-title=Olatz Rivera Olmedo is promoted to the UEFA Elite category |url=https://www.cope.es/programas/tiempo-de-juego/noticias/olatz-rivera-olmedo-asciende-categoria-uefa-elite-20241220_3066983.html |website=COPE |language=es |date=20 December 2024 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> She has refereed two [[Supercopa de España Femenina]] finals, the 2026 [[Copa de la Reina]] final, a [[UEFA Women's Euro 2025]] group match and the [[2025 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup]] final, and in 2026 she became the second woman to officiate in Spanish men's professional football.<ref>{{cite web |title=Un nuevo árbitro vizcaino para la Primera División |trans-title=A new Biscayan referee for the First Division |url=https://www.deia.eus/futbol/2026/06/23/arbitro-vizcaino-primera-division-futbol-11235251.html |website=Deia |language=es |date=23 June 2026 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
 
== Early life and refereeing beginnings ==
 
Rivera was born in Bilbao, in the [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque]] province of [[Biscay]], on 7 October 1996. She played football before turning to officiating and took up refereeing as a teenager, making her debut in the women's top flight at about the age of 20; she gave up playing once she was promoted to that level. Away from the pitch she trained as a computer engineer and competes in [[triathlon]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Olatz Rivera: el arbitraje femenino español se abre camino |trans-title=Olatz Rivera: Spanish women's refereeing makes its way |url=https://yosoynoticia.es/general/olatz-rivera-el-arbitraje-femenino-espanol-se-abre-camino |website=Yo Soy Noticia |language=es |date=16 November 2023 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
 
== Women's football ==
 
Rivera reached the top category of Spanish women's football in 2017 and became a UEFA international referee in 2022, joining the body's second international category.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rivera Olmedo arbitrará la final Barcelona-Real Madrid, con Huerta de Aza en el VAR |trans-title=Rivera Olmedo will referee the Barcelona–Real Madrid final, with Huerta de Aza on VAR |url=https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2025/01/24/rivera-olmedo-arbitrara-la-final-barcelona-real-madrid-con-huerta-de-aza-en-el-var/ |website=Infobae |language=es |date=24 January 2025 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> With her promotion to the UEFA Elite category in December 2024 she joined [[Marta Huerta de Aza]] among Spain's elite officials, having belonged to UEFA's second international tier since 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=La internacional Olatz Rivera Olmedo se incorpora a la categoría élite de UEFA |trans-title=International referee Olatz Rivera Olmedo joins UEFA's elite category |url=https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2024/12/20/la-internacional-olatz-rivera-olmedo-se-incorpora-a-la-categoria-elite-de-uefa/ |website=Infobae |language=es |date=20 December 2024 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> She has also officiated league ''[[Women's Clásico|Clásicos]]'' between [[FC Barcelona Femení|Barcelona]] and [[Real Madrid Femenino|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Olatz Rivera Olmedo, árbitra del Clásico Femenino |trans-title=Olatz Rivera Olmedo, referee of the women's Clásico |url=https://iusport.com/art/137701/olatz-rivera-olmedo-arbitra-del-clasico-femenino |website=Iusport |language=es |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
 
Her first Supercopa de España final came in 2024, when Barcelona beat [[Levante UD Femenino|Levante UD]] 7-0.<ref>{{cite web |title=El Levante UD se ve superado por el FC Barcelona (7-0) en la final de la Supercopa Femenina |trans-title=Levante UD are overcome by FC Barcelona (7-0) in the women's Supercopa final |url=https://www.levanteud.com/noticias/el-levante-ud-se-ve-superado-por-el-fc-barcelona-7-0-en-la-final-de-la-supercopa-femenina |website=Levante UD |language=es |date=20 January 2024 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> On 26 January 2025 she refereed her second Supercopa final, between Barcelona and Real Madrid at the [[Estadio Municipal de Butarque]] in [[Leganés]]; it was her fourth Clásico since reaching the elite.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vivimos con Olatz Rivera la previa a la final de la Supercopa |trans-title=We experience the build-up to the Supercopa final with Olatz Rivera |url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/vivimos-con-olatz-rivera-la-previa-la-final-de-la-supercopa |website=Real Federación Española de Fútbol |language=es |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
 
In May 2026 the Technical Committee of Referees chose Rivera to officiate the [[Copa de la Reina]] final between Barcelona and [[Atlético Madrid Femenino|Atlético de Madrid]] at the [[Estadio de Gran Canaria]], the first Copa de la Reina final of her career; Marta Huerta de Aza acted as fourth official.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olatz Rivera, árbitra de la final de la Copa de la Reina |trans-title=Olatz Rivera, referee of the Copa de la Reina final |url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/olatz-rivera-arbitra-de-la-final-de-la-copa-de-la-reina |website=Real Federación Española de Fútbol |language=es |date=11 May 2026 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
 
== International appointments ==
 
Rivera made her debut at a senior international tournament at [[UEFA Women's Euro 2025]] in Switzerland, where she was appointed to the Group C match between [[Poland women's national football team|Poland]] and [[Denmark women's national football team|Denmark]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Olatz Rivera debutará en la Eurocopa con el Polonia - Dinamarca |trans-title=Olatz Rivera will make her European Championship debut with Poland–Denmark |url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/olatz-rivera-debutara-en-la-eurocopa-con-el-polonia-dinamarca |website=Real Federación Española de Fútbol |language=es |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> She was accompanied by assistant referee Eliana Fernández, with [[Guillermo Cuadra Fernández]] on the [[video assistant referee]].<ref>{{cite web |title=La árbitra española Olatz Rivera debutará en la Eurocopa de Suiza con el Polonia - Dinamarca |trans-title=Spanish referee Olatz Rivera will make her debut at the Switzerland Euro with Poland–Denmark |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2025/07/10/la-arbitra-espanola-olatz-rivera-debutara-en-la-eurocopa-de-suiza-con-el-polonia-dinamarca/ |website=Infobae |language=es |date=10 July 2025 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> The match was described in the Spanish press as a milestone for the presence of women in international refereeing.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olatz Rivera debuta en la Eurocopa dirigiendo el Polonia-Dinamarca |trans-title=Olatz Rivera debuts at the Euro officiating Poland–Denmark |url=https://www.elindependiente.com/deportes/futbol/2025/07/10/olatz-rivera-debuta-en-la-eurocopa-dirigiendo-el-polonia-dinamarca/ |website=El Independiente |language=es |date=10 July 2025 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
 
Later that year, FIFA designated Rivera to referee the final of the [[2025 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup]] in [[Rabat]], Morocco, again with Eliana Fernández as her assistant.<ref>{{cite web |title=La árbitra española Olatz Rivera, designada por FIFA para dirigir la final del Mundial Sub-17 femenino |trans-title=Spanish referee Olatz Rivera designated by FIFA to officiate the women's U-17 World Cup final |url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/la-arbitra-espanola-olatz-rivera-designada-por-fifa-para-dirigir-la-final-del-mundial-sub |website=Real Federación Española de Fútbol |language=es |date=6 November 2025 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> The final, played on 8 November 2025, was contested by [[North Korea women's national under-17 football team|North Korea]] and the [[Netherlands women's national under-17 football team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web |title=La española Olatz Rivera arbitrará la final del Mundial Femenino sub-17 en Marruecos |trans-title=Spaniard Olatz Rivera will referee the women's U-17 World Cup final in Morocco |url=https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2025/11/06/la-espanola-olatz-rivera-arbitrara-la-final-del-mundial-femenino-sub-17-en-marruecos/ |website=Infobae |language=es |date=6 November 2025 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
 
== Men's football ==
 
Rivera also officiates in men's football. She made her debut in the [[Segunda Federación]] in 2023 and reached the [[Primera Federación]] in 2024, where she became the first woman to referee an official first-team match of [[CD Tenerife]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Olatz Rivera Olmedo, primera mujer que arbitrará un partido oficial del Tenerife |trans-title=Olatz Rivera Olmedo, the first woman to referee an official Tenerife match |url=https://www.eldiario.es/canariasahora/Deportes/futbol/olatz-rivera-olmedo-primera-mujer-arbitrara-partido-oficial-cd-tenerife_1_12768146.html |website=elDiario.es |language=es |date=14 November 2025 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref> In June 2026 she was promoted to the [[Segunda División]], becoming only the second woman to officiate in Spanish men's professional football, after Marta Huerta de Aza.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sánchez |first=Pablo |title=Los cuatro árbitros señalados por la RFEF que descienden a Segunda |trans-title=The four referees marked by the RFEF who drop to the Second Division |url=https://www.eldesmarque.com/futbol/liga-1a-division/20260622/arbitros-senalados-rfef-descenso-laliga-hypermotion_18_019518069.html |website=ElDesmarque |language=es |date=22 June 2026 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>
 
== Honours and recognition ==
 
Rivera was named best female referee of the year at [[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'s women's sport awards (Premios del Deporte Femenino) in 2023, the second time she received the distinction; that same year she had also been recognised as the best [[Liga F]] referee of the season at the Vicente Acebedo Awards given by the Spanish Football Federation's Technical Committee of Referees.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olatz Rivera, mejor árbitra del año según el diario deportivo Marca |trans-title=Olatz Rivera, best referee of the year according to the sports daily Marca |url=https://rfef.es/es/noticias/olatz-rivera-mejor-arbitra-del-ano-segun-el-diario-deportivo-marca |website=Real Federación Española de Fútbol |language=es |date=2 November 2023 |access-date=25 June 2026}}</ref>

[[File:Caroline Francischini crop.jpg|thumb|Francischini in 2006]]

'''Caroline Capovila Francischini''' (born April 4, 1989) is a Brazilian model. She walked for the fashion houses [[Salvatore Ferragamo (company)|Ferragamo]], [[Gucci]], [[Fendi]], and [[Max Mara]], and worked for [[Victoria's Secret]] and [[Calvin Klein (fashion house)|Calvin Klein]]. She is among the models with the most appearances at [[São Paulo Fashion Week]].

== Biography ==
Born in [[Valinhos]], she began her modeling career at the age of thirteen after winning the Riachuelo Mega Model,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sampaio |first=Ana Ligia |date=2008-11-13 |title=A BRINCALHONA CAROL FRANCISCHINI CONQUISTA NY |url=https://caras.com.br/arquivo/a-brincalhona-carol-francischini-conquista-ny.phtml |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=CARAS Brasil |language=pt-BR}}</ref> a national modeling contest. She left elementary school and moved to [[New York City|New York]], where she walked for brands such as [[Cartier (jeweler)|Cartier]], [[Diesel (company)|Diesel]], and the designer [[Vera Wang]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-31 |title=Quem é Carol Francischini? Modelo expôs agressão do irmão nas redes |url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/pop/quem-e-carol-francischini-modelo-expos-agressao-do-irmao-nas-redes/ |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=CNN Brasil |language=pt-BR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sampaio |first=Ana Lígia |date=2006-09-20 |title=BRASIL SE CONSAGRA NA SEMANA DE MODA DE NY |url=https://caras.com.br/arquivo/brasil-se-consagra-na-semana-de-moda-de-ny.phtml |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=CARAS Brasil |language=pt-BR}}</ref> She appeared on the cover of the Brazilian and Argentine editions of ''[[Elle (magazine)|Elle]]'' and did editorials for ''[[Nylon (magazine)|Nylon]]'' and ''[[Teen Vogue]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Caroline Francischini - Fashion Model {{!}} Models {{!}} Photos, Editorials & Latest News {{!}} The FMD |url=https://www.fashionmodeldirectory.com/models/caroline_francischini/ |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=The FMD - FashionModelDirectory.com}}</ref> She also worked in advertising campaigns for [[Tommy Hilfiger (company)|Tommy Hilfiger]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Caroline Francischini - Model |url=https://models.com/models/caroline-francischini |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=MODELS.com}}</ref>

In 2009, she made an appearance on the television program ''[[TV Fama]]''. She had a daughter in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carol Francischini fala sobre a criação da filha: "Ela não sente falta da figura paterna" |url=https://epoca.globo.com/sociedade/bruno-astuto/noticia/2017/09/carol-francischini-fala-sobre-criacao-da-filha-ela-nao-sente-falta-da-figura-paterna.html |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=Época}}</ref> In 2013, she walked at [[Rio Fashion Week|Fashion Rio]] for the Brazilian fashion brand Oh, Boy!.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-08-24 |title=Carol Francischini desfila no Rio |url=https://revistaquem.globo.com/Fashion-Rio-Verao-20132014/noticia/2013/04/carol-francischini-desfila-em-sp.html |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=Quem - Globo |language=pt-br}}</ref> In 2016, she participated in São Paulo Fashion Week, walking for the stylist [[Amir Slama]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-10-26 |title=Carol Francischini desfila para Amir Slama no SPFW |url=https://vogue.globo.com/celebridades/noticia/2016/10/carol-francischini-desfila-com-exclusividade-para-amir-slama-no-spfw.ghtml |access-date=2026-07-11 |website=Vogue |language=pt-br}}</ref>

In re-enactments, she played the silent role of an anonymous young woman in the 1960s in ''[[Salut les copains (radio program)|SLC Salut les copains]].'' === New roles and chronicles === In April 2014, Constance appeared on the television channel [[Téva]] in the short program ''Constance ou la gueule de l'emploi''.{{Cite web |last=Montarou |first=Maël |date=April 22, 2014 |title=Constance ou la gueule de l'emploi : le programme très court mais très bon de Téva (VIDEO) |url=https://www.programme.tv/news/videos/100705-constance-ou-la-gueule-de-lemploi-le-programme-tres-court-mais-tres-bon-teva-video/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.programme.tv%2Fnews%2Fvideos%2F100705-constance-ou-la-gueule-de-lemploi-le-programme-tres-court-mais-tres-bon-teva-video%2F |archive-date=November 5, 2019 |access-date=July 15, 2026 |website=programme.tv}} From {{date||novembre|2017}}, she has a column in the show ''Par Jupiter !'' on France Inter.{{Cite web |date=August 3, 1985 |title=Constance Pittard biographie, news, photos, vidéos et avis |url=https://tv-programme.com/constance-pittard-people-p6006270cc7864 |access-date=July 15, 2026 |website=tv-programme.com |language=fr}} On August 28, 2018, she led a column named ''Parlons Balcon, Parlons Nichons'' (''Let's Talk Balcony, Let's Talk Tits)'', related to her regret that [[breastfeeding]] women in public spaces is regularly a scandal. She denounced the "moralizing puritans"{{Cite web |date=August 28, 2018 |title=Parlons balcon, parlons nichons |url=https://www.radiofrance.fr/franceinter/podcasts/la-chronique-de-constance/parlons-balcon-parlons-nichons-6844009 |access-date=July 15, 2026 |website=France Inter |language=fr}} and concluded her speech [[topless]] to illustrate her point.{{Cite web |date=August 29, 2018 |title=L'humoriste Constance se met seins nus en pleine chronique sur France Inter |url=https://www.20minutes.fr/arts-stars/medias/2327511-20180829-france-inter-humoriste-constance-met-seins-nus-denoncer-puritains-moralisateurs |access-date=July 15, 2026 |website=20 Minutes |language=fr}}{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6U6ZcdVl7JA |title=Parlons balcon, parlons nichons – La chronique de Constance |date=August 28, 2018 |last=France Inter |access-date=July 15, 2026 |via=YouTube}} This column caused a [[media frenzy]]. On March 24, 2025, she made her first appearance as a member in the show ''[[Les Grosses Têtes]]'' hosted by [[Laurent Ruquier]] on [[RTL Lëtzebuerg|RTL]].{{Cite web |date=March 24, 2025 |title=VIDÉO – "Les Grosses Têtes" : l'humoriste Constance fait sa première ! |url=https://www.rtl.fr/culture/medias-people/video-les-grosses-tetes-l-humoriste-constance-fait-sa-premiere-7900486304 |access-date=July 15, 2026 |website=RTL.fr |language=fr-FR}} === Burnout syndrome and depression, then a new show === At the end of 2021, Constance, who suffered from a [[Occupational burnout|burnout]], suspended her tour and ceased all activity. '''Akinori Wase''' ({{langx|ja|早稲 昭範}}; born 8 September 1985), also known as '''WASSE''', is a Japanese [[teqball]] player and sports administrator. A former professional [[freestyle football]] performer, he began playing teqball in 2017 and has represented Japan at international competitions. He is the president of the Japan Teqball Association and won a silver medal in mixed doubles at the [[2026 Asian Games]] with [[Yuina Sakamoto]].<ref name="JOC">{{cite web
|title=早稲 昭範
|url=https://www.joc.or.jp/athletes/waseakinori/index.html
|publisher=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]]
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="JOCInterview">{{cite web
|title=ギネス記録保持者からテックボールのパイオニアへ。自国開催のアジア大会で目指す「金メダル」と普及への情熱
|url=https://www.joc.or.jp/article/teqball_260824.html
|publisher=[[Japanese Olympic Committee]]
|date=24 August 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

== Career ==

Wase was born in [[Osaka Prefecture]] and graduated from [[Kyoto Sangyo University]] in 2008 with a degree in economics. Before taking up teqball, he was a professional freestyle football performer and became known for performing football juggling tricks. He also held a Guinness World Record for juggling while lying down.<ref name="JOCInterview"/><ref name="KyotoSU">{{cite web
|title=卒業生が金メダル！テックボール世界大会で優勝！
|url=https://www.kyoto-su.ac.jp/news/news-001936.html
|publisher=[[Kyoto Sangyo University]]
|date=13 November 2025
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

Wase began playing teqball in 2017 after being recommended to the Japanese Teqball Association because of his freestyle football background. He initially expected the skills to transfer directly from freestyle football, but found that teqball required different techniques and ball control.<ref name="JOCInterview"/>

Wase competed for Japan at the first World Teqball Championships and continued to represent the country at international competitions. He became one of the leading Japanese players in the sport and, from 2020, served as the representative director of the Japan Teqball Association, working on the development and promotion of teqball in Japan.<ref name="JOCInterview"/>

In September 2025, Wase and [[Yuina Sakamoto]] won the bronze medal in mixed doubles at the Teqball World Series event in Beijing. It was the first time that a Japanese pair had reached the podium at an international teqball world-series event. Wase also partnered with Seiya Arai in the men's doubles, where they reached the round of 16.<ref name="JTFBeijing">{{cite web
|title=TEQBALL国際大会で日本代表が世界3位を獲得！！
|url=https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000054.000040360.html
|publisher=Japan Teqball Association
|date=24 September 2025
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

In October 2025, Wase and Arai won the men's doubles title at the Beach International Teqball Cup in [[Wanning]], [[Hainan]], China. The victory was Japan's first world title in beach teqball. Wase also reached the quarterfinals of the men's singles competition.<ref name="BeachCup">{{cite web
|title=テックボール日本代表が世界一を獲得！
|url=https://teqball.jp/
|publisher=Japan Teqball Association
|date=2025
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref><ref name="KyotoSU"/>

At the Beach Teqball World Tour event in Wanning in November 2025, Wase won the silver medal in men's singles and the bronze medal in men's doubles with Arai.<ref name="BeachTour">{{cite web
|title=ビーチテックボールワールドツアー2025にて世界14か国のトップ選手が集結、日本の早稲昭範選手がシングルスカテゴリで世界2位を獲得！
|url=https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000000059.000040360.html
|publisher=Japan Teqball Association
|date=23 December 2025
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

At the 2025 Teqball World Championships, Wase and Sakamoto reached the quarterfinals of the mixed doubles event, while Wase and Arai reached the round of 16 in men's doubles.<ref name="JTFWorld2025">{{cite web
|title=テックボール歴史的快挙
|url=https://teqball.jp/category/%E6%9C%AA%E5%88%86%E9%A1%9E/
|publisher=Japan Teqball Association
|date=31 December 2025
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>

Wase was selected to represent Japan at the [[Teqball at the 2026 Asian Games|2026 Asian Games]] in Aichi-Nagoya in men's singles and mixed doubles. He partnered Sakamoto in the mixed doubles event.<ref name="JOC"/><ref name="JapanTeam2026">{{cite web
|title=テックボール日本代表決定
|url=https://mainichikirei.jp/prtimes/article/20260902prt00m100000158a.html
|publisher=Mainichi Kirei
|date=2 September 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref> In the mixed doubles competition, Wase and Sakamoto defeated the Iraqi pair of Abdulrahman Ahmed Radhi and Samar Shakir Aben in the semifinals to reach the gold-medal match. Their victory guaranteed Japan a medal in teqball on its Asian Games debut.<ref name="OCAsemi">{{cite news
|title=Japan's mixed doubles teqball team give fans plenty to cheer about
|url=https://oca.asia/news/7905-japans-mixed-doubles-teqball-team-give-fans-plenty-to-cheer-about.html
|publisher=[[Olympic Council of Asia]]
|date=19 September 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref> In the mixed doubles final on 20 September 2026, Wase and Sakamoto lost to Thailand's Phakpong Dejaroen and Suphawadi Wongkhamchan and won the silver medal. The result gave Japan its first Asian Games medal in teqball, which made its debut at the Games in Aichi-Nagoya.<ref name="OCAfinal">{{cite news
|title=Thailand's Wongkhamchan completes golden double in mixed doubles teqball
|url=https://oca.asia/news/7924-thailands-wongkhamchan-completes-golden-double-in-mixed-doubles-teqball.html
|publisher=[[Olympic Council of Asia]]
|date=20 September 2026
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref> Wase also competed in the men's singles event at the 2026 Asian Games. He progressed from his group to the knockout stage, but did not reach the medal positions.<ref name="FITEQ2026">{{cite web
|title=Men's Singles and Men's Doubles Open Teqball Competition at Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games
|url=https://fiteq-web-prod.azurewebsites.net/news/1060
|publisher=[[International Teqball Federation]]
|access-date=8 October 2026
}}</ref>
